sections.text: perceptionusual attribute: wisdom untrained: yesper­cep­tion is used when the imme­di­ate ques­tion is what the char­ac­ter's senses reveal. it covers move­ment, sound, scent, changes in the sur­round­ings, con­cealed objects, and creatures attempt­ing to remain unnoticed.a char­ac­ter might hear quiet move­ment beyond a door, smell smoke before seeing a flame, catch a distant figure break­ing the skyline, notice a sudden draft, spot an object partly con­cealed beneath fur­niture, or pick out a creature hiding among natural cover. per­cep­tion may operate when some­thing draws atten­tion or when the char­ac­ter delib­er­ately watches, listens, or exam­ines the imme­di­ate scene.light­ing, dis­tance, noise, dis­trac­tion, and con­ceal­ment shape how dif­fi­cult a detail is to notice. con­nect­ing several details or recon­struct­ing the event that pro­duced them uses invest­ig­a­tion.

sections.title: Performance (Field)
sections.text: performance (field)usual attribute: charisma untrained: yesper­form­ance uses a prac­ticed art to enter­tain, impress, move, dis­tract, or com­mu­nic­ate with an audi­ence. each field is a sep­ar­ate skill. a per­former can choose suit­able mater­ial, prepare or rehearse it, adapt the deliv­ery to the setting, sustain an audi­ence's atten­tion, and convey a mood, story, argu­ment, or char­ac­ter through the chosen art.

sections.title: Profession (Field)
sections.text: profession (field)usual attribute: varies untrained: trained onlypro­fes­sion rep­res­ents the broad prac­tical know­ledge and judg­ment of a live­li­hood. each field is learned sep­ar­ately. it covers the occu­pa­tion's routine work, working con­di­tions, cus­tom­ary stand­ards, hazards, records, tools, mater­i­als, and rela­tion­ships with employ­ers, cus­tom­ers, sup­pli­ers, or fellow prac­ti­tion­ers.a pro­fes­sional can plan an ordin­ary workday, estim­ate common needs and delays, recog­nize when con­di­tions are unsafe or unusual, super­vise routine labor, main­tain the records expec­ted of the trade, and under­stand how people in that occu­pa­tion usually solve famil­iar prob­lems. the exact attrib­ute follows the task and the pro­fes­sion.narrow spe­cial­ist work uses its ded­ic­ated skill. a pro­fes­sion (sailor) under­stands watches, duties, cargo routines, and life aboard ship, while seaman­ship con­trols the vessel. pro­fes­sion (steward or sen­eschal) covers the ordin­ary work of a house­hold or estate; the ruler system governs the insti­tu­tion itself.pro­fes­sion (soldier) covers mil­it­ary routine, service customs, camp duties, and the ordin­ary work of sol­dier­ing. weapon use and combat man­euvers follow the char­ac­ter's actual train­ing and the combat rules.land and resources: agri­cul­ture; fisher; for­ester; gardener; hunter; miner; shep­herd; trapper or furrier; wood­cut­ter.trade and trans­port: baker; butcher; driver or team­ster; mer­chant; miller; porter; sailor.ser­vices and insti­tu­tions: bar­ris­ter; clerk; groom or stable­keeper; innkeeper; lib­rar­ian; midwife; scribe; soldier; steward or sen­eschal.

sections.title: Research
sections.text: researchusual attribute: intelligence untrained: limitedresearch finds, com­pares, and assesses inform­a­tion held in books, ledgers, archives, cata­logues, cor­res­pond­ence, maps, and similar organ­ized sources. it follows ref­er­ences, recon­ciles con­flict­ing accounts, recog­nizes gaps in a record, and draws a sup­por­ted answer from mater­ial scattered across several sources.guild ledgers can trace own­er­ship; maps and travel accounts may pre­serve an older name for a ruin; con­flict­ing chron­icles can be com­pared for what they agree upon. cor­res­pond­ence may pre­serve a for­got­ten agree­ment, while a library cata­logue can identify where a needed text is held.a clear answer in a famil­iar source may be found untrained. obscure, extens­ive, con­tra­dict­ory, or poorly organ­ized mater­ial requires train­ing. research estab­lishes what the sur­viv­ing sources contain; rel­ev­ant know­ledge helps the char­ac­ter under­stand spe­cial­ist subject matter found within them.

sections.title: Ride
sections.text: rideusual attribute: dexterity untrained: yesride covers mount­ing, guiding, stop­ping, turning, and keeping one's seat on a riding animal. routine travel on a calm, trained mount usually needs no check.a check may become appro­pri­ate when the mount stumbles or rears, the rider must nego­ti­ate steep or crowded ground, a sudden turn or obstacle threatens the rider's seat, or the animal must be guided through imme­di­ate

sections.title: Ropework
sections.text: ropeworkusual attribute: dexterity untrained: yesrope­work covers choos­ing and tying knots, making lash­ings and hitches, joining lines, secur­ing loads, and judging whether a fasten­ing will hold. it may be used to anchor a climb­ing line, lash cargo to a wagon, fasten a boat, secure a shelter, join two ropes, make an impro­vised loop or harness, or release a knot tightened by strain and weather.the rope, anchor, load, access, and con­di­tions determ­ine how demand­ing the work is. rope­work can assess the fasten­ing being made, but damaged rope or an unsound anchor remains a phys­ical weak­ness.making rope is craft (rope­mak­ing). once it is in hand, rope­work governs its knots and fasten­ings; aboard ship, seaman­ship governs the wider oper­a­tion they support.

sections.title: Seamanship
sections.text: seamanshipusual attribute: dexterity untrained: limitedseaman­ship covers the demand­ing oper­a­tion of boats and ships. it includes hand­ling sails and rigging, steer­ing, coordin­at­ing prac­tical crew work, and keeping a vessel under control as wind, current, water, or damage changes its beha­vior.its ordin­ary uses include setting or redu­cing sail, bring­ing a vessel along­side a pier, steer­ing through dif­fi­cult water, respond­ing to a sudden change in wind, and com­pens­at­ing for damaged rigging or other prob­lems that affect control. basic work under dir­ec­tion may be attemp­ted untrained; oper­at­ing a vessel inde­pend­ently or under haz­ard­ous con­di­tions requires train­ing.nav­ig­a­tion estab­lishes where the vessel should go. seaman­ship handles the vessel that must get there. within the broader pro­fes­sion (sailor), seaman­ship is the spe­cial­ist skill for con­trolling the vessel itself.

sections.title: Sense Motive
sections.text: sense motiveusual attribute: wisdom untrained: yessense motive reads emo­tional state, sin­cer­ity, guarded interests, and likely inten­tion through beha­vior and context. it can reveal unease, eager­ness, con­cealed hos­til­ity, divided loyalty, a rehearsed answer, or signs that someone is trying to steer the con­ver­sa­tion.a mer­chant may appear reluct­ant while showing every sign of wanting the sale com­pleted quickly. an envoy may speak warmly while repeatedly check­ing the exits. a pris­oner may react more strongly to one name than to

sections.title: Sleight of Hand
sections.text: sleight of handusual attribute: dexterity untrained: yessleight of hand uses quick, con­trolled move­ment to palm, conceal, pass, switch, or remove a small object without attract­ing notice. it can slip a coin into a sleeve, exchange one small object for another, pass some­thing between com­pan­ions, hide an item during a search, manip­u­late a game piece, or take advant­age of a brief dis­trac­tion.the object's size and pos­i­tion, the avail­able con­ceal­ment, the observer's atten­tion, and the char­ac­ter's oppor­tun­ity shape the dif­fi­culty. manip­u­lat­ing an unat­ten­ded object beneath a crowded table is easier than remov­ing some­thing worn by an alert person in plain view.

sections.title: Stealth
sections.text: stealthusual attribute: dexterity untrained: yesstealth governs ordin­ary attempts to avoid notice through quiet move­ment, careful pos­i­tion­ing, con­trolled noise, and the use of con­ceal­ment. a char­ac­ter may choose a route that stays behind cover, wait for a guard's atten­tion to turn, cross a noisy surface care­fully, keep equip­ment from strik­ing together, or coordin­ate a group's move­ment through dark­ness or dis­trac­tion.a stealth attempt begins from cir­cum­stances that provide a plaus­ible route or place to remain unnoticed, such as cover, dark­ness, dis­trac­tion, or broken lines of sight. changes in those cir­cum­stances may create a new oppor­tun­ity, expose the char­ac­ter, or alter what con­tin­ued con­ceal­ment requires.the observer's atten­tion and the char­ac­ter's method determ­ine whether the check is unop­posed or opposed under the ordin­ary check rules. moving across noisy ground, passing close to an alert guard, or con­ceal­ing more than one person may change the dif­fi­culty.related talents: hide and sneak. both build on stealth for excep­tional con­ceal­ment and quiet move­ment.

sections.title: Survival
sections.text: survivalusual attribute: wisdom untrained: yessur­vival covers living and trav­el­ling safely beyond settled places. it may be used to find food and water, make a defens­ible or weather­proof camp, protect sup­plies from the ele­ments, judge approach­ing weather, identify natural hazards, and choose a prac­tical line of travel through dif­fi­cult country.sur­vival also sup­ports delib­er­ate exam­in­a­tion of phys­ical tracks when usable signs remain. foot­prints, dis­turbed soil, broken veget­a­tion, dung, ashes, and dis­carded mater­ial may reveal a dir­ec­tion of travel and other con­clu­sions jus­ti­fied by the sur­viv­ing evid­ence. poor ground, weather, age, con­ceal­ment, and inter­rup­ted signs can make the task more dif­fi­cult or limit what can reas­on­ably be learned.nav­ig­a­tion determ­ines pos­i­tion and course. sur­vival keeps people sup­plied and safe while cross­ing the terrain.related talent: track­ing. track­ing builds on sur­vival for rapid recog­ni­tion and pursuit of usable signs.skill mastery: survivalsur­vival skill mastery unlocks trail recon­struc­tion. a char­ac­ter with this mastery can recon­struct the likely route between sep­ar­ated sur­viv­ing signs and reac­quire a trail after its con­tinu­ous trace has been lost, con­cealed, or delib­er­ately broken, provided enough phys­ical evid­ence remains.trail recon­struc­tion takes the time appro­pri­ate to careful exam­in­a­tion. it can bridge gaps jus­ti­fied by sur­viv­ing signs, but it cannot create evid­ence where no usable signs remain.track­ing retains its extraordin­ary speed of recog­ni­tion and pursuit. trail­craft remains a sep­ar­ate scout feature. it grants its listed +4 to par­tic­u­lar sur­vival checks for food, water, shelter, weather, and natural travel hazards; the bonus does not extend to trail recon­struc­tion, fol­low­ing tracks, nav­ig­a­tion, or avoid­ing becom­ing lost.

sections.title: Additional Skills and Fields
sections.text: additional skills and fieldsthe cata­logue presents common recur­ring skills rather than every field that can exist. when a new dis­cip­line becomes import­ant during play, the dm may intro­duce an appro­pri­ate skill or know­ledge field; a char­ac­ter is not pen­al­ized for lacking a skill that had not pre­vi­ously existed as an avail­able choice.

sections.title: Talents and Feats
sections.text: talents and featstalents and feats are exceptional abilities learned beyond ordinary skills. ordinary talents are tied to jobs and their rank-access tables. feats are learned separately from job progression. grandmaster talents are the character-wide exceptional advancement available after the level-31 grand master gate and use their own procedure below.

sections.title: Learning Talents
sections.text: learning talentsa talent is an ability made available by a job's rank-access table or by another explicit grant. reaching a listed rank permits the character to buy the talent; it does not grant every talent at that rank automatically.a talent is learned once. access to the same talent through another job does not grant a second copy, and it does not refund xp already spent. a talent creates numbered tiers or another exception only when its own entry explicitly says so.when a character's jobs offer the same talent at different ranks, use the earliest rank the character has already reached. this determines both access and xp price; the character's main job does not matter.earliest unlocked accessxp costapprentice or journeyman5 xpveteran or expert10 xpmentor, master, or champion15 xptalents available through expert rank may be self-trained when the character has the necessary time and opportunity. talents available at mentor rank or later require a willing instructor who knows the talent or is otherwise established as capable of teaching it. there is no single training time that applies to every talent.individual talent entries may impose additional prerequisites or restrictions. job access and xp payment do not waive them. an exclusive talent is available only through the named job unless another rule explicitly grants access.some starting packages or other rules grant a named talent automatically. an automatic grant costs no xp and does not become an additional copy if the character later finds purchase access through another job.

sections.title: Grandmaster Talents
sections.text: grandmaster talentsgrandmaster talents, abbreviated gm talents, do not use the ordinary job-rank price table. a character becomes eligible after one job reaches level 31 and the dm recognizes the character as a grand master.record every gm talent on one character-wide known list. a new gm talent costs 10 xp for each gm talent the character will know after learning it: 10 xp for the first, 20 xp for the second, 30 xp for the third, and so on. every numbered entry is purchased and counted separately. there is no fixed maximum, shared tier sequence, capacity track, or separate grandmaster level.each entry states gm talent requirement: n, meaning the minimum number of other gm talents the character must already know. it also states its own prerequisites and training or achievement gate. gm talents are permanent and are not ordinarily retrained, exchanged, or refunded.the complete current engine and initial nineteen-entry catalogue belong to the separate gm and beyond expansion. the universal session-xp procedure remains dm-facing and is not repeated here.

sections.title: Reading a Talent Entry
sections.text: reading a talent entryevery talent entry begins with a classification label:talent identifies a talent whether it is purchased or granted automatically.mastery appears beside talent only when the ability is an explicit member of a class mastery. it does not mean master rank or skill mastery.job feature identifies an automatic job feature included here for discovery. it is not a purchasable talent merely because it appears in this chapter.an entry then gives the jobs that provide access, its xp price or automatic-grant status, any additional prerequisites, and its effect.job-defining abilities are reproduced here from classes. bard entries give each ability's own rules and link to the shared performance rules in classes. teaching examples remain in classes.

sections.title: Alertness
sections.text: alertnesstalentaccess: barbarian xp: 10 xpalertness gives the barbarian a supernatural awareness of danger. the barbarian cannot be surprised or made flat-footed unless the attacker is a rogue whose rogue job level is at least 5 higher than the barbarian's job level, or a scout whose scout job level is at least 5 higher and who uses ambush.when a concealed, potentially dangerous supernatural presence or effect is within 60 feet, the dm secretly makes a wisdom check for the barbarian. success reveals that something is wrong, but not its identity, nature, or location.invisible creatures, unseen magical forces, unnatural conditions, curses, hauntings, and magical traps may trigger this sense. ordinary mundane traps and harmless or beneficial magic do not. the dm determines when the hidden check is made.

sections.title: Ambush
sections.text: ambushtalent · masteryaccess: scout xp: 15 xpranged mastery, rapid fire, and ambush form one package. they may work together when their individual requirements are met. selecting another job's class mastery suppresses every scout-mastery benefit for that round. if ranged mastery or ambush first becomes relevant through an opening attack, lock or choose scout mastery immediately before that attack roll. ambush can therefore select scout mastery during round 0. rapid fire cannot operate during round 0 because it requires a full attack.ambush. ambush is a purchased master talent that may be used only on the scout's first attack attempt of a combat. before rolling, the scout may declare it for a ranged attack against a target within 60 feet that cannot perceive or anticipate the scout. add the scout job level to that attack roll. the bonus applies only to that attack and can increase damage only through positive attack margin. it does not apply to a rapid fire attack or another projectile. the opportunity is expended whether the attack hits or misses.scout camouflage can help establish ambush but is not required when the scout is otherwise genuinely unperceived and unanticipated. ambush may initiate combat during round 0 because it is a scout job mastery. the round 0 attack cannot receive the adventurer chassis's once-per-battle damage addition. an otherwise qualifying ambush in round 1 or later may receive that separate addition on its resulting damage roll.

sections.title: Arcane Ward
sections.text: arcane wardtalentaccess: sorcerer xp: 15 xpusing arcane ward takes a main action. the sorcerer creates a visible, stationary arcane glyph filling the sorcerer's current space and hovering just above the supporting surface. it lasts for 1 minute.only the sorcerer who created the ward receives its benefits, and only while standing within it. leaving suspends those benefits; returning before it ends restores them. the glyph does not move with the sorcerer.spells cast from within the ward gain +2 to their spell dc and cost 2 less me, to a minimum cost of 1 me. the sorcerer need not commit concentration to begin one of these spells, but must still occupy and resolve any concentration required to maintain it. damage cannot interrupt a spell the sorcerer is casting from within the ward. the ward does not prevent attacks of opportunity, damage, grappling, forced movement, or any other consequence. the sorcerer may create another arcane ward 1 hour after the previous ward ends.

sections.title: Aura of Negation
sections.text: aura of negationtalentaccess: barbarian xp: 15 xpafter connecting with a melee attack, the barbarian may spend 2 pe and activate aura of negation as part of that hit. resolve the attack's ordinary damage normally. the barbarian may instead use the main action to touch a willing adjacent creature.record the barbarian's total magic resistance, including trained and equipment magic resistance, then roll percentile dice against it. whether the roll succeeds or fails, the barbarian's magic resistance becomes 0 for 1 minute and then returns normally.on success, every ongoing beneficial or harmful magical effect on the touched creature is dispelled without a separate dispel check. enchanted equipment, permanent item properties, inherent abilities, and effects explicitly impossible to dispel are unaffected.

sections.title: B Augmented Sixth
sections.text: b augmented sixthtalent · masteryaccess: bard xp: 10 xpeach direct note deals a number of d6 of magical sonic damage equal to half the bard job level, rounded down, with a minimum of 1d6. complete the nominal dice expression, roll no more than four damage dice, and replace each excess die with +2. bard level 30 therefore produces 4d6 + 22, not 15 rolled dice. converted +2 values remain part of the damage-dice subtotal for critical multiplication if an explicit later rule ever permits a critical; the direct notes themselves make no attack roll and cannot critically hit.magic resistance applies. magic protection and worn physical armor's flat dr reduce the damage. direct notes use no penetration / armor grade comparison, attack margin, or critical hit.spend 4 pe and use a main action. every other creature within 120 feet, including allies and enemies but excluding the bard, takes the damage; a successful fortitude save halves it. it does not affect objects unless an explicit rule says otherwise.see classes — bard: shared performance rules.

sections.title: Backstab
sections.text: backstabtalent · masteryaccess: rogue xp: 5 xpsneak attack, backstab, hamstring, and dual backstab form one package. they may work together when their individual requirements are met. selecting another job's class mastery suppresses every rogue-mastery benefit for that round. finesse, quick draw, casing, underworld courtesy, skirmish, envenom, and other non-mastery features or talents remain available under their own rules.if sneak attack or backstab first becomes relevant through an opening attack, lock or choose rogue mastery immediately before that attack roll. rogue mastery may therefore be selected during round 0 when one of its abilities is otherwise legal.sneak attack and backstab each grant the same +1 pen increase. these increases do not stack: an attack qualifying for both gains +1 pen total, not +2.backstab. backstab is a purchased apprentice talent that modifies a melee attack made with a short, one-handed piercing weapon, normally a dagger, short sword, rapier, rondel dagger, tanto, or comparable weapon. the target must be genuinely unaware that they are in danger; merely being flat-footed is insufficient.on a successful backstab, add the rogue job level as fixed raw damage before damage reduction. this fixed damage is not multiplied by a critical hit or another dice multiplier. a qualifying backstab gains +1 pen, which does not stack with sneak attack's pen increase. backstab costs no pe, may operate during round 0, and is not automatically lethal damage. it may combine with sneak attack when that attack independently satisfies sneak attack's requirements.

sections.title: Bash
sections.text: bashtalentaccess: mercenary; barbarian xp: 5 xponce per round, the character may spend 2 pe and replace one attack with bash. the attacker makes a roll-under strength check with bab against the defender's choice of a roll-under strength or dexterity check with bab.on success, the defender becomes prone. success by 8 or more also permits the attacker to begin a grapple immediately without another attack or pe cost. the attacker drops held objects, follows the defender down, and continues with the grapple procedure. failure by 8 or more makes the attacker prone.both participants must have their feet on the ground. a one-category creature-size difference grants +4 to the larger participant. bash cannot be used across a difference of two or more size categories. a trained bash failure does not provoke an attack of opportunity.see combat — hard trip and bash for the shared maneuver rules and untrained attempts.

sections.title: Berserk
sections.text: berserkjob feature · masterygrant: barbarian xp: noneberserk and fury are mutually exclusive states in one class-mastery package. activating or maintaining either state selects class mastery: barbarian for the round. if another class mastery has already been selected for the round, neither state can be activated during that round. an active berserk or fury must continue selecting barbarian mastery in later rounds. choosing another job's mastery while a state is active ends it immediately and invokes its catch-breath consequence. neither state automatically applies the separate frenzied condition.

sections.title: Blind Fighting
sections.text: blind fightingtalentaccess: barbarian xp: 10 xpblind fighting provides combat awareness of creatures and dangers within 10 feet. within that range, the character makes otherwise legal rolled active defenses at -2 and attacks at -2. blindness alone does not make the character surprised or flat-footed against a threat perceived through blind fighting.the 50% miss chance caused by blindness or an unseen target does not apply within that 10-foot awareness. blind fighting does not remove an unrelated miss chance. outside 10 feet, use the ordinary blinded procedure unless another sense or ability provides awareness.

sections.title: Blitzkrieg
sections.text: blitzkriegtalentaccess: mercenary xp: 15 xpdeveloped by the taslamaran military to break shield walls and punish exposed actions, blitzkrieg is an immediate interrupt costing 3 pe. it may be used once per round.when a perceived enemy within 30 feet begins a main action, attack, item use, spell, or blitzkrieg, the mercenary may respond before that action resolves. the mercenary moves up to 15 feet without provoking attacks of opportunity and must end within melee reach of that enemy. a qualifying quick draw permission may draw an accessible weapon during this response. an action the mercenary cannot perceive or recognize cannot trigger blitzkrieg.the mercenary then makes one melee attack. if it hits and leaves at least 1 damage after protection, the target makes a fortitude save against dc 10 + damage taken. failure loses the triggering action. success allows it to continue if it remains possible. the hit retains every other normal consequence, including the ordinary rules for interrupting a spell in progress.blitzkrieg may interrupt another blitzkrieg. resolve the most recently declared blitzkrieg first, then work backward through the interrupted sequence while each remaining action is still possible. ordinary movement, free actions, and reactions other than blitzkrieg do not trigger this talent.

sections.title: Brawling
sections.text: brawlingtalentaccess: mercenary; swashbuckler; barbarian; scout; rogue; bard; shaman; paladin; hellion xp: 10 xp  prerequisite: self defensebrawling allows the character to make an unarmed full attack and adds +0.5 attack speed to its primary unarmed attack. second attack and third attack do not contribute.both hands must be empty or equipped only with qualifying fist weapons. these include knuckles, claws, katars, punch knives, and comparable weapons designed to function as extensions of unarmed combat. armed and unarmed attacks cannot be mixed in a full attack receiving brawling's benefit.when brawling bare-handed, each attack deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage with pen 0. when using a qualifying fist weapon, use that weapon's printed damage profile.a brawling full attack pays the ordinary full-attack pe cost and no additional brawling cost. a defender attempting to parry a brawling attack takes -8 parry unless the defender possesses enhanced parry, in which case the penalty is -4.brawling does not remove self defense's -4 penalty when the brawler uses a bare hand to parry an armed attack.

sections.title: Brew
sections.text: brewtalentaccess: priest; shaman; sorcerer; warlock; necromancer xp: 10 xp through priest, sorcerer, warlock, or necromancer; 15 xp through shamanbrew allows the character to place eligible spells into prepared potion vials. a spell can be brewed only when its spell entry explicitly marks it brewable. the absence of that marker means that the spell cannot be brewed.a potion affects the creature that drinks it. choices that the spell would normally require are fixed during brewing unless the spell says otherwise. anyone may drink a completed potion, and doing so costs no personal magical energy.brewing uses the shared brew and scribe construction procedure below.brew and scribe constructionbrew and scribe are separate talents, but their construction follows the same procedure. brew uses wisdom and produces potions. scribe uses intelligence and produces scrolls.the crafter must know and currently be able to cast every spell placed in the item. neither talent can store a bard performance, talent, spell-like ability, ritual spell, or true necromancy.construction requires eight hours of focused work for each stored spell. the crafter invests each spell's normal magical energy cost during that work. after completing all of the work, make one construction check: a wisdom check for brew or an intelligence check for scribe. apply every penalty from the item and its stored spells, then roll d20. a result equal to or below the adjusted attribute succeeds.failure destroys the prepared blank and loses the work and magical energy invested in it.

sections.title: Prepared Blanks
sections.text: prepared blanksevery prepared vial or scroll blank has two independent ratings: capacity and potency. the artisan making the blank determines both. the brewer or scriber chooses an available blank rather than freely declaring its potency.when a spell is available through more than one job, the crafter chooses which job is being used to make the item. use that job's spell circle, magical energy cost, casting attribute, art, and caster level. an explicit non-job casting route supplies the same values.the stored caster level cannot be lower than the minimum caster level at which the chosen route grants the spell circle or higher than the crafter's current caster level through that route. for a job using the standard nine-circle progression, the minimums for circles 1 through 9 are caster levels 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, and 15.capacity is the caster-level load the blank can safely hold. each spell must fit individually: its stored caster level cannot exceed the blank's capacity. add the stored caster levels together to find the item's total load. when several spells share one blank, each point of total load above capacity imposes -1 on the construction check.standard blanks have a whole-number capacity from 1 through 15. a blank has a base typical value of 5 silver pieces (sp) for each point of capacity, then applies its potency multiplier. typical value is an expected value under ordinary conditions rather than a guaranteed shop price. capacity 13 through 15 blanks are normally restricted and must be commissioned. capacity above 15 exists only as an exceptional item with the dm's permission.craft (glassworking) is used to make potion vials. craft (calligraphy and illumination) or craft (bookbinding) is used to make scroll blanks. a suitable craft mastery is required to create a strong or overpowered blank. a trained craftsperson may create weak and normal blanks.potencyconstruction checkeffect on each stored spellblank valueweakno penaltyhalve caster-level effects, rounding down to a minimum of 1; halve duration; -5 spell dchalf base valuenormalno adjustmentno adjustmentbase valuestrong-2+2 effective caster levels; increase duration by half; +2 spell dcthree times base valueoverpowered-4+4 effective caster levels; double duration; +4 spell dcten times base valuethe spell-dc adjustment in this table is the complete potency adjustment. do not add a second dc change for the effective caster-level increase. capacity is compared with the chosen caster-level load before potency is applied. apply potency's caster-level change before calculating a caster-level-based duration, then apply the separate duration change in the table. whenever potency changes a duration, round down and retain a minimum of one applicable time unit.

sections.title: Construction Check
sections.text: construction checkapply all of these penalties to the wisdom or intelligence check:take the highest spell circle stored in the item and apply -1 for each circle above first. apply this penalty once, even when the item contains several spells.when the item contains several spells, apply -1 for each point by which their total stored caster-level load exceeds its capacity.apply the potency penalty shown in the table.apply -4 for each stored spell after the first.

sections.title: Using the Finished Item
sections.text: using the finished itemusing a finished potion or scroll costs no personal magical energy. each spell in a scroll is activated and consumed separately as a main action. activating a scroll requires the scrolls talent or another explicit permission. drinking a potion releases all of its stored spells together.an instant effect remains instant. a spell with its own fixed duration keeps that duration unless its entry or the item says otherwise. a spell normally maintained by concentration instead lasts 1 minute for each effective caster level. apply potency to this duration, rounding down to a minimum of 1 minute.example: an elven compound potionfor this example, treat cure critical as a fourth-circle spell and sanctuary as a second-circle spell. an elven brewer places two cure critical effects at caster level 6 and one sanctuary effect at caster level 3 into the same potion. the total load is 15, so a capacity 15 vial holds the spells without a capacity penalty.the highest spell circle imposes -3. the second and third stored spells impose another -8. with wisdom 18, the brewer therefore succeeds on 7 or less using a normal vial, 5 or less using a strong vial, or 3 or less using an overpowered vial.before adding the completed magic, the capacity 15 vial has a typical value of 75 sp at normal potency, 225 sp at strong potency, or 750 sp at overpowered potency.

sections.title: Butcher
sections.text: butchertalentaccess: scout; barbarian xp: 5 xp through scout; 10 xp through barbarianwith suitable cutting tools and a carcass containing usable flesh, make an intelligence check. success dresses the carcass into good-quality cuts ready to cook or cure. the dm determines how much can be recovered from the creature's size, anatomy, condition, and remaining usable flesh.ordinary survival or a suitable profession may be enough for familiar animals under good conditions. butcher allows reliable field dressing and the processing of unusual prey when those ordinary approaches would be more difficult or insufficient.

sections.title: C Major
sections.text: c majortalent · masteryaccess: bard xp: 5 xpeach direct note deals a number of d6 of magical sonic damage equal to half the bard job level, rounded down, with a minimum of 1d6. complete the nominal dice

sections.title: Clarity
sections.text: claritytalentaccess: priest; sorcerer; warlock; necromancer xp: 15 xponce after each long rest, and no more than once per 24 hours, the character may declare clarity when beginning an actual spell whose casting starts with a main action and uses a numeric spell speed.after every other cost adjustment, that spell's magical energy cost becomes 0. this takes precedence over arcane ward's minimum cost of 1 magical energy.clarity cannot be used with a magical device, bard performance, talent, spell-like ability, ritual spell, true necromancy, or a spell whose casting requires rounds,

sections.title: Climb
sections.text: climbtalentaccess: rogue; barbarian xp: 10 xpwhen a route is physically climbable, the character automatically succeeds on climbing checks rated hard or easier.the character ignores ordinary mountain-terrain travel penalties to speed and does not make constitution checks for exhaustion caused solely by climbing. very hard and extreme climbs still require the appropriate check. severe weather, altitude, magical hazards, and other exceptional dangers retain their ordinary effects.

sections.title: Combat Casting
sections.text: combat castingtalentaccess: paladin; hellion xp: 10 xpcombat casting costs 4 pe in addition to the spell's magical energy cost. it creates a special casting sequence rather than a full attack, so the ordinary full-attack pe cost is not added.any movement must occur first. choose one qualifying one-handed melee weapon and begin the spell during that weapon's first initiative pass while already within melee reach. every remaining pass supplied by that weapon during the round may be used for one melee

sections.title: Countersong
sections.text: countersongtalent · masteryaccess: bard xp: 5 xpcost: 2 me to start; 1 me per minute to maintain.choose one hostile song within 60 feet that the bard can hear. make an opposed d20 + bard job level + charisma modifier roll against its performer. countersong must win; a tie preserves the existing song. on a win, that song is suppressed while both performances continue and remain in range. on failure, the bard may restart countersong on a later turn by paying its starting cost again.countersong occupies the bard's one maintained-song allowance. starting another song ends countersong, and starting countersong ends another song the bard was maintaining.while countersong is active, or when the bard has specifically readied it against sonic damage, reduce each sonic-damage result within 60 feet by a number of d6 equal to half the bard job level, rounded down, with a minimum of 1d6. damage cannot be reduced below 0.

sections.title: Counterstrike
sections.text: counterstriketalentaccess: barbarian xp: 15 xp  prerequisite: alertnessthe first attack that hits the barbarian during round 0, or before the barbarian has taken any offensive action in the battle, may trigger counterstrike if its source is within the barbarian's melee reach. the barbarian must have attempted an active defense against that attack; using the default static defense does not permit counterstrike.calculate the triggering attack's damage through margin of success and every applicable damage addition, but record it before applying the barbarian's damage reduction or other mitigation. the triggering attack still resolves against the barbarian normally.the barbarian then makes a melee attack against its source with a +5 bonus, using a held weapon or an unarmed attack. this response costs no pe and deals no weapon or unarmed damage of its own. it may be dodged but cannot be parried or blocked.on a hit, the source receives twice the recorded damage. the source's own damage reduction and other protection apply normally. sanctuary, presence, spirit aura, and comparable effects that would ordinarily prohibit attacking the source do not prevent counterstrike.the first qualifying attack is the only counterstrike opportunity in that battle. declining it or missing the +5 attack provides no later attempt.

sections.title: Cross-Slash
sections.text: cross-slashtalentaccess: swashbuckler xp: 15 xpcross-slash costs 2 pe and follows the ordinary charge procedure. the swashbuckler moves along a straight, clear route and then attacks the charged target once with each of two melee weapons, one held in each hand.both attacks receive the charge's attack bonus. the swashbuckler takes its defense penalty, and the movement provokes attacks of opportunity normally.

sections.title: Dance
sections.text: dancetalent · masteryaccess: bard xp: 5 xpactivating dance uses movement and costs 2 pe. it lasts for a number of complete rounds equal to the bard's charisma modifier, with a minimum of one round. before it expires, the bard may renew it by spending movement and 2 pe again.dance is a sequence of strange, broken-rhythm movements that makes the bard difficult to read; it is neither ordinary social dancing nor required travel across the battlefield. the bard gains a +4 dodge-type bonus to dodge and +4 bluff. the dodge-type bonus does not stack with featherfoot or another dodge-type bonus; use the greatest applicable bonus. enhanced dodge expressly adds its +1.its dodge benefit is visual, mind-affecting misdirection. it provides no dodge bonus against a mindless attacker, an attacker immune to mind-affecting effects, or an attacker unable to perceive the movement. immobilization or an incompatible physical action ends dance.the bard may fold unusual movement into the sequence. if compatibility is genuinely uncertain, the dm may call for a performance check. dance itself permits that specific check without requiring a separately learned performance field and grants +4 on it. the bonus applies only to incorporating the uncertain action into dance; it does not improve another performance field, a song or direct-note dc, or another bard ability. dance may coexist with one song and activates that song's printed dance effect.see classes — bard: shared performance rules.

sections.title: Detect Evil
sections.text: detect eviljob featuregrant: paladin xp: nonedetect evil. while conscious, the paladin passively senses exceptional or supernatural evil. the sense reveals presence and approximate strength rather than

sections.title: Dirt Kick
sections.text: dirt kicktalentaccess: mercenary; swashbuckler; barbarian; bard xp: 5 xpdirt kick replaces one attack during a full attack or uses the character's main action. it costs 2 pe and targets one creature within melee reach. the target must have reachable eyes, and suitable dirt, sand, ash, or similar loose material must be available.the target makes a reflex save against the character's ordinary talent dc. on failure, the target is blinded for 1d4 rounds. the target may spend its main action clearing its eyes and ending the condition early.eye protection may grant a situational bonus on the save or make dirt kick impossible, as the dm determines. a creature without eyes or whose eyes cannot be reached is not a legal target. see combat — blinded and deafened for the condition's effects.

sections.title: Disarm
sections.text: disarmtalentaccess: mercenary; swashbuckler; barbarian; bard; paladin; hellion xp: 5 xp through paladin or hellion; 10 xp through mercenary, swashbuckler, barbarian, or bardonce per round, the character may spend 1 pe and replace one attack with disarm.against a defender who lacks disarm, make an unopposed roll-under dexterity check without adding bab. against a defender who possesses disarm, the attacker and defender make opposed roll-under dexterity checks and add bab. on success, the defender drops the targeted weapon in their own space.the holder of the heavier weapon gains +2. wielding a weapon in two hands against a weapon not wielded in two hands grants another +4; these bonuses stack. a one-category creature-size difference grants +4 to the larger participant. disarm cannot be used across a difference of two or more size categories.apply a situational advantage to one participant's threshold. when the check is unopposed, a defender's advantage becomes an equal penalty to the attacker's threshold. magic, unusual equipment, locked gauntlets,

sections.title: Disguise
sections.text: disguisetalentaccess: rogue; scout; bard xp: 5 xp through rogue; 10 xp through scout or bardpreparing a disguise requires a disguise kit and 10 minutes. the disguise may alter apparent age, facial features, build, coloring, and similar visible details. it may also present the character as a similar race when the difference can be achieved through plausible physical disguise, such as false ears used to appear elven.disguise cannot substantially change the character's size, body plan, or number of limbs. a stocky human might pass for a dwarf with the right materials; a slight human cannot acquire dwarven proportions through disguise alone.casual observers accept a plausible disguise unless something gives them reason to investigate. deliberate scrutiny uses the disguised character's bluff against the observer's perception. familiarity, behavior, clothing, location, the assumed role, and the quality of the supporting materials affect the attempt normally.disguise is nonmagical and does not register as magic merely because it is unusually convincing.

sections.title: Divine Intervention
sections.text: divine interventionjob featuregrant: priest, paladin, or hellion xp: nonedivine intervention. a priest, paladin, or hellion with this feature may once during their lifetime petition their god concerning a matter of paramount importance to that god's doctrine when ordinary avenues are exhausted. there is no fixed roll, action, magnitude, or promised form; the god determines the answer and any demand or lasting consequence. making the petition consumes the one lifetime opportunity even when the answer is smaller, stranger, or more dangerous than requested. divine intervention is neither a spell nor a class mastery.

sections.title: Dual Backstab
sections.text: dual backstabtalent · masteryaccess: rogue xp: 10 xpsneak attack, backstab, hamstring, and dual backstab form one package. they may work together when their individual requirements are met. selecting another job's class mastery suppresses every rogue-mastery benefit for that round. finesse, quick draw, casing, underworld courtesy, skirmish, envenom, and other non-mastery features or talents remain available under their own rules.if sneak attack or backstab first becomes relevant through an opening attack, lock or choose rogue mastery immediately before that attack roll. rogue mastery may therefore be selected during round 0 when one of its abilities is otherwise legal.sneak attack and backstab each grant the same +1 pen increase. these increases do not stack: an attack qualifying for both gains +1 pen total, not +2.dual backstab. dual backstab is a purchased expert talent. once per round, after a successful backstab leaves its victim alive, the rogue may immediately make one additional attack against that victim with an eligible backstab weapon. this attack spends no pe and consumes no scheduled attack, attack pass, main action, or movement.for this immediate attack, the victim may make an ordinary active dodge even if the opening strike's surprise or flat-footed state would otherwise prevent it, but cannot parry or block. the second strike receives backstab's fixed damage and +1 pen despite the victim's new awareness. the opening strike's surprise or flat-footed state alone does not make this second strike a sneak attack; sneak attack applies only when another qualifying trigger still applies, such as flanking. dual backstab cannot trigger itself and may follow a round 0 backstab.

sections.title: Dual Wield
sections.text: dual wieldtalentaccess: swashbuckler xp: 5 xpdual wield applies while the character wields two one-handed weapons. choose one as the primary attack and the other as the offhand weapon. each may be light or medium.a light offhand removes the ordinary two-weapon attack and parry penalties.

sections.title: Endurance
sections.text: endurancetalentaccess: mercenary; swashbuckler; barbarian; scout; rogue; bard; priest; shaman; paladin; hellion; warlock xp: 5 xp through mercenary or barbarian; 10 xp through swashbuckler, rogue, bard, shaman, paladin, hellion, or warlock; 15 xp through priest; no xp for the scout's automatic grantendurance improves the character's level-based physical energy progression:a warrior with endurance gains 1 pe at every qualifying job level except multiples of three.a non-warrior with endurance gains 1 pe at every qualifying odd job level.a scout uses the warrior endurance schedule until pathfinding replaces it with the scout's every-level progression.only job levels that establish a new overall level contribute level-based pe. secondary catch-up levels do not grant another progression. when endurance is learned later, immediately add the positive difference between the no-endurance progression and the applicable endurance progression across the qualifying levels that contributed to the character's overall level.endurance increases the character's one shared pe pool. it does not multiply purchased pe trains or create a separate pool.

sections.title: Enhanced Damage
sections.text: enhanced damagetalentaccess: mercenary; swashbuckler; barbarian; rogue; bard; paladin; hellion xp: 5 xp through mercenary, barbarian, paladin, or hellion; 10 xp through swashbuckler, rogue, or bardon each weapon-damage roll, the character may reroll either one weapon-damage die or the entire weapon-dice pool once and must keep the new result. attack margin, strength, and other fixed modifiers are not rerolled.enhanced damage applies only to weapon damage, never to spells or another non-weapon damage source. it requires no pe, may apply to every eligible weapon attack, and remains available while the character uses a class mastery.

sections.title: Envenom
sections.text: envenomtalentaccess: rogue; exclusive xp: 15 xpenvenom teaches the rogue which ingredients can produce useful venoms, where those ingredients might be found or purchased, how to compound them, and how to apply the finished poison. it requires no separate herbalism or alchemy skill.the rogue and dm establish which ingredients are reasonably available and their cost. gathering or procuring them may take additional time according to the location and circumstances.preparing a batch requires one day and an intelligence check. success creates ten doses of one selected poison. a failed batch is unusable. prepared doses remain effective for one week.applying one dose to a melee weapon is a main action. pain poison, blinding poison, and another non-deadly poison remain on the weapon until its next successful damaging hit, then the coating is expended. a missed attack does not expend the coating.deadly poison is the exception. its coating remains active on the melee weapon for one minute and adds its damage to every successful damaging hit made with that weapon during that time.one dose may instead coat a number of pieces of slashing or piercing ammunition equal to the rogue's intelligence modifier, to a minimum of one. each piece carries the poison for one successful damaging hit. a weapon or piece of ammunition cannot carry more than one envenom poison at a time;

sections.title: Exploit Weakness
sections.text: exploit weaknesstalent · masteryaccess: hellion; exclusive xp: 10 xpexploit weakness and hellion cleave form one package and may combine when their requirements are met. neither ability grants the other, and neither places the separately catalogued sweeping slash feats inside hellion mastery. neither may be used during a round already locked to a different class mastery.exploit weakness. exploit weakness is an exclusive veteran talent. immediately before the hellion's first qualifying melee attack of a round, lock or choose class mastery: hellion if the round's mastery has not already been selected.the target must currently suffer an ongoing detrimental condition or penalty imposed by the hellion or one of the hellion's allies. intimidated, poisoned, weakened, blinded, and being overcome by presence are examples. an advantageous circumstance does not qualify merely because it makes the target easier to attack; the detriment must have been imposed. add half the hellion job level, rounded down, to every qualifying melee attack against such a target during that round. the bonus adds no fixed damage,

sections.title: F Minor
sections.text: f minortalent · masteryaccess: bard xp: 5 xpeach direct note deals a number of d6 of magical sonic damage equal to half the bard job level, rounded down, with a minimum of 1d6. complete the nominal dice expression, roll no more than four damage dice, and replace each excess die with +2. bard level 30 therefore produces 4d6 + 22, not 15 rolled dice. converted +2 values remain part of the damage-dice subtotal for critical multiplication if an explicit later rule ever permits a critical; the direct notes themselves make no attack roll and cannot critically hit.magic resistance applies. magic protection and worn physical armor's flat dr reduce the damage. direct notes use no penetration / armor grade comparison, attack margin, or critical hit.spend 1 pe and use a main action to affect one creature within melee reach. no attack roll or save is made.see classes — bard: shared performance rules.

sections.title: Fast Healing
sections.text: fast healingtalentaccess: mercenary; swashbuckler; barbarian; bard; paladin; hellion xp: 5 xp through mercenary, swashbuckler, or barbarian; 10 xp through bard, paladin, or hellionafter resting uninterrupted for 10 minutes, the character automatically restores hp equal to half the highest job level among the character's jobs that currently grant access to fast healing, rounded down, plus the constitution modifier. fast healing always restores at least 1 hp.the character cannot use fast healing again for one hour. it cannot restore hp above the character's maximum.

sections.title: Featherfoot
sections.text: featherfoottalentaccess: swashbuckler; rogue xp: 15 xpat the start of the character's turn, the character may spend 2 pe as a free action to gain a +4 dodge-type bonus to dodge until the start of the next turn.

sections.title: Finesse
sections.text: finessetalentaccess: swashbuckler; rogue xp: 10 xp when purchased through swashbuckler; no xp for the rogue's automatic grantwhen using a light or medium melee weapon, the character may use the dexterity modifier instead of the strength modifier for attack, weapon damage, and parry. dexterity replaces strength in each calculation; the two modifiers are not added together.finesse remains available while the character uses a class mastery. it does not grant or alter quick draw.

sections.title: Fletch
sections.text: fletchtalentaccess: scout xp: 5 xpfletch allows a scout to salvage, select, and shape suitable materials into arrows and crossbow ammunition. the scout may gather those materials in the wild, recover them from other objects, or purchase what is needed.with suitable tools and materials, eight hours of work produces forty pieces of ordinary ammunition. the

sections.title: Fury
sections.text: furytalent · masteryaccess: barbarian xp: 15 xpberserk and fury are mutually exclusive states in one class-mastery package. activating or maintaining either state selects class mastery: barbarian for the round. if another class mastery has already been selected for the round, neither state can be activated during that round. an active berserk or fury must continue selecting barbarian mastery in later rounds. choosing another job's mastery while a state is active ends it immediately and invokes its catch-breath consequence. neither state automatically applies the separate frenzied condition.using berserk or fury. activating either state uses movement and costs 2 pe. every effect other than fury's attack-speed increase begins immediately. the state remains active through the activation round and for one plus the barbarian's constitution modifier complete rounds afterward, with a minimum of one complete round. after that free duration expires, spend 1 pe at the start of each subsequent round, before that round's attack schedule is established, to continue the state through that round. continuation does not refill temporary hp. neither state can be activated while berserk or fury is already active.

sections.title: Greased Lightning
sections.text: greased lightningtalent · masteryaccess: swashbuckler; exclusive xp: 15 xpgreased lightning is an exclusive mentor talent. it costs no pe and begins as part of a melee attack against

sections.title: Haggle
sections.text: haggletalentaccess: mercenary; swashbuckler; scout; rogue; bard; hellion xp: 5 xp through swashbuckler or rogue; 10 xp through mercenary, scout, or hellion; 15 xp through bardwhen negotiating a purchase or sale, the character may make a charisma check. success shifts the price 5% in the character's favor, plus another 5% for every four points of check margin.if the other negotiator also has haggle, make opposed charisma checks. the higher check margin wins and shifts the price in that negotiator's favor by 5%, plus another 5% for every four points by which the winning check margin exceeds the losing margin. a tie leaves the price unchanged.commerce or diplomacy may supply useful knowledge or favorable circumstances, but neither skill replaces haggle or is required to use it.

sections.title: Hamstring
sections.text: hamstringtalent · masteryaccess: rogue; exclusive xp: 10 xphamstring is a special extension of sneak attack and belongs to class mastery: rogue. when making a qualifying sneak attack, the rogue may spend 2 pe and declare hamstring before resolving the attack.resolve the attack and protection normally, but the damage remaining after protection cannot exceed 5. if at least 1 damage remains, the target makes a fortitude save against the rogue's dexterity-based job dc. a creature larger than the rogue gains +8 on this save.

sections.title: Hard Trip
sections.text: hard triptalentaccess: mercenary; swashbuckler; rogue; bard xp: 5 xponce per round, the character may spend 2 pe and replace one attack with hard trip. the attacker and defender each choose strength or dexterity, then make opposed roll-under checks with bab.on success, the defender becomes prone. failure by 8 or more makes the attacker prone. both participants must have their feet on the ground.a one-category creature-size difference grants +4 to the larger participant. hard trip cannot be used across a difference of two or more size categories. a trained hard trip failure does not provoke an attack of opportunity.see combat — hard trip and bash for the shared maneuver rules and untrained attempts.

sections.title: Heckle
sections.text: heckletalentaccess: swashbuckler xp: 5 xpthe swashbuckler may spend 2 pe and replace one attack within a full attack with heckle, or use heckle as a main action. choose one creature within 30 feet that can see, hear, understand, and be emotionally provoked by the swashbuckler.the target makes a will save against the swashbuckler's charisma-based job dc. on failure, it takes -1 attack and defense for each point of the swashbuckler's charisma modifier, with a minimum penalty of -1. the effect lasts one round per point of that modifier, with a minimum of one round.the swashbuckler can have only one creature affected by heckle at a time. heckling another target immediately ends the previous effect. a creature incapable of emotional provocation is unaffected.

sections.title: Hedgehog Stance
sections.text: hedgehog stancetalentaccess: swashbuckler xp: 15 xpat the very start of the swashbuckler's turn, before taking any other action, the swashbuckler may enter hedgehog stance as a free action. the stance lasts until the start of the swashbuckler's next turn and costs no pe.entering hedgehog stance commits the swashbuckler's entire turn. after activating it, the swashbuckler takes no further voluntary action that turn; the parry responses described below remain available while the stance lasts.

sections.title: Hellion Cleave
sections.text: hellion cleavetalent · masteryaccess: hellion; exclusive xp: 15 xpexploit weakness and hellion cleave form one package and may combine when their requirements are met. neither ability grants the other, and neither places the separately catalogued sweeping slash feats inside hellion mastery. neither may be used during a round already locked to a different class mastery.hellion cleave. hellion cleave is an exclusive mentor talent. once per battle, the hellion may declare it for the first attack the hellion makes in that battle. that opening attack must be melee and use a slashing weapon physically capable of severing the target. declaring it selects class mastery: hellion if no mastery is already locked.on a hit, add the hellion job level as fixed raw damage before protection. this addition is not a damage die and is not multiplied by a critical hit. it may combine with exploit weakness when the target qualifies. a target currently overcome by presence uses static defense 10 against hellion cleave.if this attack causes an unprevented mortal wound, the dm may make it a severing injury when the weapon, anatomy, and circumstances make that plausible. preventing the mortal wound prevents the severing result.

sections.title: Herbalism
sections.text: herbalismtalentaccess: scout xp: 5 xpthe scout can gather useful wild herbs whose preparations heal injuries, restore energy or produce magical effects.finding herbsspend eight hours searching suitable wilderness and make a wisdom attribute check. on success, find one dose, plus one additional dose for every four full points of check margin.roll separately for each dose on the searched biome's herb table. the die depends on your scout job rank. higher ranks unlock additional herbs while keeping the common results available. you may find the same herb more than once.scout rankscout job levelssearch diejourneyman5–81d4veteran9–121d6expert13–161d8mentor17–201d10master or higher21+1d12using herbseach dose retains its potency for one year after harvest. consuming it takes one main action, costs no me and requires no spellcasting or concentration.anyone able to consume a dose can use it. each herb has fixed effects, durations and saving throws, regardless of who gathered or consumed it.some herbs carry drawbacks. resolve the benefit first, followed by the drawback and its listed saving throw. secondary drawbacks normally allow a fortitude save; harmful herbs may use a different save. applicable magic resistance still applies. poison immunity prevents effects identified as poison, but does not prevent other magical drawbacks or a spell's mandatory aftermath.combining preparationsyou can benefit from one ongoing herbal preparation at a time. multiple benefits supplied by the same dose count as one preparation.

sections.title: Hide
sections.text: hidetalentaccess: rogue; hellion xp: 5 xphide grants +10 on stealth checks while the character remains perfectly still in a place where hiding is physically possible.a character who also possesses sneak may move while retaining this bonus, provided the character remains concealed enough to use stealth. detect invisibility reveals a character using hide.hide does not create concealment or a hiding place, and it does not grant sneak.

sections.title: Juggle
sections.text: juggletalentaccess: swashbuckler; bard xp: 5 xpwhen a task ordinarily requires one free hand, the character may perform it while both hands are occupied by momentarily tossing, shifting, or releasing one held object and returning to the original grip. this can allow the character to drink a potion, reload or throw a weapon, manipulate an item, or perform another one-handed task without first freeing a hand.juggle does not reduce the action the task requires, retrieve an inaccessible item, satisfy a requirement for two free hands, permit extra weapons to be wielded simultaneously, or allow two one-handed tasks to be performed at once.

sections.title: Kick
sections.text: kicktalentaccess: mercenary; swashbuckler xp: 5 xp through swashbuckler; 10 xp through mercenaryonce per round, the character may spend 1 pe, in addition to the ordinary full-attack cost, to add one kick-only attack pass anywhere in that full attack. kick counts toward the full-attack limit.make a kick attack using 1d20 + bab + strength modifier + applicable talent and situational modifiers. kick requires no free hand and can target only a creature of the character's size or smaller. it may be dodged or blocked with a shield but cannot be parried.on a hit, kick deals no hp damage. it instead removes 1d6 pe, never reducing pe below 0. armor creates no special interaction with kick.

sections.title: Kip-Up
sections.text: kip-uptalentaccess: swashbuckler xp: 10 xponce per round, when the character becomes prone, the character may immediately attempt a dexterity check at -4 without spending pe. on success, the character regains their footing before prone removes any unresolved attack passes.this reaction uses no movement and does not provoke an attack of opportunity. on failure, the character remains prone and resolves the condition normally. attempting kip-up expends its once-per-round use whether the check succeeds or fails.

sections.text: loretalentaccess: bard xp: 10 xpby touching an object and concentrating for one uninterrupted minute, the bard may seek impressions left by its past. the dm secretly makes an intelligence check. for this check, increase the bard's intelligence score by 1 for every two bard job levels, then apply any penalty warranted by the obscurity of the object's history.on success, the bard receives useful impressions concerning matters such as the object's history, former owners, associated places, curses, activation words, riddles, or secrets. failure

sections.text: lucid dreamingtalentaccess: priest; shaman; sorcerer; warlock; necromancer xp: 10 xp through priest, sorcerer, warlock, or necromancer; 15 xp through shamanonce after each long rest, and no more than once per 24 hours, the character may use both movement and the main action to restore magical energy equal to the highest job level among the character's jobs that grant access to lucid dreaming.the character's main job and the job through which this talent was purchased do not change the amount restored. lucid dreaming requires neither sleep nor an actual dream and cannot restore magical energy above its maximum.

sections.title: Mana Shield
sections.text: mana shieldtalentaccess: sorcerer xp: 15 xpmana shield protects the sorcerer only during the interval in which the sorcerer is casting a spell. when the sorcerer would take damage during that interval, resolve applicable damage reduction and any pe mitigation first. before applying the remaining damage, the sorcerer may spend any amount of me; each me spent prevents 1 damage.this expenditure requires no separate action. if mana shield reduces the remaining damage to 0, that damage does not interrupt the spell. mana shield is not a continuing personal barrier outside a casting interval and does not activate merely because the sorcerer is maintaining a spell that has already resolved.

sections.title: Pathfinding
sections.text: pathfindingtalentaccess: scout; requires endurance xp: 10 xpwhen the scout guides wilderness travel and route choice can materially shorten the journey, pathfinding halves the expected travel time. a journey that would normally require eight hours therefore takes four. pathfinding provides no benefit when an established road is already the fastest route.

sections.title: Peek
sections.text: peektalentaccess: rogue xp: 5 xpwhen the rogue can observe a creature well enough to notice its clothing, carried equipment, and movement, make a perception check.success gives the rogue a useful impression of what the target carries, what may be concealed upon the target, and where a concealed object is likely kept. the dm determines how much detail the circumstances reveal. an object whose presence produces no observable sign remains hidden.peek requires no fixed action or range beyond a useful opportunity to observe.

sections.text: planttalentaccess: rogue; bard xp: 10 xp through rogue; 15 xp through bardplant uses sleight of hand to place a concealable object upon a creature or among that creature's possessions without being noticed.in combat, plant ordinarily uses a main action. outside combat, it takes however long the attempt naturally requires. an unaware target does not automatically receive an opposed check. an alert, suspicious, or actively guarded target may oppose plant with perception.the object must physically fit in the selected location, and the character must be able to reach the target or the relevant possessions. object size, vigilance, clothing, and accessibility modify the attempt normally.

sections.title: Rescue
sections.text: rescuetalentaccess: mercenary; barbarian; scout; bard; paladin; hellion xp: 5 xp through mercenary, scout, paladin, or hellion; 10 xp through barbarian or bardonce per round, use rescue as an immediate interrupt when a perceived attack or hostile targeted spell selects a willing ally within 10 feet.the rescuer moves into the ally's position without provoking attacks of opportunity, moves the ally into an adjacent legal space of the rescuer's choice, and becomes the target of the triggering effect. the effect then resolves normally against the rescuer.the rescuer must be a legal target for the triggering effect, and an adjacent legal space must exist for the ally. rescue cannot intercept an area effect.if the rescuer makes a full attack during the next round, first establish and cap its legal schedule, then forfeit one retained attack pass. if the rescuer takes another main action instead, rescue imposes no additional action loss. forfeiting a paired pass removes both attacks belonging to it.rescue costs no pe and requires a willing ally.

sections.title: Scout Camouflage
sections.text: scout camouflagejob featuregrant: scout xp: nonethe scout may spend 10 minutes preparing camouflage from materials appropriate to the current terrain. while it remains matched to that terrain, the scout gains +20 on stealth checks to remain hidden. this bonus does not stack with hide's +10; use the greater applicable bonus.the scout may remain stationary normally. if the scout also possesses sneak, movement made while sneaking does not end the camouflage. otherwise movement ends it. attacking, casting a spell, taking another conspicuous action, or leaving the matching terrain ends the camouflage after the action resolves.scout camouflage is physical concealment rather than invisibility. detect invisibility does not reveal the scout, and ordinary scent-based detection cannot locate the scout through the camouflage alone. tremorsense and another sense that directly detects the scout's movement or physical contact with the ground still function normally. the +20 remains a stealth modifier rather than automatic success.
