sections.title: Skinning
sections.text: skinningtalentaccess: scout xp: 10 xpthe scout can recover hides, pelts and scales from slain monsters while preserving their exceptional protective properties for use in armor, clothing and other equipment.ordinary animals such as bears, wolves and rabbits can be skinned using survival and the appropriate craft skills. those skills may also recover material from monsters, such as dragon scales. skinning preserves the exceptional hide's protective properties, including supernatural dr, that ordinary harvesting would lose.harvesting a hide. the creature must have usable skin, hide or scales, and its threat band must be equal to or lower than the scout's job rank. for example, harvesting a master-threat creature requires a master scout. the dm determines the applicable threat band; this is separate from the creature's lettered domain ranks. constructs and mechanical bodies cannot be skinned. aberrations may qualify when their anatomy provides a usable hide.the scout must have suitable skinning tools capable of cutting and working the creature's hide. the dm determines whether the available tools are adequate; without them, the attempt cannot be made.make a survival check using wisdom, with a penalty equal to half the hide's dr, rounded down. dr 10 imposes -5; dr 20 imposes -10. use the protection supplied by the hide itself, excluding worn armor, temporary spells and unrelated defensive abilities.on success, recover usable hide with its exceptional protective properties preserved. on failure, the hide is mangled and yields no usable material. the dm

sections.title: Skirmish
sections.text: skirmishtalentaccess: mercenary; swashbuckler; rogue xp: 10 xpafter using movement to travel at least 10 feet, every ranged weapon attack the character makes later that turn gains +1d6 damage.skirmish applies to bows, crossbows, slings, and thrown weapons. it does not apply to spells or another non-weapon effect. the movement must precede the benefiting attack. a full attack made after that movement applies skirmish to every qualifying ranged attack it contains.skirmish costs no pe, has no separate usage limit, and is not a class mastery.

sections.title: Smite Evil
sections.text: smite eviljob feature · masterygrant: paladin xp: noneimmediately before resolving one otherwise legal physical attack, the paladin may spend 1 pe and declare that attack a smite. a physical attack for this purpose is a weapon or unarmed attack, not a spell or spell-like effect unless an explicit rule says otherwise. declaring a smite requires neither movement nor a main action, grants no extra attack, and changes none of the underlying attack's normal timing or requirements. the pe is spent whether the attack hits or misses.the declaration selects paladin mastery for that round if no mastery is already locked. a different locked mastery prevents smite. once paladin mastery is selected, any number of the paladin's remaining weapon or unarmed attacks that round may each

sections.title: Sneak
sections.text: sneaktalentaccess: swashbuckler; scout; rogue; bard; hellion; elf or dark elf xp: 5 xp through a job; no xp for an automatic racial granta character with sneak automatically succeeds on stealth checks against creatures that are not actively on guard, provided the character remains outside their immediate line of sight.sneak does not grant hide. a character who also possesses the hide talent may move while retaining hide's +10 stealth bonus, provided concealment continues to make hiding physically possible. detect invisibility still reveals a character using hide.

sections.title: Sneak Attack
sections.text: sneak attacktalent · masteryaccess: rogue xp: 5 xpsneak attack, backstab, hamstring, and dual backstab form one package. they may work together when their

sections.title: Songs of Antimagic
sections.text: songs of antimagictalent · masteryaccess: bard xp: 5 xpcost: 3 me to start; 1 me per minute to maintain.reduce the effective caster level of every affected caster and ongoing spell effect by half the bard job level, rounded down. the reduction is at least 1 and at most 10, and it cannot reduce a caster level below 1. this changes caster-level-derived damage dice, durations, caster-level checks, and comparable values. it does not change spell access, spell circle, me cost, or spell speed. ordinarily it does not change spell dc.

sections.title: Songs of Dancing
sections.text: songs of dancingtalent · masteryaccess: bard xp: 10 xpcost: 4 me to start; 1 me per round to maintain.the bard must already have dance active and maintain it throughout the song. every other hearer makes a will save. on failure, involuntary dancing consumes that creature's movement each round while the effect continues; it retains its main and free actions. this is mind-affecting. leaving the area, losing hearing, the song ending, or dance ending removes the effect.see classes — bard: shared performance rules.

sections.title: Songs of Death
sections.text: songs of deathtalent · masteryaccess: bard xp: 5 xpcost: 3 me to start; 1 me per round to maintain.each pulse deals flat magical hp damage equal to one-fifth of the bard job level, rounded down, with a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 6, to every living hearer, including the bard, allies, and enemies. a successful will save negates the entire performance for that creature, including dance's pe loss. magic protection applies; physical armor does not.the damage stops at 0 hp and never crosses into lp. the first time a creature reaches 0 hp from this continuous performance, it becomes unconscious and makes one fortitude save against the bard's dc. failure also makes it permanently deafened. this deafness prevents later pulses from affecting that creature but does not itself wake the creature. song-induced unconsciousness ends when the performance ends or the creature rises above 0 hp. while dance is active, each affected creature also loses 1 pe per pulse.see classes — bard: shared performance rules.

sections.title: Songs of Healing
sections.text: songs of healingtalent · masteryaccess: bard xp: 5 xpcost: 2 me to start; 1 me per round to maintain.each pulse restores hp equal to one-tenth of the bard job level, rounded up, with a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 3, to every living hearer, including the bard, allies, and enemies: 1 hp at bard levels 1–10, 2 at 11–20, and 3 at 21–31. armor-contributed hp belongs to the same hp pool and can be restored. the song does not restore lp or temporary hp. while dance is active, each pulse also restores 1 pe.for each listener, track how much hp and pe this bard has actually restored with songs of healing today. that bard can restore at most hp equal to the bard job level and, separately, pe equal to half that level rounded down to the same listener in one day. a pulse that reaches a remaining limit restores only the available amount; a full hp limit does not prevent legal pe restoration, or vice versa. restoration prevented by a full resource pool does not count toward the daily limit.see classes — bard: shared performance rules.

sections.title: Songs of Magic
sections.text: songs of magictalent · masteryaccess: bard xp: 10 xpcost: 4 me to start; 1 me per round to maintain.every creature that hears the song, including the bard, allies, and enemies, increases effective caster level by one-third of the bard job level, rounded down, with a minimum increase of 1 and a maximum of 10. this changes caster-level-derived damage dice, durations, caster-level checks, and comparable values. it does not change spell access, spell circle, me cost, or spell speed. ordinarily it does not change spell dc.while dance is active, the increase also raises spell dc one-for-one, symmetrically with songs of antimagic. the increase applies to spells cast while hearing the song; it does not alter effects created before exposure.see classes — bard: shared performance rules.

sections.title: Songs of Protection
sections.text: songs of protectiontalent · masteryaccess: bard xp: 5 xpcost: 2 me to start; 1 me per minute to maintain.

sections.title: Songs of Silence
sections.text: songs of silencetalent · masteryaccess: bard xp: 15 xpcost: 4 me to start; 1 me per round to maintain.this song creates a moving 60-foot field centered on the bard. sound created inside remains audible inside but does not ordinarily pass out. sound originating outside enters normally. very loud sound may escape at the dm's judgment. verbal spell components work inside the field. while dance is active, the outward boundary becomes absolute. the field is environmental and does not require hearing or a save.see classes — bard: shared performance rules.

sections.title: Songs of Sleep
sections.text: songs of sleeptalent · masteryaccess: bard xp: 15 xpcost: 4 me to start; 1 me per round to maintain.each enemy hearer makes an initial will save. on failure, first establish and cap the creature's legal full-attack schedule, then remove one retained attack, to a minimum of one remaining attack. also add 1 pe to every action or reaction already costing pe; a 0-pe action remains free.while dance is active, an initial failure requires a second will save at the beginning of the creature's next turn. failure makes it sleep and become unconscious until damaged, unable to hear the song, or the song ends. success on the second save leaves the base penalties in place; waking from damage also leaves them while the performance continues. immunity to magical or mundane sleep blocks only the final sleep. complete mind-affecting immunity blocks the entire song.see classes — bard: shared performance rules.

sections.title: Songs of War
sections.text: songs of wartalent · masteryaccess: bard xp: 5 xpcost: 2 me to start; 1 me per minute to maintain.each hearing ally gains a morale attack bonus equal to one-fifth of the bard job level, rounded down, with a minimum of +1 and a maximum of +6. while dance is active, the same morale bonus applies to rolled active and static defense, including dodge, parry, and block. dance also grants +0.5 attack speed through bard job level 19 or +1 at level 20 or later; apply it to the next round's schedule.the morale bonus does not stack with heroism, rallying cry, or another morale bonus; use the greatest. the attack-speed increase does not stack with haste, rallying cry, or another temporary effect-based attack-speed increase; use the greatest. allies retain their own class masteries.see classes — bard: shared performance rules.

sections.title: Spirit Bond
sections.text: spirit bondjob featuregrant: shaman xp: noneonce per year, the shaman may petition a spirit with whom they have an established bond and ask for aid. a shaman may maintain bonds with several spirits, but they all share this single use. the request is limited by

sections.title: Staves
sections.text: stavestalentaccess: scout; rogue; bard; priest; shaman; sorcerer; warlock; necromancer xp: 5 xp through priest, shaman, sorcerer, warlock, or necromancer; 15 xp through scout, rogue, or bardstaves permits the character to activate magical staves. use the common activation, class-eligibility check, charge, and targeting procedure under spells and spellcasting — staves.the talent does not teach the stored spell. the staff and its spell determine stored values and exceptional effects. staves does not grant staff weapon training.

sections.title: Steal
sections.text: stealtalentaccess: rogue xp: 5 xpsteal uses sleight of hand opposed by perception to remove an accessible object from an unaware creature or from that creature's carried possessions without being noticed.in combat, steal uses a main action. outside combat, it takes however long the attempt naturally requires.an object no larger than a small dagger carries no additional penalty. removing a larger object, up to approximately the size of a shortsword, applies -4 to sleight of hand. larger objects are not ordinarily eligible.the rogue may reach into an accessible pocket, belt, backpack, or similar carried container. the object must physically fit through the opening and be reachable. an item currently held, wielded, or otherwise being actively manipulated cannot be taken with steal.failure, discovery, and the possibility of another attempt follow the circumstances and the ordinary repeated-effort rule.

sections.title: Street Network
sections.text: street networktalentaccess: bard; rogue xp: 5 xp through bard; 15 xp through roguestreet network represents the character's ability to read urban territory, reach useful local contacts, and follow information through word of mouth.finding contacts and services. in a settlement large enough to support the relevant activity, spend one hour and reasonable local expenses to locate one plausibly available contact or service. suitable results include a fence for ordinary stolen goods, a black-market seller, discreet lodging or a temporary safe place, a local guide, messenger, or intermediary, or someone able to provide a useful lead about a person, item, faction, or recent event.common and locally available services are found automatically. dangerous, secret, scarce, or heavily watched services require a charisma check. street network cannot create a contact or service that does not plausibly exist, guarantee cooperation, dictate prices, or remove the ordinary cost and risk of illegal activity.reading the streets. after ten minutes observing a district, the character learns its obvious street-level structure: who appears to control it, where law or gang patrols concentrate, which visible routes seem safest, and whether recent trouble has changed ordinary behavior.concealed control, a carefully hidden danger, or another non-obvious fact may require perception, investigation, knowledge (underworld), or another appropriate check. once familiar with the district, the character gains +4 on checks made there to detect a tail, recognize an impending street ambush, or avoid becoming lost.following a rumor trail. the character gains +4 on charisma checks made to question people and pursue rumors about a named person, item, faction, place, or event. this bonus improves the character's approach; it does not grant automatic answers. a source can reveal only what that source plausibly knows, and repeatedly questioning the same source does not create new information without changed circumstances.

sections.title: Suppression
sections.text: suppressiontalentaccess: barbarian; exclusive xp: 10 xpsuppression costs no pe. the barbarian spends the entire turn and makes a wisdom check.on success, the barbarian's personal magic resistance, including trained or inherent mr, becomes 0 for one minute. magic protection is unaffected.mr granted by equipment cannot be suppressed. equipment that remains worn continues to apply its mr normally; equipment must be removed if the barbarian does not want that mr to oppose incoming magic.the barbarian may end suppression early as a free action. before it expires, the barbarian may spend another entire turn and make another wisdom check. success restarts the one-minute duration without ending the continuous suppression period. failure leaves the existing duration unchanged.when suppression finally ends, the suppressed personal mr returns immediately. roll that restored mr separately against every ongoing magical effect acquired during the continuous suppression period that mr could originally have resisted. success purges that effect; failure leaves it in place.instantaneous results are not reversed. hp already restored remains restored, damage remains dealt, and expended resources remain spent. effects already present before suppression began are not checked again.suppression is not a class mastery.

sections.title: Tame
sections.text: tametalentaccess: scout; exclusive xp: 5 xptame allows a scout to arrest the aggression of a wild creature without turning it into a pet or companion. using it is a main action, and the creature must be able to perceive the scout.against an unintelligent wild creature, make a charisma check. increase the scout's effective check threshold by 1 for every five scout levels, to a maximum of +6 at level 30. the dm applies any penalty or bonus warranted by the creature's threat and the circumstances.the first successful check stops the creature's aggression toward the scout. the scout may immediately make a second check as part of the same

sections.title: Taunt
sections.text: taunttalentaccess: swashbuckler; exclusive xp: 10 xptaunt costs no pe. use it as a main action or in place of one attack during a full attack. choose one creature that can see and hear the swashbuckler. the target makes a will save against the swashbuckler's ordinary charisma-based talent dc. a creature that cannot understand the swashbuckler's words gains +4 on the save.the dm may apply a small circumstance modifier for an obvious numerical advantage, usually 2 and never more than 4. a target secure behind superior numbers is easier to provoke and takes the penalty; a badly outnumbered target gains the bonus.on a failed save, the target must direct its actions toward attacking, hindering, or reaching the swashbuckler to the best of its ability. it cannot voluntarily retreat, use recall to leave combat, or otherwise abandon the confrontation.for taunt's duration, reduce the target's intelligence score by the swashbuckler's charisma modifier. this is a temporary penalty, not lasting ability damage. immediately recalculate the target's available spell circles and concentration capacity. the target drops enough maintained spells to fit the reduced capacity and cannot cast a spell circle its reduced intelligence no longer supports. any spell it can still cast must serve its aggression toward the swashbuckler. a dropped spell does not resume when taunt ends.

sections.title: Third Attack
sections.text: third attacktalentaccess: mercenary; barbarian; paladin; hellion xp: 15 xpthird attack adds +0.5 attack speed to the primary attack of a weapon full attack. it does not increase the attack speed of a brawling or wild-fighting full attack. apply it through the ordinary fractional schedule. a full attack still costs 1 pe total regardless of the number of passes it produces.third attack provides no benefit while a swashbuckler uses dual wield. it stacks with generally applicable attack-speed increases such as fury when their own requirements are met.

sections.title: Tornado Slash
sections.text: tornado slashtalent · masteryaccess: swashbuckler xp: 15 xptornado slash is part of class mastery: swashbuckler. it costs 4 pe, uses the main action, and requires greased lightning to be at its full +6 buildup.every other creature within 10 feet is affected, including allies. use the main-hand weapon's ordinary damage die. roll one such die for every two swashbuckler levels, to a maximum of fifteen dice. roll no more than four damage dice and replace each additional die with +2. a level-30 swashbuckler therefore rolls 4dx + 22.add the ability modifier ordinarily used for the weapon's damage, every explicit weapon damage modifier, and the expended +6 greased lightning buildup once.tornado slash makes no attack roll. it adds no margin of success, cannot critically hit, and receives no attack-only modifier. use the main-hand weapon's pen and damage type.

sections.title: Toughness
sections.text: toughnesstalentaccess: barbarian xp: 10 xptoughness grants flat physical damage reduction equal to half the barbarian job level, rounded down. add 1 at barbarian level 7 and another 1 at barbarian level 10.toughness has no armor grade, so armor penetration does not reduce it. against ordinary physical damage, compare toughness with the final grade-adjusted damage reduction from worn physical armor or natural hide and use the greater value; do not add them together. separately applicable magical or supernatural protection remains independent unless its own rule says otherwise.toughness applies to ordinary physical damage generally, not only to named weapon attacks.

sections.title: Tracking
sections.text: trackingtalentaccess: barbarian; warlock; scout xp: 15 xp through barbarian or warlock; no xp for the scout's automatic granttracking is an extraordinary ability to recognize and interpret trails at a glance. briefly scanning for a trail requires a wisdom check. in combat, the scan uses a main action; outside combat, it requires a short pause appropriate to the scene.conditions, concealment, weather, elapsed time, and the quality of the remaining signs determine the check's difficulty. success can reveal the trail's direction, approximate numbers, broad creature type, and roughly when the passage occurred.once a trail is found, the character may follow it at ordinary walking or riding speed without the slow deliberate search required by survival. tracking can follow an airborne creature when it leaves a discernible trace.tracking cannot invent evidence where no physical, supernatural, or otherwise perceptible trace remains. there is no universal maximum trail age; circumstances can make an old or concealed trail impossible. deliberate extraordinary or supernatural concealment may oppose the attempt.tracking is not a spell, a survival use, or a class mastery.

sections.title: Trance
sections.text: trancetalentaccess: priest; shaman; paladin; hellion; sorcerer; warlock; necromancer xp: 10 xp through priest, shaman, sorcerer, warlock, or necromancer; 15 xp through paladin or hellionfive uninterrupted minutes of trance restore magical energy equal to the character's wisdom modifier, with a minimum of 1 and no increase above maximum magical energy.the first use after a long rest succeeds automatically. each later attempt may be made no more than once per hour and requires a wisdom check at -4. a failed check consumes the five minutes and that hour's attempt.a long rest refreshes the automatic use, no more than once per 24 hours. trance is distinct from elven reverie.

sections.title: Tumbling
sections.text: tumblingtalentaccess: bard xp: 10 xptumbling has two uses. neither is part of class mastery: bard.tumbling through threatened space. declare tumbling as part of movement before crossing threatened space and make one acrobatics check for the complete movement.begin with the character's current acrobatics threshold. add the character's bab, subtract the greatest bab among the enemies that could make an attack of opportunity because of that movement, and apply another -2 for each additional such enemy beyond the first. armor mobility and every other relevant circumstance apply.success prevents every attack of opportunity caused by that movement. failure permits each eligible enemy to use an available attack-of-opportunity allowance normally. this use costs no pe and does not permit movement through occupied space, impassable terrain, physical restraints, or another obstacle the character cannot actually cross.tumbling behind an ally. once per round, when an attack declares the bard as its target, spend 1 pe to use tumbling as an immediate interrupt. choose a willing adjacent ally within 5 feet.the bard and ally exchange positions without provoking attacks of opportunity, and the ally becomes the target of the triggering attack. the bard must perceive the attack, be able to move, and select an ally who is a legal

sections.title: Ultimate Evasion
sections.text: ultimate evasiontalentaccess: rogue xp: 15 xpultimate evasion is a passive talent and is not part of class mastery: rogue.after a discrete ranged attack connects but before its damage or other delivered effects resolve, roll d100. on 50 or less, the rogue evades the attack completely. roll separately against every qualifying attack. ultimate evasion costs no pe, consumes no dodge use or other action, and has no per-round limit.the attack must be one that could physically be evaded, and its projectile can be no larger than a small boulder. arrows, bolts, bullets, thrown weapons, and a spell-created projectile with a genuine travel path can qualify. area effects, explosions, automatic-hit effects, and anything that cannot physically be dodged do not qualify.the rogue need not see the projectile, but must possess enough usable sensory awareness to react and must be able to move freely. ultimate evasion does not function when the rogue is entirely unaware of the attack or unable to move.successful ultimate evasion negates the complete hit, including a critical hit and any secondary effect delivered by it.

sections.title: Wands
sections.text: wandstalentaccess: rogue; bard; sorcerer; warlock; necromancer xp: 5 xp through sorcerer, warlock, or necromancer; 15 xp through rogue or bardwands permits the character to activate magical wands. use the common activation, class-eligibility check, charge, and targeting procedure under spells and spellcasting — wands.the talent does not teach the stored spell. the wand and its spell determine stored values and exceptional effects.

sections.title: Weapon Mastery
sections.text: weapon masterytalent · masteryaccess: mercenary xp: 10 xp for i; 15 xp for ii or iii  prerequisites: weapon mastery ii requires weapon mastery i; weapon mastery iii requires weapon mastery iiweapon mastery is the mercenary's passive class mastery. each tier is purchased separately when its rank becomes available, and each selection applies to a trained weapon group rather than one individual weapon. weapon mastery ii requires weapon mastery i, and weapon mastery iii requires weapon mastery ii.tiermastered weapon groupsbenefits while mercenary mastery is selectedweapon mastery ichoose one trained weapon group.+2 attack and +2 parry with weapons in every mastered group.weapon mastery iichoose a second trained weapon group.the bonuses become +4 attack and +4 parry with weapons in every mastered group.weapon mastery iiichoose a third trained weapon group.the bonuses become +6 attack and +6 parry with weapons in every mastered group. a mastered primary attack also gains +0.5 attack speed.weapon mastery grants no separate direct damage bonus; its attack bonus can increase damage through positive attack margin. during two-weapon fighting, each weapon receives the attack and parry bonuses when it belongs to a mastered group. weapon mastery iii's attack-speed increase applies to the mastered primary attack.every benefit in this weapon mastery line belongs to class mastery: mercenary. if another job's class mastery is selected for the round, weapon mastery's attack, parry, and attack speed benefits are suppressed for that entire round.when weapon mastery iii could change the coming round's attack speed, choose the round's class mastery at the start of that round before establishing the attack schedule. selecting mercenary mastery includes its qualifying +0.5 attack speed; selecting another mastery excludes it. gaining or losing the qualifying

sections.title: Wild Fighting
sections.text: wild fightingtalent · masteryaccess: barbarian xp: 15 xpwild fighting can be used only while berserk or fury is active and operates inside class mastery: barbarian.both hands must be empty or equipped only with the qualifying fist weapons described under brawling. armed and wild-fighting attacks cannot be mixed in the same full attack.wild fighting adds +0.5 attack speed to the primary unarmed attack. each pass granted by ordinary unarmed attack speed, brawling, and wild fighting contains two qualifying unarmed attacks. a single-attack main action still contains one attack. every wild fighting attack receives +4 attack. a defender attempting to parry one takes -4 parry.when wild fighting bare-handed, each attack deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage with pen 2. when using a qualifying fist weapon, use that weapon's printed damage die and damage type, and treat its pen as at least 2. every wild fighting attack deals lethal damage.while using wild fighting, the barbarian may parry an armed attack unarmed without the normal -4 penalty. wild fighting imposes no separate dodge penalty.second attack, third attack, and ordinary two-weapon fighting do not apply to a wild-fighting full attack. a generally applicable attack-speed increase adds unpaired passes with the primary attack. the full attack remains subject to the full-attack limit and pays the ordinary full-attack pe cost with no additional wild fighting cost.

sections.title: Wolverine Stance
sections.text: wolverine stancetalent · masteryaccess: swashbuckler xp: 15 xpwolverine stance is part of class mastery: swashbuckler. it has no activation cost, requires greased lightning at its full +6 buildup, and requires one light or medium one-handed melee weapon in each hand. these are the same weapon boundaries used by dual wield; the two weapons need not both be swords.activate wolverine stance as a free action at the beginning of the swashbuckler's turn. it cannot be voluntarily deactivated and ends when greased lightning ends.while wolverine stance is active, the swashbuckler cannot parry, gains 20 feet of speed, and does not provoke attacks of opportunity through movement. dodge remains available. a defender attempting to parry or block a wolverine attack takes -4 on that defense; dodge is unaffected.combined full attacks. establish the legal full-attack schedule and apply its attack limit before wolverine combines attacks. halve the retained qualifying weapon attacks, preserving a half-step when necessary. the ordinary full-greased-lightning schedule of five weapon attacks therefore becomes 2.5 combined attacks: three in the first wolverine round, two in the next, then alternating.

sections.title: Feats
sections.text: featslearning featsa feat is a character option learned outside the job-rank talent ladders. a job does not provide access merely because a feat would suit that job.after character creation, learning a feat requires all of the following:the prerequisites and any access restriction printed in the feat's entry;a willing and qualified instructor who knows the feat;suitable downtime for training; andthe feat's xp price.unless its own entry states another price, a feat costs 10 xp. there is no universal training duration.every feat has an availability rating. common feats are taught through ordinary martial, professional, or academic networks. uncommon feats require specialist instruction. rare feats require a master instructor. restricted feats require a particular instructor, school, order, or tradition approved by the dm. availability grants no feat automatically and waives none of its prerequisites, xp price, downtime, or training requirements.a human's creation-only bonus feat is an exception. during character creation, the human may select one legal ordinary feat without paying xp or finding an instructor and training time. the character must still meet the feat's prerequisites and any explicit access restriction.

sections.title: Reading a Feat Entry
sections.text: reading a feat entryevery feat entry is marked feat. it gives the feat's availability, prerequisites, any access restriction, xp price, and complete effect. if an entry establishes a special training condition or duration, that instruction applies only to that feat.

sections.title: Articulated Weapon Training
sections.text: articulated weapon trainingfeatavailability: rare prerequisites: bab +4 and training with a qualifying articulated weapon training: master instructor required xp: 10 xpflail and heavy flail qualify for articulated weapon training. another weapon qualifies only when its own rule identifies it as articulated.against an attack made with a qualifying articulated weapon, parry takes -8 and shield block takes -4. for flail and heavy flail, these penalties replace the weapons' ordinary -2 parry and -1 shield block

sections.title: Bracket Assault
sections.text: bracket assaultfeatavailability: rare prerequisite: bab +3 training: master instructor required xp: 10 xpbracket assault requires two allied combatants who both know the feat. they must act during the same initiative pass, stand within 5 feet of one another, possess one unresolved melee attack each, and threaten the same opponent. the opponent must be within one size category of both participants.the allies jointly declare bracket assault before either attack roll. each spends one available melee attack. the attacks occur simultaneously and otherwise resolve normally.the target cannot use the same defense type against both attacks. if it dodges one attack, it cannot dodge the other; if it shield blocks one, it cannot shield block the other. it may parry both only by using two separate weapons capable of parrying, one against each attack.

sections.title: Defensive Fighting
sections.text: defensive fightingfeatavailability: uncommon prerequisite: bab +3 xp: 10 xpwhen declaring a melee attack or melee full attack, before making the first attack roll, choose a whole-number penalty no greater than the character's

sections.title: Disarming Parry
sections.text: disarming parryfeatavailability: restricted prerequisites: dexterity 15 and disarm training: kasshin-ryu instructor required xp: 10 xpwhen declaring a full attack, the character may omit one available attack from that schedule. until the beginning of the character's next turn, one successful parry may trigger a disarm attempt against the attacker without spending another attack or pe.if that disarm succeeds, the character may immediately make one normal attack against the disarmed opponent. disarming parry can trigger only once each round.

sections.title: Duelist Stance
sections.text: duelist stancefeatavailability: rare prerequisites: bab +6 and trained knowledge (duelling) training: master instructor required xp: 20 xpat the beginning of a combat round, before the first

sections.title: Enhanced Block
sections.text: enhanced blockfeatavailability: uncommon prerequisite: bab +3 xp: 10 xpenhanced block grants +2 shield block, including blocks against qualifying projectiles. this bonus stacks with the shield's listed bonus, material bonuses, magical accuracy, and weapon focus (shields).at bab +3, enhanced block grants one additional penalty-free shield block each round. it grants one more for every three bab thereafter, to a maximum of five additional shield blocks at bab +15.enhanced block does not grant a shield or make shield block legal when the character could not otherwise use it.

sections.title: Enhanced Dodge
sections.text: enhanced dodgefeatavailability: common prerequisite: bab +3 xp: 10 xpenhanced dodge permanently increases the character's dodge by 1. this feat increase adds to the greatest applicable dodge-type bonus and to other legal bonuses affecting dodge. it applies once, even when several copies or references describe the feat.at bab +3, enhanced dodge grants one additional penalty-free dodge each round. it grants one more for every three bab thereafter, to a maximum of five additional dodges at bab +15.

sections.title: Enhanced Parry
sections.text: enhanced parryfeatavailability: uncommon prerequisite: bab +3 xp: 10 xpat bab +3, enhanced parry grants one additional penalty-free parry each round. it grants one more for every three bab thereafter, to a maximum of five additional parries at bab +15. these uses enter one shared parry pool and are not multiplied by wielding more than one weapon.enhanced parry does not make a weapon or attack capable of parrying when it could not otherwise do so.

sections.title: Feint
sections.text: feintfeatavailability: restricted prerequisites: bab +8 and trained bluff training: specific instructor or tradition required; somewhat more available to adventurers xp: 20 xpfeint replaces one melee attack. make an opposed bluff check against the target's sense motive check, adding bab to both thresholds.on success, choose one later melee attack the character makes against that target during the same round. against that attack, the target's defense is 10 + bab + applicable magical modifiers. the benefit expires at the end of the round if unused.after the character attempts to feint a target, every later feint attempt by that character against the same target during that encounter takes -4, whether the first attempt succeeded or failed.

sections.title: Field Medic
sections.text: field medicfeatavailability: uncommon prerequisites: intelligence 15 and trained medicine xp: 10 xpfield medic grants access to the urgent-care procedures described under bleeding and mortal wounds. this includes treating moderate or serious bleeding and attempting to remove one medically removable mortal wound when treatment begins within 10 minutes of the injury.these procedures stabilize the injury and remove the specified condition. they do not restore hp or lp, regrow missing tissue, or erase a lasting physical consequence.

sections.title: First Step of the Wind
sections.text: first step of the windfeatavailability: restricted prerequisite: bab +3 training: specific instructor or tradition required xp: 10 xpat the beginning of the character's turn, the character may declare first step of the wind. until the beginning of the character's next turn, add the character's wisdom modifier to dodge, parry, and shield block.the benefit remains while the character takes no offensive action. it also remains while using defensive fighting, provided every attack made during that turn is declared through defensive fighting.the benefit ends immediately if the character makes an attack that is not using defensive fighting, casts a harmful spell, or uses another hostile ability.the same wisdom modifier cannot be added more than once to one defense through first step of the wind, tekken, or another wisdom-to-defense ability.

sections.title: Flight
sections.text: flightfeatavailability: uncommon training: qualified instructor and practical flight training required xp: 10 xpflight teaches the character to control magical flight: holding position, turning, judging clearances and landing safely. a spell or other effect must supply the ability to fly.with this feat, use the effect's normal flight speed and control. while airborne, take -2 to all attack and active defense rolls. the effect's own movement, duration and action limits still apply.without flight: use half the effect's normal flight speed and take -8 to all attack and active defense rolls, replacing the trained -2 penalty. when control matters, make the following attribute checks:dexterity: hovering, tight turns, avoiding obstacles and difficult landings.intelligence: establishing control or recovering it after disruption.use the ordinary roll-under attribute-check procedure, with difficulty determined by the circumstances. make at most one such control check per round, using the attribute appropriate to the immediate problem. success achieves the attempted control; on failure, the

sections.title: Fool’s Guard
sections.text: fool’s guardfeatavailability: restricted prerequisites: intelligence 13 and bab +3 training: kasshin-ryu instructor required xp: 10 xpfool's guard is a stance used with a one-handed bladed weapon, a longsword, or a katana. at the beginning of the character's turn, the character may enter fool's guard. it cannot be active alongside another stance.entering fool's guard reduces the character's attack speed by 0.5 for the current round and the following round. the character cannot enter fool's guard again while that reduction remains.until the beginning of the character's next turn, the character gains +4 parry against the first melee attack made against them. if that parry succeeds, the character may immediately make one counterattack that cannot be parried.if that first melee attack hits, it deals +4 damage. it also qualifies for sneak attack when the attacker possesses sneak attack.an opponent with bab +5 or higher who has previously seen the character employ fool's guard may oppose the character's bluff with sense motive before making the qualifying attack. if the opponent wins, fool's guard grants no +4 parry and no counterattack against that

sections.title: Formation Combat
sections.text: formation combatfeatavailability: uncommon prerequisite: military drill xp: 10 xpwhen the character and an ally who also possesses formation combat are fighting the same opponent, the character may spend movement to grant that ally advantage on the ally's next attack or defense roll against that opponent.

sections.title: Frame Repair Training
sections.text: frame repair trainingfeatavailability: restricted prerequisites: trained engineering and trained craft (golem frames) training: qualified frame engineer, military repair corps, or comparable authorized tradition required xp: 10 xpframe repair training permits exceptional diagnosis and field restoration attempts involving serious or critical frame lp damage or system damage. every required tool, material, spell, plan, physical access condition, and skill check still applies.this feat never creates unavailable material, waives a physically necessary hangar, or permits ordinary fabricate to affect a core, magical relay, magical circuitry, mithril, adamantite, or another excluded material. the complete limits and restoration procedures belong to golem frames. the dm  determines what can be stabilized in the field.

sections.title: Golem Ranged Training
sections.text: golem ranged trainingfeatavailability: restricted prerequisites: qualified golem pilot and bab +1 training: instructor with an operational frame or equivalent training rig required xp: 10 xpthe character may operate ordinary ranged weapons installed on an elven-interface golem frame. this grants permission rather than an attack bonus. a particularly unusual weapon may require additional training.without golem ranged training, the character cannot make a frame ranged attack. emergency operation

sections.title: Guarded Menace
sections.text: guarded menacefeatavailability: rare prerequisites: bab +3; wielding a sword in one hand and a shield in the other training: master instructor required xp: 10 xpat the beginning of the character's turn, the character may enter guarded menace as a free action. it cannot be active alongside another stance.each time the character successfully shield blocks an attack made by an opponent, the critical-threat range of the character's sword attacks against that opponent expands by 1, to a maximum increase of 5. a critical  threat of 20 therefore becomes 19–20 after one qualifying block.after the character scores a critical hit against that opponent, that opponent's accumulated increase resets to 0.guarded menace ends when the character voluntarily ends it at the beginning of a turn, begins another stance, ceases to wield the required sword-and-shield configuration, becomes unconscious, or dies. every accumulated increase ends with the stance.

sections.title: Halfswording
sections.text: halfswordingfeatavailability: rare prerequisites: bab +3 and training with longsword, katana, claymore, estoc, or elven thinblade training: master instructor required xp: 10 xphalfswording requires a qualifying sword wielded in two hands, with no separate offhand weapon or shield. a future weapon may qualify when its own rule explicitly says so.once each round, the character may use one of these techniques:after successfully parrying a melee weapon, deal 1d6 + strength modifier damage to the attacker. use the held sword's pen, including its material and enchantment modifiers.

sections.title: Improved Grapple
sections.text: improved grapplefeatavailability: uncommon prerequisites: bab +3 and strength 13 or dexterity 13 xp: 10 xpimproved grapple allows a grab to replace one attack instead of consuming the entire main action. the grab takes no -2 attack penalty and does not provoke the defender's special free attack.using the grab during a full attack adds the grab's 1 pe cost to the ordinary full-attack cost. once the character controls a grapple, it may be maintained at the beginning of the character's turn without spending an attack. all other grab and grapple rules remain as described in combat.

sections.title: Jaded
sections.text: jadedfeatavailability: restricted prerequisites: three successful sanity checks against horrifying events, wisdom 14 or higher, and sanity 14 or lower access: dm approval xp: 20 xp, reduced by 1 xp for each humanoid the character has personally killed, to a minimum of 5 xpthe character has endured wonders and horrors beyond ordinary experience. mundane death, ordinary violence, and most monstrous abominations no longer require sanity checks or fear tests from the character.terrors of the abyss affect the character normally.

sections.title: Mailbreaker Training
sections.text: mailbreaker trainingfeatavailability: rare prerequisites: bab +4 and training with a qualifying mailbreaker weapon training: master instructor required xp: 10 xpwhen the character strikes the other participant in a grapple with a rondel dagger or another weapon explicitly identified as a mailbreaker, that weapon gains +1 pen against grade-sensitive physical armor.mailbreaker training does not alter flat, energy, or supernatural damage reduction.

sections.title: Military Drill
sections.text: military drillfeatavailability: uncommon prerequisite: basic military training xp: 10 xpwhile standing shoulder-to-shoulder with an ally who also possesses military drill, the character gains +1 attack and +1 defense. when three or more characters with military drill stand in one line, each gains +2 attack and +2 defense instead.

sections.title: Mounted Archer
sections.text: mounted archerfeatavailability: rare prerequisites: trained ride and mounted combat training: master instructor required xp: 10 xpmounted archer permits the character to use normal ranged attack speed and make ranged full attacks while mounted. the mount must complete its movement before the first attack.the character takes no ranged attack penalty while the mount is stationary or uses ordinary movement, -2 after double movement, and -4 after the mount runs. mounted weapon restrictions and reloading procedures remain as described in mounted ranged combat.

sections.title: Mounted Combat
sections.text: mounted combatfeatavailability: uncommon prerequisites: bab +1 and trained ride xp: 10 xpmounted combat permits normal melee attack speed and melee full attacks while mounted. attacks aimed at the mount are redirected to the rider.the rider gains +4 attack against a medium or smaller opponent on foot. a mounted charge gains +4 attack in place of the ordinary charge bonus, does not impose the ordinary -2 defense penalty, and may combine with the foot-opponent bonus. mounted combat also reduces ranged penalties caused by the mount's movement, but still permits only one mounted ranged attack rather than a ranged full attack.the complete mounted procedure, including charge pen, appropriate-weapon damage, and remaining mounted after damage, appears under mounted combat.

sections.title: Power Attack
sections.text: power attackfeatavailability: uncommon prerequisite: bab +3 xp: 10 xpwhen declaring a melee attack or melee full attack with a weapon wielded in two hands, before making the first attack roll, choose a whole-number value no greater than the character's bab or 6, whichever is lower.until the start of the character's next turn, subtract the chosen value from dodge, parry, and shield block. add  the same value to the damage of every successful melee attack made with a weapon wielded in two hands during that time.power attack cannot increase ranged-attack damage.

sections.title: Precise Shot
sections.text: precise shotfeatavailability: common prerequisite: bab +3 xp: 10 xpthe character ignores the ordinary -4 attack penalty for firing a ranged weapon at a target engaged in melee. precise shot does not remove cover, concealment, range, or another distinct modifier.

sections.title: Pressing Attack I
sections.text: pressing attack ifeatavailability: rare prerequisite: bab +5 training: master instructor required xp: 10 xpbefore making a melee attack roll, the character may declare pressing attack i. that attack takes a -2 penalty.if the target successfully defends against the attack, it takes a cumulative -2 penalty to its defense against that character's subsequent pressing attacks, to a maximum of -6. track the accumulation separately for each attacker and target; no other attacker benefits from it.when that character's pressing attack connects with the target, that character's accumulated penalty against the target resets to 0. the accumulation also ends with the encounter.

sections.title: Pressing Attack II
sections.text: pressing attack iifeatavailability: rare prerequisites: pressing attack i and bab +9 training: master instructor required xp: 10 xppressing attack ii follows the complete pressing attack i procedure, including the -2 attack penalty, but each successful defense imposes a cumulative -4 penalty against that character's later pressing attacks, to a maximum of -12.a character possessing pressing attack ii uses that version rather than combining both versions.

sections.title: Run
sections.text: runfeatavailability: common xp: 10 xpthe character may run up to five times speed, or four times speed while wearing heavy armor or while encumbered. the character retains the dexterity modifier to defense while running.run duration, pe expenditure, and the consequences of exceeding the character's constitution follow the complete run procedure in combat.

sections.title: Skill Focus
sections.text: skill focusfeatavailability: common prerequisites: bab +4 and training in the selected skill xp: 10 xp for each selectionchoose one trained skill. each selection grants +2 on checks with that skill.a character may possess a total number of skill focus selections equal to the permanent intelligence modifier + 1, with a minimum capacity of one. temporary intelligence and equipment do not increase this capacity.the same skill may be selected up to three times, granting a maximum of +6. every selection counts against the character's total skill focus capacity.skill focus does not grant skill training. it remains separate from skill mastery and stacks with it; skill mastery grants advanced uses rather than a universal numerical bonus.

sections.title: Sweeping Slash I
sections.text: sweeping slash ifeatavailability: rare prerequisites: warrior job level 8 and bab +3 training: master instructor required xp: 10 xpwhen one of the character's attack passes is reached during a full attack, the character may replace that entire pass, including every attack it would normally contain, with sweeping slash i. it requires a two-handed melee weapon that deals slashing damage.choose up to three creatures within the weapon's reach and make one attack roll. each target chooses and resolves its defense separately against that roll.sweeping slash i cannot score a critical hit. a natural 20 retains its ordinary attack total and must still meet each target's defense. every connecting result is an ordinary hit and cannot trigger critical damage or critical effects.roll damage separately for every target the attack connects with. subtract 3 from each damage result before protection, to a minimum result of 0.only one sweeping slash may be attempted each round.

sections.title: Sweeping Slash II
sections.text: sweeping slash iifeatavailability: rare prerequisites: sweeping slash i and bab +7 training: master instructor required xp: 10 xpsweeping slash ii follows the complete sweeping slash i procedure without reducing its damage results. a character possessing sweeping slash ii uses that procedure rather than combining both versions.like sweeping slash i, it cannot score critical hits or trigger critical effects.

sections.title: Weapon Focus
sections.text: weapon focusfeatavailability: common xp: 10 xp for each selectionchoose one weapon group from the equipment chapter. the character gains +1 attack and +1 parry with weapons in that group.alternatively, choose shields. this choice grants +1 shield block with any shield, including blocks against qualifying projectiles.weapon focus may be learned more than once. each weapon group and the shields choice may be selected only once. if a weapon belongs to more than one focused group, apply the bonus only once.

sections.title: Equipment at a Glance
sections.text: equipment at a glancean equipment profile keeps an item's rules, handling, weight, typical value, and availability together. weapons list damage and armor penetration (pen); armor lists armor grade (grade), damage reduction (dr), and armor hp; shields list the defensive bonuses they provide. pen is compared with grade to determine how much physical armor dr applies, while armor hp increases the wearer's maximum hp rather than measuring the armor's structural durability. typical value is a comparison point, not a guaranteed shop price, and availability shows how readily an item can normally be found. a specific item's entry controls any exception to these general rules.

sections.title: Silver-Equivalent Accounting
sections.text:
silver-equivalent accountingten copper equal one silver, and ten silver equal one gold. equipment uses silver as its ordinary reference value, so prices, treasure, and foreign coins can be compared without requiring players to maintain several parallel accounting systems.
record the mint or origin of a character's money when it matters. the character may still total that money by its silver-equivalent value: a pouch can contain taslamaran crowns or imperial deniers while the character sheet records what the collection is ordinarily worth in silver.
silver-equivalent accounting does not guarantee that every coin will be accepted at that value. a merchant may weigh, discount, exchange, or refuse an unfamiliar or distrusted mint.
as approximate economic comparisons, one copper is about an ordinary laborer's daily earnings, one silver is about a skilled artisan's weekly earnings, and one gold is about ten weeks of skilled work. these are guides to scale, not fixed wages or modern-currency conversions.

sections.title: Local Currencies and Foreign Coin
sections.text: local currencies and foreign cointhe nations use their own coinage. these names use vanaheim's ordinary ten-to-one accounting ratio.

sections.title: Typical Value and Variable Prices
sections.text:
typical value and variable pricesan item's typical value is its expected silver-equivalent value under ordinary conditions. it is not a guaranteed shop price.
region, scarcity, war, quality, legality, demand, and coin reputation can change the actual price or make an item unavailable. the dm determines the local result from the situation; there is no universal market-price modifier table.
catalogue values are based on the labor, materials, construction, and availability appropriate to vanaheim.

sections.title: Availability and Scarcity
sections.text:
availability and scarcityequipment can carry one of four availability labels:
common: normally present in ordinary trade where the item is culturally and practically appropriate.limited: obtainable through the right market, craft, supplier, or modest search, but not reliably stocked everywhere.rare: normally requires a specialist source, connection, substantial search, or unusual opportunity.restricted: controlled, prohibited, politically sensitive, or limited to authorized buyers. an item can be restricted without being physically rare.
availability communicates an item's position in the market. it does not establish a public dc, settlement requirement, waiting period, or guarantee of access. when acquisition requires mechanical resolution, the dm may use a private contact, fixer, or fence procedure.
some exceptional armor and shields are marked nationally controlled instead of receiving an ordinary market label. they are priceless for catalogue purposes, have no public typical value, and cannot be acquired merely by offering sufficient silver.

sections.title: Reading Equipment Profiles
sections.text: reading equipment profilesan equipment profile lists the values and exceptions needed to use an item. it does not repeat universal combat procedures, and it does not create a rule from a field that is absent.

sections.title: Common Profile Fields
sections.text:
common profile fieldsfieldmeaningitemthe ordinary or proper name of the equipment.categorya formal equipment classification, such as a light, medium, or heavy weapon or armor. a category can establish baseline values and interactions.handlinghow the item is held, worn, carried, mounted, installed, loaded, or activated. weapon profiles use the separate hands field.damagethe item's listed damage dice or other explicit damage value. the complete damage procedure belongs to combat.armor penetration (pen)a weapon or attack's ability to defeat grade-sensitive physical armor.protection valuesarmor grade (grade) measures physical armor resistance; damage reduction (dr) subtracts from applicable damage; armor hit points (armor hp) increase the wearer's maximum hp while worn; a shield bonus contributes to block.range, capacity, and speedeffective range is the distance within which a ranged weapon attacks without a range penalty. capacity records ammunition, charges, fuel, or another finite supply. speed records movement supplied by an item, mount, or vehicle.typical valuethe item's expected value in silver under ordinary conditions, not a guaranteed local selling price.availabilitycommon, limited, rare, or restricted, as defined under money, markets, and availability.weightthe item's weight in pounds. a container's contents add their own weight.requirements and restrictionsconditions that govern who can use the item or how it can be used.propertiesdefined keywords or short item-specific rules that modify the ordinary procedure.
an item lists typical value, availability, and weight when those values are known and relevant. a blank or dash in one of these fields never means that the item is free, unrestricted, or weightless.

sections.title: Equipment Categories and Properties
sections.text:
equipment categories and propertiesa category is part of the item's basic classification. for example, light, medium, and heavy establish the ordinary starting pen of a weapon and the ordinary starting grade of armor. a category does not automatically determine every other field.
a property is a defined rule attached to a particular item. it can supply special handling, an alternate use, a restriction, or an exception. a property changes only what its text states; its name does not imply additional rules.

sections.title: Requirements and Restrictions
sections.text:
requirements and restrictionsa requirement identifies something needed for a listed use, such as a minimum ability, training, free hands, ammunition, or a particular situation. a restriction identifies a use that is unavailable, such as a bow that cannot be fired while mounted.
the item entry states the consequence of failing a requirement or meeting a restriction. only the listed consequences apply; an additional penalty or reduced-use option requires an explicit rule.

sections.title: Item-Specific Exceptions
sections.text:
item-specific exceptionsa specific item can override a general rule by stating the exception in its own profile. the exception is narrow: permission to use one bow while mounted does not change other longbows, and a weapon that qualifies for one special maneuver does not grant that qualification to its entire category.
when an item profile and a universal procedure appear to conflict, apply the item text only to the exact value or use it changes. the remaining universal procedure still applies.

sections.title: Carrying Capacity and Encumbrance
sections.text:
carrying capacity and encumbranceuse the character's strength score to find the carrying values below. the two blocks form one continuous table arranged side by side.
strengthunencumbered throughmaximum loadstrengthunencumbered throughmaximum load15 lb.10 lb.1487 lb.175 lb.210 lb.20 lb.15100 lb.200 lb.315 lb.30 lb.16115 lb.230 lb.420 lb.40 lb.17130 lb.260 lb.525 lb.50 lb.18150 lb.300 lb.630 lb.60 lb.19175 lb.350 lb.735 lb.70 lb.20200 lb.400 lb.840 lb.80 lb.21230 lb.460 lb.945 lb.90 lb.22260 lb.520 lb.1050 lb.100 lb.23300 lb.600 lb.1157 lb.115 lb.24350 lb.700 lb.1265 lb.130 lb.25400 lb.800 lb.1375 lb.150 lb.
a character carrying no more than unencumbered through suffers no load penalty. carrying more than that value makes the character encumbered. the character can carry up to maximum load while encumbered; above maximum load, the character cannot move normally while carrying the weight.

sections.title: Readily Accessible Equipment
sections.text:
readily accessible equipmenthalf the character's dexterity score, rounded down, is the practical guideline for how much equipment can be kept readily arranged on the body. treat this as a guideline, not an exact slot limit.
worn clothing and armor do not consume this capacity. weapons, component satchels, potion belts, packs, and comparable arranged equipment do. an ordinary item counts as at least one; a bulky or awkward item may count as two, three, or more at the dm's judgment and never counts as a fraction.
a suitable container counts according to its own bulk rather than making every small object inside it count separately. its contents are stored unless the container explicitly makes a particular item accessible. a backpack can count as more than one.

sections.title: Values Used in Combat
sections.text: values used in combatthis section is a map of the combat system. the later sections supply the complete procedures and exceptions.ability modifierthe modifier derived from an ability score. combat formulas use the modifier unless a rule explicitly calls for the full score or a roll-under ability check.main job and job leveleach job keeps its own level. the highest-level job is the main job; if several are tied, the one acquired first remains main. an ability tied to a particular job uses the level of the job that granted it.base attack bonus (bab)the character's core combat bonus. bab contributes to attack, dodge, parry, block, and many combat maneuvers.initiative1d20 + dexterity modifier + explicit initiative modifiers. initiative establishes the order in which combatants act.round and initiative passa round contains one or more sweeps through initiative order. the first sweep is the first initiative pass; later passes resolve additional attacks. spells complete at their scheduled initiative values.movement and main actionseparate allowances normally used on the first pass. a main action may be a single attack, full attack, spell, or another legal action.primary attackyour character's primary method of attacking. choose it when declaring a full attack; it supplies that full attack's ordinary attacks. unless stated otherwise, attack speed increases apply to the primary attack.attack speedthe number of attack passes supplied by the primary attack during a full attack. fractional speeds alternate between a higher and lower round, beginning every combat with the higher round.single attack and full attacka single attack uses the main action for one attack. when declaring a full attack, choose its primary attack and optional abilities; the resulting attacks form its schedule. the full attack spends 1 pe and ordinarily resolves no more than five attacks.attack and defensethe attacker rolls against the defender's declared dodge, parry, or block. the defender may instead use passive defense: 10 + bab + applicable passive magical defensive modifiers. the choice is made before either combat roll. an attack that meets or exceeds defense connects.margin of successattack - defense. a tied result hits with margin 0. a positive margin is added to damage.armor penetration (pen) and armor grade (grade)pen measures an attack's ability to defeat physical armor. grade measures how difficult that armor is to defeat. for armor with a grade, compare them to determine how much of its listed dr applies.damage reduction (dr)protection subtracted from damage before physical energy mitigation and before damage reaches hit points or life points.hit points (hp) and life points (lp)hp are one protective pool increased by jobs, training, worn armor, and other effects. temporary hp is separate only when its source says so. lp represent bodily survival. ordinary damage depletes hp before reaching lp.physical energy (pe) and magical energy (me)pe pays for strenuous physical options, including a full attack. me pays spell costs. neither pool may be spent for a purpose unless a rule permits it.

sections.title: The Combat Sequence
sections.text: the combat sequenceuse this sequence for an ordinary encounter:begin combat. a hostile action starts mechanical combat. the dm determines who is involved, who perceives the danger, and who is surprised or flat-footed.roll initiative. every current participant rolls initiative. a character drawn into combat during a round rolls to enter on the next round.resolve round 0 when needed. eligible aware creatures receive either movement or one main action that is not a full attack. if everyone expected the fight, begin with round 1 instead.establish current attack modifiers. apply any attack-speed changes that begin this round. when a character declares a full attack, choose its primary attack and optional additions, then establish that full attack's exact schedule.resolve the first initiative pass. act from highest initiative to lowest. each combatant may use movement and one main action, subject to conditions and other restrictions. a full attack costs 1 pe and begins its sequence of attacks. a maneuver may replace the main action or an attack only when its own procedure permits it.resolve each attack. declare the target and attack. the defender declares a legal active defense or passive defense. roll attack and any active defense, calculate margin of success on a hit, and calculate raw damage. compare pen with grade when the armor has a grade, apply the resulting dr and any flat dr, apply eligible pe mitigation, then route the remainder through hp and lp.resolve later passes. return to the top of initiative for combatants with unresolved full-attack passes. later passes normally grant no movement or unrestricted main action. resolve scheduled spell completions at their proper initiative values.end the round. after every attack pass and scheduled completion has resolved, apply anything timed for the end of a turn or round. begin the next round and advance any fractional attack speed schedule.

sections.title: Example: One Complete Ordinary Combat Round
sections.text: example: one complete ordinary combat rounda mercenary and a guard expect a fight, so there is no round 0. the mercenary has initiative 17, attack speed 1.5, strength modifier +3, and a medium 1d8 sword with pen 2. the guard has initiative 12, attack speed 1, a sword and shield, medium armor with grade 2, dr 2, and armor hp 6, and 8 hp before armor. the worn armor therefore raises the guard's maximum hp to 14.first pass, initiative 17. the mercenary moves 20 feet into reach, declares a full attack, and spends 1 pe. because this is the first round of combat, attack speed 1.5 provides two attack passes. the guard declares dodge before the dice are rolled.the mercenary's attack total is 24 and the guard's dodge is 20. the attack connects with margin 4. the sword rolls 5 damage, producing 5 + 3 strength + 4 margin = 12 raw damage. pen 2 equals grade 2, so the armor's normal dr 2 reduces this to 10. the damage reduces the guard's 14 hp to 4 hp. the armor hp is part of that same hp total rather than a separately tracked damage pool.first pass, initiative 12. the guard uses the main action for one attack. the mercenary declares parry. the guard's attack is 18 and the mercenary's parry is 21, so the attack misses.second pass, initiative 17. only the mercenary has another attack pass. no ordinary movement is available. the guard declares block. attack and block both total 20, so the attack connects with margin 0. the sword rolls 4, producing 4 + 3 strength + 0 margin = 7 raw damage. dr 2 reduces this to 5. the guard's remaining 4 hp are removed and the final 1 damage reaches lp.no other combatant has an attack pass or scheduled completion, so the round ends. in round 2, the lower side of the mercenary's attack speed 1.5 schedule provides one attack pass.

sections.title: Example: Mercenary and Swashbuckler Attack Speed
sections.text: example: mercenary and swashbuckler attack speedmercenary. a mercenary wielding a two-handed mastered weapon begins with attack speed 1. second attack raises it to 1.5, third attack raises it to 2, and weapon mastery iii raises it to 2.5. the mercenary therefore makes three attacks in the first round, two in the second, then repeats that cycle. every attack uses the two-handed primary attack.swashbuckler. a swashbuckler with dual wield makes one primary and one offhand attack in each paired pass. second attack grants a second paired pass, producing four attacks each round. at full greased lightning buildup, the swashbuckler gains one additional unpaired attack and reaches five attacks.

sections.title: Example: Spell Speed Across Initiative Counts
sections.text: example: spell speed across initiative countsa speed 3 spell begun at initiative 25 is scheduled for initiative 22. every ordinary action at 22 resolves first, then the spell completes at the end of that count. a speed 2 spell begun at initiative 24 also completes at the end of 22, so both spells resolve simultaneously. if a speed 30 spell begins at initiative 5, it completes at initiative -25 during the same round; passing initiative 0 does not move a numeric spell speed into the next round.
