sections.title: Example: Tracking Defense Uses
sections.text: example: tracking defense usesa bab +9 sword-and-shield fighter with enhanced parry begins the round with four penalty-free parries: one from the weapon and three from enhanced parry. the shield supplies one separate penalty-free block, and the fighter also has one penalty-free dodge. a fifth parry takes -4. before any attack, the fighter may choose passive defense instead and spend none of these uses.if the same fighter wields two suitable weapons instead, each weapon supplies one base parry and enhanced parry adds three more to the shared pool, producing five penalty-free parries rather than eight.

sections.title: Example: Ordinary Two-Weapon Fighting
sections.text: example: ordinary two-weapon fightinga character with primary attack speed 1.5 makes three primary attacks across two rounds. fighting with a second weapon adds one offhand attack during that cycle, producing two attacks in each round. if both weapons can parry, each also supplies one base parry use; the ordinary two-weapon penalty applies to both.

sections.title: Example: Cover and Concealment
sections.text: example: cover and concealmenta guard stands behind ordinary cover in thick smoke, gaining +4 defense from cover and a 20% concealment miss chance. against the first arrow, the guard commits block and adds the cover bonus. the arrow connects, but concealment negates it; the block use is still spent. against the next arrow, the guard trusts concealment instead, using passive defense with the +4 cover bonus. if the arrow connects and the miss chance fails, the guard cannot declare an active defense afterward.

sections.title: Damage Reduction, Armor Penetration, and Armor Grade
sections.text: damage reduction, armor penetration, and armor grade

sections.title: Example: Reading Pen and Grade
sections.text: example: reading pen and gradea medium weapon with pen 2 striking heavy armor with grade 3 and dr 9 is one point lower, so the armor applies dr 13: its normal 9 plus half of 9, rounded down to 4. a heavy weapon normally has pen 3; heavy attack raises it to pen 4, which applies half dr against heavy grade 3 armor and ignores the dr of medium grade 2 armor.

sections.title: Example: Damage from Attack Roll to Life Points
sections.text: example: damage from attack roll to life pointsan attack of 24 meets defense 20 with margin 4. the weapon rolls 8, then adds +4 strength, +4 explicit damage, and +4 margin for 20 raw damage. the weapon has pen 2 and the armor has grade 2 with listed dr 4. equal pen and grade leave that dr unchanged, reducing the damage to 16. the defender spends 4 pe to halve that result to 8. the defender has 2 temporary hp and 5 hp remaining, so the damage removes both temporary hp and all 5 hp; the final 1 point reaches lp. if the same final result were lethal damage, it would bypass both hp pools and remove 8 lp instead.

sections.title: Example: Critical Damage and Multiple Multipliers
sections.text: example: critical damage and multiple multiplierstwo ordinary x2 multipliers applied to the same value combine into x3, not x4. effects that change the number of weapon dice happen before a critical instead. a qualifying mounted charge changes a 1d8 weapon to 2d8; if those dice roll 11 on a critical hit, double that one rolled result to 22, then add +3 strength and +4 margin once for 29 damage. do not double the strength or margin.

sections.title: Example: Dividing an Odd Life Point Total
sections.text: example: dividing an odd life point totala character with maximum lp 17 assigns 9 points to light, leaving 8. those remaining points divide evenly into 4 serious and 4 critical. the exact bands are therefore light at 17 through 9 lp, serious at 8 through 5, and critical at 4 through 1. at 4 lp the character takes the total -4 wound penalty, cannot run, and loses 0.5 primary attack speed; an attack speed of 1 remains 1 because it cannot fall below the general minimum.

sections.title: Preventing a Mortal Wound with Physical Energy
sections.text: preventing a mortal wound with physical energy

sections.title: Example: Entering Negative LP and Preventing a Mortal Wound
sections.text: example: entering negative lp and preventing a mortal wounda constitution 18 character at 8 lp takes 12 actual lp damage from one attack. the attack would leave them at -4 and satisfies both entry into negative lp and the greater-than-half-maximum-lp trigger, but one source can cause no more than one mortal wound. if the character can spend 5 pe before becoming unconscious, they instead fall to -1 lp and receive no mortal wound.if the same character begins at 18 lp and loses 10 lp from one attack, they remain at 8 lp but have lost more than half their maximum. if the dm applies a mortal wound, spending 5 pe prevents that wound without restoring the 10 lp. no 5-pe response can save the character from damage that has already carried them to -10 lp, one point below their survivable boundary.

sections.title: Casting a Spell and Paying Magical Energy
sections.text: casting a spell and paying magical energy

sections.title: Example: Combat Casting Through Multiple Passes
sections.text: example: combat casting through multiple passesa caster chooses a one-handed melee weapon whose current attack speed is 3. they move into melee before beginning the sequence, then use the first pass to cast, paying 4 pe plus the spell's me cost. the second and third passes may each make one attack with that weapon. do not add the ordinary 1-pe full attack cost. if a hit during the casting interval is reduced to 0 actual damage by dr or pe mitigation, it does not interrupt; if at least 1 actual damage remains, the caster must pass the half-wisdom preservation roll.

sections.title: Example: Opposed Roll-Under Margins
sections.text: example: opposed roll-under marginsan attacker with adjusted threshold 20 rolls 23, producing check margin -3. the defender with threshold 18 rolls 20, producing margin -2. both missed their thresholds, but -2 is the higher and therefore less severe failure, so the defender wins. if both margins had been -2, the defender would also win because opposed ties favor the defender.

sections.title: Example: Paying for a Heavy Attack
sections.text: example: paying for a heavy attacka character beginning the round with three attacks may attack normally on the first pass, then declare heavy attack on the second. that one heavy attack consumes both remaining attacks and is rolled at -2 attack. a 2d6 heavy weapon becomes 4d6; if the dice total 15, strength is +4, and the ordinary margin is 3, heavy attack raises the effective margin to 7 for 26 raw damage. the weapon's pen 3 becomes pen 4. against heavy armor with grade 3 and listed dr 9, this applies half dr, rounded down to 4, leaving 22 damage before pe mitigation and hp.a character who began with only one attack may instead make the heavy attack at initiative 0 with -5 attack. a character who began with two attacks must use heavy attack on the first pass.

sections.title: Example: Establishing Grapple Control
sections.text: example: establishing grapple controlan unarmed character uses normal grab against a ready spearman. normal grab applies -2 attack, weapon edge adds another -4, and the spearman receives the special free attack. the free attack hits, but after applicable dr its final damage is 0, so the grab continues. the adjusted grab attack is 21 against dodge 18 and connects.the attacker then checks strength score + bab with threshold 24 and rolls 10, giving margin 14. the defender has threshold 20 and rolls 9, giving margin 11. the attacker wins and becomes the controller. improved grapple against a defender without weapon edge would remove the normal grab penalty and special free attack, replace one attack, and cost 1 pe in addition to any full attack cost.

sections.title: Example: Maintaining Grapple, Pin, and Choke
sections.text: example: maintaining grapple, pin, and chokea character with attack speed 3 begins a full attack and spends 1 pe. the first pass uses improved grapple, costing another 1 pe and establishing control. the second pass successfully establishes pin; the third establishes choke. establishing pin and choke requires two separate attacks.in the next round, spending one attack to continue choke also maintains pin and the underlying grapple. at the end of the target's turn, they make the first fortitude save with no elapsed-time penalty. if choke continues, the next save is at -4 and the third is at -8. suppose the target fails the second save: they become unconscious. if released, they wake in 1d4 rounds unless something else prevents it. if choke continues, the target's next turn is the grace round with no lp loss; the first 1 lp is lost at the end of the following turn.a controller who intends to use only the one attack required to maintain choke need not declare a full attack. to maintain the hold and use later attack passes for additional strikes or other grapple options, the controller declares a full attack and pays its ordinary 1 pe.

sections.title: Outside Attacks, Area Effects, and Spellcasting
sections.text: outside attacks, area effects, and spellcasting

sections.title: Example: Attacking Someone in a Grapple
sections.text: example: attacking someone in a grapplean archer targets the controller, whose grapple defense is 15. the controller maintains control; the archer's attack 19 connects with margin 4, then a 50/50 roll determines whether the controller or grappled target receives that same hit, margin, and damage. if the controller releases before the attack, the archer instead attacks the declared target normally and no 50/50 roll occurs. a fireball or another area effect affects both participants and never uses the 50/50 procedure.

sections.title: Example: Mounted Ranged Combat
sections.text: example: mounted ranged combata rider with mounted combat may let the mount use ordinary movement and then make one ranged attack at no movement penalty, but cannot make a ranged full attack. a mounted archer with attack speed 2.5 on the high side of the schedule may finish a double movement, spend 1 pe, and then make three ranged attacks at -2 each. a ride-only rider cannot make a ranged attack during a round in which the mount runs.

sections.title: Example: Firing and Reloading a Mounted Crossbow
sections.text: example: firing and reloading a mounted crossbowa rider may fire an already-loaded crossbow as their permitted ranged attack. reloading it on a later round consumes the main action and prevents attacking or casting. the mount may move before or after the reload, but must be stopped while the crossbow is actually being reloaded.

sections.title: Example: Combat Unit Formation and Defense
sections.text: example: combat unit formation and defenseformation example. a twenty-member veteran warrior unit has bab 6 and a +3 ability modifier, giving it a +9 representative attack before equipment. its melee formation bonus is +10. five contributors produce 3 impact and +4 contribution, so it attacks at +23 before the d20. if it rolls 12, its total attack is 35. against defense 31, all 3 impact remain and its positive attack margin is 4. with 1d8 + 3 weapons, the combined damage is 3d8 + 3 + 4. if those weapons have pen 2 and the target has grade 2 armor with dr 4, equal pen and grade leave dr 4 unchanged; subtract it once from the combined result, not once per impact.if the defense were instead 40, meeting attack would remove 1 impact and the first full 4 points within its defensive margin of 5 would remove 1 more. the remaining 1 impact would deal 1d8 + 3: meeting the aggregate attack always removes the first impact, and every additional full 4 points removes another.successful dodge example. twenty archers focus on aslan, producing 10 impact. their total attack is 20 and aslan's dodge is 28. meeting attack removes 1 impact, and his defensive margin of 8 removes 2 more, leaving 7, so the successful dodge still leaves damage to resolve. their 1d8 bows produce a combined 7d8 damage-dice expression, which becomes 4d8 + 6 before the roll. add the representative fixed damage modifier once, and add no attack margin because their attack did not exceed his defense. compare the representative bow's pen with aslan's grade once, then apply his resulting grade-sensitive and flat dr once to that combined damage. this is seven weapon-dice sets combined into one converted damage result, not seven copies of one archer's complete damage total.

sections.title: Life Point Recovery and Long-Term Care
sections.text: life point recovery and long-term care

sections.title: Example: One Shared Cure Pool
sections.text: example: one shared cure poolcure serious wounds rolls 9 for a living recipient at full hp and 9/12 lp in the light band. spend 3 points to restore the recipient to 12/12 lp; the remaining 6 points are unused.if a cure spell instead rolls 9 for a recipient missing 4 hp and 7 eligible lp, it could restore 4 hp and 5 lp, 2 hp and 7 lp, or another legal combination totaling no more than 9. it cannot restore 9 hp and then also restore lp from a second copy of the roll.

sections.title: Example: Recovering Through Multiple Wound Bands
sections.text: example: recovering through multiple wound bandsa character with maximum lp 15 and constitution modifier +2 begins at -1 lp under sustained competent care. after seven days they recover to 1 lp and wake. seven days later they reach 3 lp, and after another seven days they reach 5 lp and enter the serious band. their faster serious rate now applies: three days later they reach 7, and three days after that they reach 9 and enter light. the light rate then applies, restoring another 2 lp after one day of care.cure critical wounds is required while the character is at -1 through 3 lp. cure serious wounds or cure critical wounds can heal them at 5 through 7, and any cure tier can heal them after they reach the light band at 9 lp.

sections.title: Example: Spending TCP and LCP
sections.text: example: spending tcp and lcpa knowledge (tactics) check with margin 8 generates 3 tcp for the shared combat pool. with the leader's approval, one ally spends 1 tcp before a defense roll to gain +2 defense; that ally cannot receive another command-point benefit during the same round. later, the leader spends their main action and makes a command (leadership) check with margin 4, generating 2 lcp. during that same leader turn, both lcp are assigned to a different ally for one immediate main action. it may be one attack, a spell, or an item use, but never a full attack. any unspent lcp expire at the end of that round.

sections.title: Example: Strength 18B Against C-Ranked Opposition
sections.text: example: strength 18b against c-ranked oppositiona dragon has strength 18b. its opponent has strength 24c. the opponent has the higher raw strength score, but the dragon's strength operates one rank higher.for a direct opposed strength check, the dragon receives the one-rank +10. in a pure roll-under contest, its adjusted threshold is 18 + 10 = 28, while the opponent's threshold remains 24. any bab, size, equipment, or situational modifiers required by the particular maneuver are then applied normally, and both sides compare check margins.if the dragon rolls 12, its check margin is 28 - 12 = 16. if the opponent rolls 10, their check margin is 24 - 10 = 14; the dragon wins by 2. the c-ranked opponent can still win with a sufficiently better roll because a one-rank gap remains contestable.for a weapon attack, compare the dragon's b-ranked strength offense with the rank governing the opponent's chosen defense. if the opponent dodges with c-ranked dexterity, the dragon adds +10 to its strength-based attack and, if the attack connects, adds +10 directly to damage. suppose the dragon's ordinary attack total is 22 and the opponent's defense is 20. rank raises the attack to 32, producing margin 12. the raw damage calculation then uses the weapon dice, the dragon's unchanged ordinary strength modifier, margin 12, and the direct +10 rank bonus. protection resolves normally afterward.the +10 attack contribution has already flowed into margin and is not added to margin again. the separate +10 damage contribution is nevertheless applied because strength governs the damage formula as well. if the opponent instead used a b-ranked defense, the ranks would be equal and neither rank modifier would apply.the notation never turns the dragon's strength score into 28, changes its attribute maximum, or produces a new strength modifier. strength remains 18 for every ordinary calculation; +10 is the independent effect of the one-rank gap. against d-ranked opposition, a b-ranked strength offense receives +40 in each independently resolved relevant formula instead.

sections.title: 1. Magic and Spellcasting at a Glance
sections.text: 1. magic and spellcasting at a glancemagic is not what it was. in the first age, words of power could reshape reality and set cities ablaze. centuries of use, study, and rationalization have worn those workings into smaller, repeatable forms. the spell now called fireball is one surviving shadow. modern spells are teachable and dependable—magics sufficiently accepted by the world to function almost mundanely—and their reliability marks how much they have lost.a spellcaster learns individual spells, spends magical energy (me) to cast them, and uses caster level to determine their power. vanaheim has no daily preparation of spell slots: a learned spell remains known and can be cast whenever the character meets its requirements and can pay its cost.the core spellcasting jobs approach magic through different traditions:jobtradition and accesspriestdivine magic from a faith-modified priest list; casting requires high follower standing.shamanspirit magic from the shaman list; casting requires the spirit relationship that permits the job.paladindivine magic from the choosing god's paladin list; casting requires that god's continuing favor.helliondivine magic from the patron imperial faith's hellion list; casting requires high follower standing.sorcererinnate sorcery from the sorcerer list.warlockinnate or inherited elementalism from the warlock list.necromancerrestricted abyssal necromancy from the necromancer list, including preserved legacy spells where classes permits them.each character has one shared me pool even when several jobs grant spellcasting. bard performances are magical talents rather than spells and do not use this chapter's ordinary spellcasting procedure.ordinary necromancer spells use the same casting procedure as other spells, although their source and magical interactions are necromantic. true necromancy is the separate freeform practice owned by the necromancer profile in classes; it is not an ordinary spell-circle procedure and is not expanded here.the basic procedure is:confirm that the spell is known, currently castable, and within the character's spell-circle limit.confirm its target or area, components, me cost, and required free concentration.use the main action, pay me, and begin casting. resolve armor spell failure when applicable.complete the spell after its spell speed.resolve mr, protective spells, any saving throw, the spell's effect, and applicable protection in the order given under resolving a spell.combat supplies the detailed initiative, interruption, defensive casting, combat casting, and damage-routing procedures. individual spells state their own targets, ranges, areas, durations, components, saving throws, and exceptions.

sections.title: 2. Spellcasters and Spell Circles
sections.text:
2. spellcasters and spell circlescaster levelunless a job, spell, or ability states otherwise, ordinary caster level is:caster level = half the relevant caster job level, rounded downa level-5 sorcerer therefore has caster level 2, and a level-30 or level-31 caster job has ordinary caster level 15. a character with more than one caster job calculates each spell from the job that grants that spell; caster job levels are not added together.caster level is not ordinarily purchased and is not the same as spell-circle access. spellcasting mastery is the explicit grandmaster exception: add the number of spellcasting mastery entries recorded for the casting job. when one known spell is available through several jobs, name the casting job before paying me and use only that job's access and caster level. spellcasting mastery never grants a spell circle, spell eligibility, or spell knowledge.caster level commonly determines damage, duration, range, checks, and other values named by a spell. see classes — caster level for the shared job calculation. the complete spellcasting mastery advancement procedure appears in gm and beyond.
    spell circlesspell circles measure the complexity of spells from first through ninth circle. job level determines the highest circle available through that job, while the character's intelligence must also support that circle.spell circleminimum intelligence111212313414515616717818919
    if intelligence falls below the minimum, the character cannot cast that circle until intelligence recovers. recalculate concentration capacity at the same time and end enough maintained spells to fit the reduced capacity.priest, shaman, sorcerer, warlock, and necromancer can eventually reach ninth-circle access. paladin and hellion use six-circle schedules. the exact job-level thresholds and any religious, spiritual, or restricted-job gates remain in each classes profile.spell eligibility and spell knowledgecircle access grants permission to learn appropriate spells; it teaches none automatically. a spell must belong to the character's actual class eligibility or be granted by another explicit rule.public spell lists are intentionally incomplete. a secret spell may belong to one or more classes without appearing on a public list. its actual class eligibility controls who may learn it. seeing, identifying, or possessing another class's spell does not by itself grant access.

pages.title: Foreword
pages.text: vanaheimforeword03core rulebook · forewordforewordtime alters all. it permeates through everything without reverence, ultimately destroying even the most fundamental bindings created by fate and destiny itself. the logical becomes irrational, the familiar uncanny, the matter-of-fact, wrong.you may have felt this, as you grew to know your parents as flawed men, as you watched them slowly decay and die; as your birthplace was changed- ravaged by war or the stupidity of its residents.you may have even seen it as the world changed, time and time again; and yet eerily, remains the same. as if some unseen hand, desperately trying to gather all the infinitely miniscule specs of sand, to pour them back into a shattered hourglass.but even that is not enough. nothing is.time alters all- there is no end, only change. relentless, merciless change towards the unknown, the uncanny, the preposterous and the obscene.vie against it as you like, support it even, ye disillusioned fools. eventually you will see time for what it really is.immortality. a fate far worse than death.

    attribute scores and modifiers
a character has six ordinary attributes: strength, dexterity, constitution, intelligence, wisdom, and charisma. each has an attribute score and an ability modifier.
the full attribute score measures the character's raw capacity. when a rule calls for an attribute check, roll d20; a result equal to or lower than the score after bonuses and penalties succeeds. most other rules use the ability modifier shown in the table.

a score of 25 receives the modifier that 26 would ordinarily provide. scores above 25 return to the normal progression: 26-27 is +8, 28-29 is +9, and 30-31 is +10. such values require an explicit extraordinary source and are not part of ordinary character generation.
every final ordinary player attribute must be at least 5. luck follows its separate generation rule and may receive a lower result. racial maximum, including any prime-attribute increase, limits normal permanent advancement. a specific magical or extraordinary effect may explicitly allow you to exceed it.what the attributes represent



attribute
meaning and principal uses



strength (str)
physical power and leverage. it governs ordinary melee attacks and damage, block, carrying capacity, and many physical maneuvers.


dexterity (dex)
agility, coordination, reaction speed, and physical precision. it governs initiative, ordinary ranged attacks, dodge, reflex saves, ride, and readily accessible equipment.


constitution (con)
health, endurance, recovery, and resistance to bodily harm. it determines base life points and contributes to physical energy, fortitude, running endurance, wound survival, and recovery.


intelligence (int)
learning, reasoning, disciplined concentration, and aptitude for acquiring skills. it governs spell concentration capacity and defensive casting and helps determine additional starting skill choices.


wisdom (wis)
judgment, awareness, magical reserve, and force of will. it governs will saves, the amount of magical energy granted by wisdom, magical energy recovery, and certain spell-preservation checks.


charisma (cha)
presence, expression, and force of personality. it governs social skills and the default difficulty classes of spells and abilities.


these are the attributes' principal uses. a skill, class, spell, talent, or other specific rule may use an attribute in another appropriate way.05character creation · attributes and ability modifiers

pages.title: Luck and Sanity
pages.text:
character creationluck and sanityluck and sanityluck. luck is generated alongside the six ordinary attributes. assign one of the character's seven generated results to luck. luck has no racial modifier, cannot be a prime attribute, and produces no ability modifier. its maximum is 18, or 19 when its generation roll showed four 6s.
luck measures favorable or unfavorable uncertainty. when the dm calls for a luck check, roll d20 equal to or below the adjusted luck score. bonuses raise the effective threshold and penalties lower it. luck may determine whether a misplaced item is found, whether a plausible improvised tool is nearby, whether an appropriately trained character can locate a possible environmental resource, or which of several reasonable encounter circumstances occurs. it cannot create something impossible or replace relevant knowledge and training. failure may establish an unfavorable circumstance.
luck also provides a small reserve of character-saving rerolls:



luck score
luck rerolls per story arc



15 or lower
0


16-17
1


18
2


19
3


the dm decides when a new story arc begins and these uses refresh. a story arc may span a substantial period of play; luck does not refresh each session, day, or encounter.
after seeing the result of one of your own d20 rolls, spend one luck reroll to roll it again and keep whichever result is more favorable. if advantage or disadvantage applied, reroll one chosen die, resolve the revised roll, and keep the more favorable complete result. before making a disadvantaged roll, you may instead spend one use to cancel the remaining disadvantage and roll one ordinary d20. damage dice and other non-d20 rolls are not normally eligible, but the dm may permit an exception when the requested intervention is genuinely a matter of luck. luck has no other universal benefit.sanity score and current sanity. sanity is not generated or assigned and produces no ability modifier. every new character begins with a sanity score of 18 and current sanity 18.
sanity score is the permanent measure of the character's connection to ordinary reality, what they regard as normal, and how much horror or hardship they have absorbed. it sets maximum current sanity. current sanity is a separate hp-like pool that receives sanity damage. ordinary sanity damage reduces current sanity without reducing the permanent score.
severe experiences can permanently lower sanity score, representing both lasting damage and hardening. when this happens, maximum current sanity falls with it. if current sanity exceeds the new maximum, reduce it to that maximum; otherwise leave it unchanged. a character whose sanity score falls from 18 to 14 while at current sanity 12 remains at 12. one who was at current sanity 16 falls to 14.
lower sanity can make a character less vulnerable to familiar bloodshed, death, filth, and hardship, while making them increasingly alienated from ordinary society. high sanity is therefore not simply better than low sanity.
18: the ordinary starting point: a broadly normal upbringing without close participation in killing, murder, disease, or extreme conditions.
17-16: meaningful hardship without losing ordinary social function. violent bereavement or living through a damaged city may fall here.
15-14: substantial direct exposure to war, killing, blood, filth, lost comrades, or repulsive acts committed to survive.
around 12: hardening is visible in habits and outlook. self-care or possessions may be neglected, tics may emerge, and the character has reconciled themselves to conclusions that more sheltered people would reject.
10 or lower: the character is becoming genuinely dysfunctional in ordinary society, and other people can readily perceive that something is deeply wrong.
8-7: the character normally approaches or crosses the boundary of playability because severe trauma-driven or socially incompatible behavior prevents ordinary social function.
these values are interpretive anchors, not mandatory biographies or automatic behavior packages.06character creation · luck and sanity

pages.title: Sanity Shocked and Recovery
pages.text:
character creationluck and sanityluck and sanity · continuedsanity checks and damage. the dm may call for a sanity check when an event meaningfully defies the character's understanding of reality or exceeds what their history has normalized. the dm gives the event an implicit qualitative sanity threshold. if the character's sanity score is equal to or below that threshold, the character is sufficiently hardened and makes no check. a lower threshold represents a more extreme event because it can affect more heavily hardened characters.
if a check is required, roll d20. the character must roll higher than their sanity score to remain unaffected. failure inflicts sanity damage and reduces current sanity. this unusual roll deliberately makes high-sanity characters more sensitive once an event qualifies, while hardened characters are less likely to react to familiar mundane horror.
sanity damage has no fixed severity table. the dm considers the event, its implicit threshold, the character's sanity score and history, the distance between that score and the threshold, and the surrounding circumstances. mild shock commonly inflicts 1d6 sanity damage, moderate shock commonly inflicts 1d10, and severe or overwhelming shock may inflict several dice or another appropriate amount.recovery. current sanity recovers through genuinely calming, grounding, reassuring, or pleasurable experiences appropriate to the character. gambling, visiting a brothel, resting beside a river, wandering open plains, or watching the sun rise after a horrific night may all help, usually restoring 1d6 sanity. one ordinary night's rest does not automatically refill current sanity. long periods of safe downtime generally restore it fully, while a dungeon expedition, military campaign, or other sustained crisis does not. abilities and divine effects may also restore current sanity, especially when they remove or reframe the cause of the horror. exact recovery remains contextual and dm-adjudicated. as an example, the dm may assign xd6 sanity 'healing' when a character has had a good chance to recover, or full when they've had a good, long break from stressful circumstances/adventuring. sanity shocked. when current sanity reaches 0, the character becomes sanity shocked and rolls d20 equal to or below half their sanity score.on success, the character becomes resolute for the remainder of the encounter or approximately one hour, whichever better fits the situation. resolute fully restores current sanity, grants +4 to appropriateactions, and restores 1d10 current sanity to the character's team each turn when the character acts inspirationally.on failure, the player or dm selects a fitting reaction: paranoid, fearful, selfish, hopeless, irrational, or abusive. the reaction guides portrayal rather than imposing an absolute script. whenever the character attempts an action in this state, the dm rolls d100. on 1-49, the character acts normally. on 50-100, the dm determines an appropriate altered action or the character accomplishes nothing useful, perhaps freezing, cackling, mumbling incoherently, or staring in terror.sanity shocked and recovery
a character who fails to become resolute remains sanity shocked for the stressful scene, as defined by the dm. continuing danger may extend this across several encounters.
a calm interval—perhaps ten minutes spent settling down—can suspend the reaction and its action restrictions. this does not restore current sanity. while current sanity remains at 0 or below, the character can act normally until another sanity check is required or the dm judges renewed stress sufficient to reactivate the effects.unhinged. sanity damage can continue below 0. when accumulated damage reaches twice the sanity score—so current sanity has reached the negative of that score—the character becomes unhinged and passes to dm control. an unhinged character may act self-destructively or irrationally, or may cease meaningful action entirely.
the jaded feat can protect a sufficiently hardened character from sanity checks and fear tests caused by mundane death, ordinary violence, or most monstrous abominations. exceptional terrors of the abyss still apply. its prerequisites, price, and complete procedure appear in talents and feats.07character creation · luck and sanity · continued

generate three complete arrays, each containing seven results. generate every result as follows:
roll 4d6.
if one or more dice show 1, choose one of those dice and reroll it once. keep the new result even if it is another 1. do not reroll any other dice showing 1.
drop the lowest die and total the other three.
if all four dice show 6, the result is 19 rather than 18.
repeat this procedure until the array contains seven results, then generate two more complete arrays in the same way.choose and assign one array
choose one of the three complete arrays and discard the other two. results cannot be exchanged or combined between arrays.
assign the chosen array's seven results freely among strength, dexterity, constitution, intelligence, wisdom, charisma, and luck. sanity is not assigned; it begins at 18.apply racial modifiers and maximums
after assigning the array, choose a race from the next section and apply its adjustments. each racial profile lists the maximum a member of that race can normally reach in each attribute. the same number determines the character's starting adjustment: subtract 20 from the listed maximum.
a listed maximum of 22 adds +2 to the assigned result.
a listed maximum of 19 applies -1 to the assigned result.
a listed maximum of 20 makes no change.
a human also chooses one prime attribute from strength, dexterity, constitution, intelligence, wisdom, or charisma. add +3 to both its starting value and permanent maximum. a half-elf chooses one prime attribute in the same way and adds +1 instead. luck and sanity cannot be prime attributes.
apply adjustments in this order: assign the generated result, apply the racial adjustment, then apply any prime-attribute increase. every resulting attribute must be at least 5. try another assignment or another generated array if one falls below 5. if none of the three arrays can keep every attribute at 5 or higher, generate three new arrays.
the racial maximum prevents ordinary permanent advancement beyond it. a miracle, wish, or similarly extraordinary effect may explicitly exceed that maximum.
    example: racial adjustment and prime attribute
a half-elf assigns 18 to dexterity. the half-elf dexterity maximum is 22, so the racial adjustment adds +2. if dexterity is also chosen as the character's prime attribute, add another +1 to its starting value and maximum. the character begins with dexterity 21 and has a permanent dexterity maximum of 23.08character creation · generate and assign attributes

humans are vanaheim's most adaptable people. their nations and traditions differ enormously, and humans can master almost any calling. their defining strength is the speed with which they learn, specialize, and advance.

half-elves combine human adaptability with elven longevity. they ordinarily mature near a human pace until roughly age 35 to 40, after which aging slows dramatically. no one can reliably predict a half-elf's lifespan: some live for centuries, some for far longer, and some may be immortal. near the final portion of life, the skin begins to harden and crack like bark and the hair loses color, though the half-elf rarely develops the frail appearance of a very old human.

pages.title: Elf · Dwarf
pages.text:
character creationraces · elf and dwarfelf
the shared elf profile covers sylvar, pyran, and common elves. sylvar are the oldest and most otherworldly elven people; pyran are protective forest-dwellers shaped by long contact with humanity; common elves descend from pyran communities that lived among humans for generations. elves are immortal in lifespan but can be killed. they retain a young-adult appearance rather than becoming visibly elderly, and chronological age need not match apparent age.
an elf player character must have a good alignment.
gain sneak, low-light vision, racial detect magic, elven reverie and sleep immunity, mana well, and cold-iron weakness.
an ordinary elf has speed 30 feet. a pyran elf instead has speed 35 feet. unless another rule says otherwise, sylvar, pyran, and common elves share the same racial traits.
sneak (talent): an elf with sneak automatically succeeds on stealth checks against creatures that are not actively on guard, provided the elf remains outside their immediate line of sight. if the elf also possesses the hide talent, hide grants +10 on stealth while perfectly still in a place where hiding is physically possible; sneak allows the elf to move while retaining that bonus so long as concealment still permits stealth. detect invisibility reveals an elf using hide.
low-light vision: in dim light, double the distance at which the elf can see, to a maximum of 200 feet and never farther than the same scene could be seen in daylight. low-light vision provides no sight in total darkness.
racial detect magic: the elf can invoke the detect magic spell by concentrating. invoking it costs the same me and uses the same spell speed, concentration rules, and effect as the spell, but requires no verbal, somatic, or material components.
elven reverie and sleep immunity: elves are immune to mundane and magical sleep. instead of sleeping, an elf spends four hours in quiet elven reverie, recalling memories without dreaming. reverie satisfies the need for sleep and refreshes mana well; it does not prevent fatigue, exhaustion, or unconsciousness from another cause. recovering me, hp, pe, and physical fatigue still requires the full rest period specified by those rules; the four hours of reverie may occur within it.mana well: every sylvar, pyran, and common elf represented by this profile possesses mana well from level 1, though it first becomes usable when one of the elf's jobs reaches level 10. dark elves are safe recipients but do not possess mana well. use the elf's highest job level for this ability; if several jobs are tied, use the one acquired first.
the elf gains one use at level 10, a second at level 20, and another every ten levels thereafter. activating a use is a main action.
each use restores me equal to half that job level, rounded down, up to the recipient's maximum. at level 10 it restores 5 me once; at level 14 it restores 7 me once; at level 20 it restores 10 me and can be used twice.
the elf may restore their own me or touch another creature to transfer the same amount. completing four hours of elven reverie restores all spent uses, no more than once per 24 hours.
elves, including dark elves, and sprites / fae can receive this transfer safely. every other race makes a will save when receiving it: dc 15 for the first transfer, increasing permanently by 1 with every later transfer to that recipient, regardless of the donor or the result of earlier saves. failure causes addiction to elves and their mana well energy; the dm adjudicates the consequences.
cold-iron weakness: elves are vulnerable to cold iron. after applicable protection reduces a cold-iron attack's damage, add half the remaining damage, rounding down, before physical energy mitigation. if protection reduces the damage to 0, the weakness creates no damage.dwarf
dwarves are broad-built, long-lived people renowned for metalwork, stonecraft, and engineering. wars with the dark elves shattered most of their ancient underground realms, leaving relatively few free communities on the surface or beneath it; vaelrain remains one of the surviving free underground settlements. dwarves commonly live for approximately 300 to 400 years.
a dwarf is medium and has speed 30 feet.
gain infravision.
infravision: the dwarf perceives heat patterns within 60 feet, including in darkness. infravision does not reveal cold detail that produces no meaningful temperature contrast.10character creation · races · elf and dwarf

character creationraces · choose a starting jobsprite
sprites are ageless magical beings whose maximum me is also their life force. outside a place with sufficiently abundant ambient magic, each sprite people loses maximum me at the rate stated by its profile. a sprite dies if its maximum me reaches 0; its animating being and soul are gone rather than merely resting or unconscious.
low-light vision: in dim light, double the distance at which the sprite can see, to a maximum of 200 feet and never farther than the same scene could be seen in daylight. low-light vision provides no sight in total darkness.
racial detect magic: the sprite can invoke the detect magic spell by concentrating. invoking it costs the same me and uses the same spell speed, concentration rules, and effect as the spell, but requires no verbal, somatic, or material components.
cold-iron weakness: sprites are vulnerable to cold iron. after applicable protection reduces a cold-iron attack's damage, add half the remaining damage, rounding down, before physical energy mitigation. if protection reduces the damage to 0, the weakness creates no damage.
sand runners: sand runners remain npc-only in the current core rules. they are medium, human-sized sprites with subtly different eyes, slightly sharper teeth, and wings that fold beneath clothing. a sand runner outside sufficiently abundant magic loses 1 maximum me per month. returning to abundant magic allows that loss to recover, but the creature profile or dm determines the rate. use the sand runner's creature profile for its land speed, flying speed, and other abilities.giant
giants retain their large build and speed 30 feet. a giant's creature profile lists any exceptional abilities it possesses, such as bash, enhanced damage, or boulder.
    choose a starting jobchoose one starting job
choose one job from classes whose entry requirements the character satisfies. the character begins at job level 1 and overall level 1 with no unspent xp. restricted jobs require the permission stated in their profiles.
apply everything explicitly granted by the job's starting package and its other level-1 features. a rank or talent-access list shows what the character may learn or purchase. entries on that list are not gained automatically unless the job says otherwise.
if the starting job belongs to the acolyte family, choose its permanent hp, me, or balanced progression now. if a human's starting job belongs to the mage family, add the human's +5 me after applying the ordinary mage level-1 me gain.starting skills and languages
every character begins fluent in one regional language associated with where the character was raised. the regional languages used for character creation are ayamaoan, taslamaran, uxmaln, zhenshi, aghelian, and imperial. vanaheim has no universal common language.
an elf also begins fluent in sylvan.
a dwarf also begins fluent in deep tongue.
a sprite also begins fluent in sylvan, though sprites remain npc-only in the current core rules.
a character whose starting job belongs to the mage family also begins fluent in arcane.
these granted languages are trained knowledge (language: specific language) fields and use no starting skill choices. every additional language is learned as a separate knowledge (language: specific language) skill and uses one starting skill choice unless another rule grants it. learning a special language during creation requires dm permission and appropriate access.
after recording the granted languages, choose starting skills in this order:
choose three skills appropriate to the training of the starting job, subject to dm approval.
add unrestricted skill choices equal to the character's positive permanent intelligence modifier after racial and prime-attribute adjustments. a modifier of +0 or lower adds no choices and never removes any of the three job-based choices.
a human adds one further unrestricted skill choice.
skills cannot be purchased twice. every separately named craft, knowledge, performance, or profession field is a different skill. these choices grant trained skills, not skill masteries, and acquiring another job later does not re-grant them. a character may spend an eligible choice on an additional language as described above.12character creation · races · starting job

pages.text: classesclasses and jobs14classes · classes and jobsclassesunderstanding classes and jobsclass familiesthe four ordinary class families are warrior, adventurer, acolyte, and mage. a family groups jobs that share a broad advancement chassis and occupies one of the four ordinary family positions available to a character.jobsa job is a level-bearing class within one class family. each job has its own level, unlock track, job features, talent access, and any spell access printed in its profile.the current core jobs are:class familycurrent jobswarriormercenary, swashbuckler, barbarianadventurerscout, rogue, bardacolytepriest, shaman, paladin, hellionmagesorcerer, warlock, necromancer (restricted; dm permission)this is the current core-book roster. necromancer is included so readers can understand the path, but it is not an ordinary starting choice. the roster does not claim that no other training exists in the setting.training beyond the core jobssome organizations and traditions teach level-bearing paths beyond the thirteen core jobs. those paths belong to the separate gm and beyond expansion; their individual requirements, progression, and interactions remain outside this core chapter.talent access and exclusive talentsevery named entry in a job's rank table is a talent, even when its name resembles an ordinary competency. a talent may call for, modify, replace, or automatically resolve a skill check, but that interaction does not turn the talent  into an ordinary skill. skills are governed separately by the skills rules.a character may learn a class talent only when one of their jobs lists that talent, the talent explicitly lists their job or class family as eligible, or another explicit rule grants access. training supplies the method of learning an eligible talent; it does not grant access by itself.an exclusive talent may be learned only through its named job unless an explicit rule says otherwise. exclusive controls who may learn a talent. it is separate from class mastery, which controls whether a signature combat engine can operate alongside one learned from another job.class masteriesa class mastery is a job's signature combat engine. a character can know class masteries from several jobs but may use only one during a round.

pages.title: Page 15
pages.text: classesclasses and jobs15classes · classes and jobsa class mastery is available when the character knows it and the current circumstances allow it to affect a roll or action. the round's choice locks immediately before the first such roll or action. if only one mastery is available, it locks automatically; if several are available, choose one. if the first relevant event is a defense before the character's turn, lock or choose the mastery before that defense roll. a mastery that becomes available later cannot replace the round's locked choice.the choice governs the entire round. apply the chosen package completely, including every applicable benefit, cost, requirement, limitation, penalty, movement permission, attack speed effect, duration rule, and ending consequence. other class masteries provide no benefit during that round. an unchosen continuing mastery supplies no benefits, but its existing costs, penalties, conditions, and other consequences remain.only explicitly tagged class-mastery abilities compete for this choice. ordinary job features, feats, spells, equipment, positioning bonuses, and untagged talents continue to function normally unless their own rules say otherwise. choosing another mastery never removes a cost, penalty, condition, or other consequence already created by an earlier activation.jobcurrent class mastery packagemercenaryclass mastery: mercenary — weapon mastery and the benefits explicitly granted by that line.swashbucklerclass mastery: swashbuckler — greased lightning and its complete engine; wolverine stance and tornado slash when separately learned and applicable. ordinary dual wield remains separate and untagged.barbarianclass mastery: barbarian — berserk and fury, including wild fighting while separately learned and applicable.scoutclass mastery: scout — ranged mastery, rapid fire, and ambush. these abilities may work together when separately learned and applicable.rogueclass mastery: rogue — sneak attack, backstab, hamstring, and dual backstab. these abilities may work together when separately learned and applicable.bardclass mastery: bard — dance, f minor, c major, b augmented sixth, countersong, and every bard song. these abilities may work together when separately learned and applicable.paladinclass mastery: paladin — smite. each smite modifies one separately declared and paid attack; selecting this mastery permits further separately paid smites during that round but never marks a target or creates a duration.hellionclass mastery: hellion — exploit weakness and hellion cleave. the separately catalogued sweeping slash feats are not part of this package.

pages.text: classesstarting and advancing16classes · starting and advancingpriest, shaman, sorcerer, warlock, and necromancer have no class mastery. their job features remain available during a round in which the character uses another job's class mastery, unless an ability says otherwise.this table identifies which ability rules travel together; it does not replace those abilities' complete job and talent descriptions.abilities in the same package may work together when their individual requirements are satisfied. sharing a package does not grant an ability, waive a cost or trigger, or complete unfinished text.reading a job profileeach job profile opens with a prominent job name and an identity and role passage explaining what the job means in vanaheim, its place in the world, and any requirements for taking it. if a job has no special requirement, none is listed. progression identifies the class-family chassis and any other advancement rules. the starting package lists everything gained at job level 1. the rank table lists every talent available through the job; this chapter fully explains only the job's signature talents, while complete rules and xp costs for the rest appear in talents and feats. class mastery, spellcasting, and other exceptional job rules follow when applicable. not every job uses every part.starting and advancingstarting at level 1a new character normally begins with one starting job at job level 1 and no unspent xp. the starting job grants its starting package, its other level-1 features, and access to anything its profile makes available at that level.unless the starting package explicitly says otherwise, the character begins with base attack bonus 0, base fortitude 0, base reflex 0, base will 0, and no purchased advancement trains. an advancement train is a purchased permanent improvement to an ordinary attribute, a created difficulty class, hit points, physical energy, or magical energy; the complete train rules appear under shared advancement. automatic family benefits and explicit racial or job features are then applied normally.each job tracks its own level. a character's overall level is the level of their highest job; levels from different jobs are never added together. the highest-level job is the main job. if two jobs are tied, the job acquired first remains main.acquiring level 1 in another job later grants that job's level-1 features and access, but it does not repeat skills, free selections, equipment, or other benefits reserved for a character's first starting package.

level-1 job was acquired.buying job levelsto raise a job by one level, pay xp equal to the new job level. raising a job from level 5 to level 6 therefore costs 6 xp. no job can advance beyond level 31.the first level of an additional job is a special entry rather than an automatic 1-xp purchase. it requires appropriate training or study and an entry cost set by the dm according to the job, otherwise.job levels unlock ranks, caps, talents, spells, and other access printed in the job profile. they do not automatically purchase base attack bonus, base saves, or advancement trains.example: buying a job level and entering another jobraising mercenary from level 5 to level 6 costs 6 xp. if that mercenary later seeks level 1 in rogue, the first rogue level instead requires the dm-set entry cost and suitable training. once rogue level 1 has been acquired, raising rogue to level 2 uses the ordinary cost of 2 xp.job ranks, training, and instructionrankjob levelsapprentice1-4journeyman5-8veteran9-12expert13-16mentor17-20master21-24champion25-30grand master31the ranks normally available to player characters run through champion. grand master represents exceptional setting-scale advancement.xp pays the numerical cost of advancement, but it does not replace the following training and achievement requirements:acquiring job levels 2 through 12 requires suitable instruction from a mentor or equivalent teacher.entering expert at job level 13 requires completing the mentor's proving task. after entering expert, the character may advance through job the warrior must meet a new challenge or achieve something that meaningfully extends their mastery.shared advancementbase attack bonusbase attack bonus (bab) is one global purchased value. job levels unlock its cap but do not grant bab automatically.each new point of bab costs xp equal to the new value. raising bab from 5 to 6 therefore costs 6 xp.the ordinary bab cap is half the character's overall level, rounded down, reaching its maximum of 15 at overall level 30 or 31.reaching a higher cap gives permission to purchase bab up to that value; equipment mr cannot be suppressed. its complete procedure belongs to talents and feats.class mastery: berserk and furyberserk and fury are mutually exclusive states in one class-mastery package. activating or maintaining either state selects class mastery: barbarian for the round. if another class mastery has already been selected for the round, neither state can be activated during that round. an active berserk or fury must continue selecting barbarian mastery in later rounds. choosing another job's mastery while a state is active ends it immediately and invokes its catch-breath consequence. neither state automatically applies the separate frenzied condition.using berserk or fury. activating either state uses movement and costs 2 pe. every effect other than fury's attack-speed increase begins immediately. the state remains active through the activation round and for one plus the barbarian's constitution modifier complete rounds afterward, with a minimum of one complete round. after that free duration expires, spend 1 pe at the start of each subsequent round, before that round's attack schedule is established, to continue the state through that round. continuation does not refill temporary hp. neither state can be activated while berserk or fury is already active.

pages.title: Example: Fury and Wild Fighting
pages.text: classesbarbarian32classes · barbarianwhen the state ends, the barbarian spends one complete turn catching breath. during that turn the barbarian cannot use movement or make an attack, including an opportunity attack or counterattack. other non-attack main actions and normal active defenses remain legal. catching breath is not the fatigued condition and applies no additional defense penalty.temporary hp, magic protection, and wounds. the temporary hp granted by these states is a separate pool depleted before hp. it cannot be healed, does not stack between berserk and fury, and disappears when the state ends. excess damage continues into hp and then lp. removing the remaining temporary hp when the state ends does not remove underlying hp or lp.their magic protection adds to other applicable magic protection while active and then disappears. it is neither magical energy nor percentile magic resistance. immunity to wound penalties suppresses the numeric serious and critical penalties, critical's attack-speed loss, and critical's inability to run. it does not remove the wound band or prevent bleeding, mortal wounds, unconsciousness, or death.berserk. while berserk, the barbarian gains +2 attack, +2 weapon or unarmed damage, +2 parry, 5 temporary hp, +5 magic protection, +4 on saving throws and on ability or skill checks made to resist spells or fear abilities, and immunity to wound penalties. the barbarian takes -2 dodge and -5 on perception and bluff checks. speaking more than three words coherently or understanding extended speech requires a roll-under intelligence check. on failure, the attempted communication is unintelligible or misunderstood as appropriate.fury. fury never stacks with berserk. while fury, the barbarian gains +6 attack, +6 weapon or unarmed damage, +6 parry, 15 temporary hp, +10 magic protection, +6 fortitude, +6 will, immunity to fear and mind-affecting effects, immunity to wound penalties, and +0.5 attack speed. both the attack and direct damage bonuses apply; positive attack margin can therefore increase the damage further.the barbarian takes -4 dodge and -10 on perception and bluff checks and uses berserk's speech restrictions. taunting a barbarian in fury succeeds automatically. an existing fear or mind-affecting effect is suppressed while fury remains active if the barbarian was able to enter fury; it is not permanently removed. the dodge penalty remains eligible for ordinary pe suppression.fury's attack-speed increase enters the schedule at the start of the next round. with second attack, third attack, and fury, the primary weapon reaches attack speed 2.5. an ordinary offhand then supplies its separate attack every two rounds, producing three attacks each round across the shared cycle.wild fighting. wild fighting is a purchased mentor talent usable only while berserk or fury is active, and it operates inside barbarian mastery. it adds +0.5 attack speed to the primary unarmed attack. each pass granted by ordinary unarmed attack speed, brawling, and wild fighting contains two qualifying unarmed or fist-weapon attacks; a generally applicable attack-speed increase adds unpaired primary attacks. a single-attack main action still contains one attack. bare attacks deal 1d6 bludgeoning damage with pen 2; a qualifying fist weapon uses its printed damage die and type with pen at least 2. the attacks deal lethal damage and receive +4 attack. a defender attempting to parry takes -4 parry. the barbarian may parry an armed attack unarmed without the normal -4 penalty. the +4 attack already makes every active defense harder; wild fighting imposes no separate dodge penalty. second attack, third attack, and ordinary two-weapon fighting do not modify its unarmed schedule. its complete equipment and pe wording belongs to talents and feats.example: fury and wild fightingonce fury's attack-speed increase has entered the schedule, a barbarian using brawling and wild fighting has two paired unarmed passes each round: base unarmed attack speed 1, +0.5 from brawling, and +0.5 from wild fighting. each paired pass contains one primary attack and one offhand attack, supplying two primary attacks and two offhand attacks every round.fury's generally applicable +0.5 attack speed adds one unpaired primary attack on the higher round of its two-round cycle. the barbarian therefore makes five attacks in round 1—three primary and two offhand—then four attacks in round 2—two primary and two offhand—and repeats that 5 / 4 sequence. second attack and third attack do not modify the wild fighting schedule.

pages.title: Example: Fury's Timing, Temporary HP, and Catching Breath
pages.text: classesbarbarian33classes · barbarianexample: fury's timing, temporary hp, and catching breatha barbarian with a constitution modifier of +0 activates fury during round 1. the activation uses movement and costs 2 pe. fury's attack, damage, parry, temporary hp, magic protection, saves, immunities, and penalties begin immediately. its +0.5 attack speed does not alter the round-1 schedule.the barbarian receives 15 temporary hp. if an attack then deals 18 damage, the temporary pool absorbs 15 and the remaining 3 reduces hp. the lost temporary hp cannot be healed or restored by continuing fury.round 2 is the one complete free round supplied by fury's minimum duration. its +0.5 attack speed now enters the schedule established at the start of the round. at the start of round 3, the free duration has expired. before establishing that round's attack schedule, the barbarian spends 1 pe to continue fury for the round. the +0.5 attack speed remains in the schedule, but the depleted temporary-hp pool is not refilled.the barbarian ends fury after round 3. during the next complete turn, the barbarian catches breath: no movement or attack is allowed, including an opportunity attack or counterattack. a non-attack main action and normal active defenses remain legal. after that turn, the barbarian acts normally again.

pages.title: Scout · Starting Package
pages.text: classesscout36classes · scoutscoutidentity and role. scouts are pathfinders, hunters, outriders, and reconnaissance specialists who operate ahead of armies and beyond settled roads. they read terrain, survive with little support, move among frontier communities, and try to decide an encounter with a concealed first shot before settling into disciplined ranged combat.progression. scouts use shared advancement and the adventurer chassis above. a scout's ordinary attack speed is 1 for both armed and unarmed combat unless an explicit talent or other rule increases it.starting packageequipment training. acquiring scout job level 1 grants training with spear, axe, dagger, bow, crossbow, staff, sword, whip, and unarmed combat. it also grants training with light armor and the buckler. it does not grant medium or heavy armor, larger shields, firearms, siege weapons, athani blackbows, gravity balls, culturally restricted equipment, or another specialist or item-specific training. an item that requires its own special training still requires that training.endurance. the scout gains endurance at job level 1 and uses its warrior-style pe schedule for qualifying scout levels unless pathfinding later replaces that rate with the scout-specific progression below.tracking. the scout gains tracking at job level 1. tracking uses its own procedure when circumstances require a check; possessing it does not turn every sign into an automatic success.trailcraft. when uncertainty requires a check, trailcraft uses survival. the scout gains +4 on survival checks to find food or water, choose safe shelter, predict ordinary weather, and recognize natural travel hazards. trailcraft does not find or follow another creature's trail, prevent the scout from becoming lost, or replace tracking or pathfinding.frontier manners. the scout gains +4 on charisma-based social checks involving hunters, trappers, wilderness guides, isolated settlements, and other people whose lives depend upon frontier or wilderness travel. this is not a general bonus with every rural person and does not guarantee hospitality, trust, supplies, or safe passage.scout camouflage. the scout gains scout camouflage at job level 1. its complete preparation and concealment procedure appears immediately below.apprentice talent access. butcher, sneak, tame, and fletch become available for purchase. none are learned automatically.scout camouflagethe scout may spend 10 minutes preparing camouflage from materials appropriate to the current terrain. while it remains matched to that terrain, the scout gains +20 on stealth checks to remain hidden. this bonus does not stack with hide's +10; use the greater applicable bonus.the scout may remain stationary normally. if the scout also possesses sneak, movement made while sneaking does not end the camouflage. otherwise movement ends it. attacking, casting a spell, taking another conspicuous action, or leaving the matching terrain ends the camouflage after the action resolves.scout camouflage is physical concealment rather than invisibility. detect invisibility does not reveal the scout, and ordinary scent-based detection cannot locate the scout through the camouflage alone. tremorsense and another sense that directly detects the scout's movement or physical contact with the ground still function normally. the +20 remains a stealth modifier rather than automatic success.class talentsthe rank table below lists every talent available through the scout job. only the selected talents and job-owned procedures most important to understanding how the scout operates are explained here. complete generic descriptions and xp costs for the remaining talents appear in talents and feats.

pages.title: Class Mastery: Scout
pages.text: classesscout37classes · scoutscout ranktalent accessapprenticebutcher; sneak; tame; fletchjourneymanherbalism; rescue; self defenseveterandisguise; brawling; pathfindingexpertsecond attack; haggle; ranged mastery i; skinningmentorranged mastery ii; rapid fire; scrolls; stavesmasterranged mastery iii; ambushpathfinding and physical energy. pathfinding requires endurance. once purchased, it replaces the scout-with-endurance level-based pe rate with 1 level-based pe at every qualifying scout job level through level 30. it does not add a second pe progression or multiply purchased pe trains. if learned late, it grants only the positive difference between the two progressions at the current scout job level, counting only scout levels that established new overall levels and contributed level-based pe. pathfinding's travel procedure appears in talents and feats.class mastery: scoutranged mastery, rapid fire, and ambush form one package. they may work together when their individual requirements are met. selecting another job's class mastery suppresses every scout-mastery benefit for that round. if ranged mastery or ambush first becomes relevant through an opening attack, lock or choose scout mastery immediately before that attack roll. ambush can therefore select scout mastery during round 0. rapid fire cannot operate during round 0 because it requires a full attack.ranged mastery. each tier is purchased separately and applies to ranged attacks with trained ranged weapons whose own loading and handling permit the attack. ranged mastery ii requires ranged mastery i, and ranged mastery iii requires ranged mastery ii.

pages.title: Example: Ambush, Rapid Fire, and the Adventurer Damage Addition
pages.text: classesscout38classes · scouttierbenefits while class mastery: scout is selectedranged mastery i+2 attack with trained ranged weapons.ranged mastery iithe attack bonus becomes +4; the ordinary far-range penalty is reduced from -8 to -4.ranged mastery iiithe attack bonus becomes +6; the scout takes no attack penalty at far range.ranged mastery grants no direct damage bonus, pen increase, additional range band, or change to extreme range. extreme range retains its full -16 attack penalty, prohibition on called shots, and removal of positive attack margin from damage. ranged mastery's attack bonus can increase damage through ordinary positive attack margin.rapid fire. when the scout makes a full attack with a trained ranged weapon capable of making the attacks under its own loading, ammunition, and handling rules, rapid fire adds one additional ranged attack to that full attack. at scout job level 30, it adds two additional ranged attacks total instead of one. resolve them immediately after the first scheduled attack of that full attack. they cost no pe beyond the full attack's ordinary total cost and count toward the full-attack limit.rapid fire is a purchased mentor talent and a flat addition once per full attack. it does not increase attack speed, create an attack pass, grant attacks once per pass, or multiply through second attack, haste, or another attack-speed effect. with second attack, the ordinary two-round schedule is 3, 2; at scout level 30 it is 4, 3. haste's +1 attack speed produces 5, 4 with level-30 rapid fire. rapid fire cannot operate during round 0 because round 0 permits no full attack.ambush. ambush is a purchased master talent that may be used only on the scout's first attack attempt of a combat. before rolling, the scout may declare it for a ranged attack against a target within 60 feet that cannot perceive or anticipate the scout. add the scout job level to that attack roll. the bonus applies only to that attack and can increase damage only through positive attack margin. it does not apply to a rapid fire attack or another projectile. the opportunity is expended whether the attack hits or misses.scout camouflage can help establish ambush but is not required when the scout is otherwise genuinely unperceived and unanticipated. ambush may initiate combat during round 0 because it is a scout job mastery. the round 0 attack cannot receive the adventurer chassis's once-per-battle damage addition. an otherwise qualifying ambush in round 1 or later may receive that separate addition on its resulting damage roll.example: ambush, rapid fire, and the adventurer damage additiona concealed scout with second attack chooses a target that cannot perceive or anticipate the scout, then selects class mastery: scout immediately before opening combat with ambush. this is a round-0 attack, so the scout adds the scout job level to the attack roll but cannot add the adventurer-chassis benefit to its damage. round 0 also forbids a full attack, so rapid fire adds nothing to this opening shot.in round 1, the scout makes a full attack. second attack supplies two scheduled attacks, and rapid fire adds one attack immediately after the first of them, producing three attacks that round. the scout may add the adventurer job level to one chosen damage roll among those attacks, not to all three. in round 2, another full attack receives one scheduled attack from second attack and one more from rapid fire, producing two attacks and completing the ordinary 3, 2 cycle.
