pages.title: Rogue · Starting Package
pages.text: classesrogue40classes · roguerogueidentity and role. rogues are infiltrators, thieves, assassins, fixers, and other specialists who win through preparation, misdirection, and control over when violence begins. they excel when an enemy is unaware, exposed, or occupied; a fair prolonged exchange gives up the advantages on which their training depends.progression. rogues use shared advancement and the adventurer chassis above. a rogue's ordinary armed and unarmed attack speed is 1 unless an explicit weapon configuration, talent, or other rule increases it.starting packageequipment training. acquiring rogue job level 1 grants training with dagger, mace, sword, whip, sling, bow, crossbow, and unarmed combat. it also grants training with light armor and the buckler. it does not grant medium or heavy armor, larger shields, culturally restricted equipment, or another specialist or item-specific training. an item that requires its own special training still requires that training.finesse. the rogue may use dexterity in place of strength for attack, weapon damage, and parry with a light or medium melee weapon. dexterity replaces strength in each applicable formula; the two modifiers are not added together. finesse remains available when another class mastery is selected.quick draw. the rogue may draw an accessible light or medium melee weapon eligible for finesse without spending movement. quick draw remains available when another class mastery is selected. it does not accelerate sheathing or retrieving a stored weapon.casing. the rogue gains +4 on checks involving entrances, exits, patrol routines, escape routes, and likely access points in a built environment. casing gathers or interprets information available from observation; it does not automatically reveal a concealed route or security measure.underworld courtesy. the rogue gains +4 on charisma-based social checks involving thieves, smugglers, fences, and similar criminal operators. this familiarity does not guarantee trust, cooperation, favorable prices, membership, or safe passage.apprentice talent access. backstab, hard trip, haggle, hide, peek, and self defense become available for purchase. none are learned automatically.class talentsthe rank table below lists every talent available through the rogue job. only the job-defining procedures needed to understand how the rogue creates and exploits an advantage are explained here. complete generic descriptions and xp costs for the remaining talents appear in talents and feats.rogue ranktalent accessapprenticebackstab; hard trip; haggle; hide; peek; self defensejourneymansneak; steal; disguise; sneak attackveteranplant; brawling; hamstring; climb; enduranceexpertenhanced damage; second attack; dual backstab; skirmishmentorenvenom; featherfoot; street network; scrolls; staves; wandsmasterultimate evasionclass mastery: roguesneak attack, backstab, hamstring, and dual backstab form one package. they may work together when their individual requirements are met. selecting another job's class mastery suppresses every rogue-mastery benefit for that round. finesse, quick draw, casing, underworld courtesy, skirmish, envenom, and other non-mastery features or talents remain available under their own rules.if sneak attack or backstab first becomes relevant through an opening attack, lock or choose rogue mastery immediately before that attack roll. rogue mastery may therefore be selected during round 0 when one of its abilities is otherwise legal.sneak attack and backstab each grant the same +1 pen increase. these increases do not stack: an attack qualifying for both gains +1 pen total, not +2.

pages.title: Page 41
pages.text: classesrogue41classes · roguesneak attack. sneak attack is a purchased journeyman talent. on every qualifying attack, add half the rogue job level, rounded down, to the attack roll. an attack qualifies when the target is flanked or when an explicit rule denies or removes the target's dexterity modifier from defense against that attack. choosing a defense calculation that does not ordinarily use dexterity does not by itself qualify.the rogue must be able to perceive and reach a vital area. sneak attack cannot be used when concealment applies to the attack. at range, it can be made from no farther than 60 feet against a target not participating in combat, or 30 feet against a target participating in combat.a qualifying sneak attack gains +1 pen. this does not stack with backstab's pen increase. the attack bonus may increase damage through positive attack margin, but sneak attack grants no separate direct damage bonus and is not automatically lethal damage. it applies to every attack that independently satisfies its requirements rather than once per round.backstab. backstab is a purchased apprentice talent that modifies a melee attack made with a short, one-handed piercing weapon, normally a dagger, short sword, rapier, rondel dagger, tanto, or comparable weapon. the target must be genuinely unaware that they are in danger; merely being flat-footed is insufficient.on a successful backstab, add the rogue job level as fixed raw damage before damage reduction. this fixed damage is not multiplied by a critical hit or another dice multiplier. a qualifying backstab gains +1 pen, which does not stack with sneak attack's pen increase. backstab costs no pe, may operate during round 0, and is not automatically lethal damage. it may combine with sneak attack when that attack independently satisfies sneak attack's requirements.

pages.title: Example: Sneak Attack, Backstab, and Dual Backstab
pages.text: classesrogue42classes · roguedual backstab. dual backstab is a purchased expert talent. once per round, after a successful backstab leaves its victim alive, the rogue may immediately make one additional attack against that victim with an eligible backstab weapon. this attack spends no pe and consumes no scheduled attack, attack pass, main action, or movement.for this immediate attack, the victim may make an ordinary active dodge even if the opening strike's surprise or flat-footed state would otherwise prevent it, but cannot parry or block. the second strike receives backstab's fixed damage and +1 pen despite the victim's new awareness. the opening strike's surprise or flat-footed state alone does not make this second strike a sneak attack; sneak attack applies only when another qualifying trigger still applies, such as flanking. dual backstab cannot trigger itself and may follow a round 0 backstab.hamstring. hamstring is a purchased veteran talent and belongs to class mastery: rogue when used as a special extension of sneak attack. its complete injury, save, cost, and duration procedure belongs to talents and feats.example: sneak attack, backstab, and dual backstaba rogue selects class mastery: rogue immediately before a round-0 attack against an unaware target. the attack uses a rondel dagger and also qualifies for sneak attack because another explicit rule denies the target's dexterity modifier from defense. sneak attack adds half the rogue job level to the attack roll, and a successful backstab adds the full rogue job level as fixed raw damage. both abilities grant +1 pen, but their identical pen increases do not stack: the attack gains +1 pen total.the victim survives, so dual backstab permits one immediate second attack. the victim may use an ordinary active dodge but cannot parry or block. backstab's fixed damage and +1 pen still apply to this second strike. the victim now knows the rogue is attacking, so the opening surprise or flat-footed state cannot by itself make the second strike a sneak attack; a separate trigger such as flanking would still qualify it.because both attacks occur during round 0, neither may receive the adventurer chassis's once-per-battle damage addition. that benefit becomes available when round 1 begins.

pages.text: classesbard44classes · bardbardidentity and role. bards are wandering performers, court artists, lorekeepers, and provocateurs who work magic through voice, instrument, and strange patterned movement. their performances can stir allies, unsettle enemies, reshape the sound of a battlefield, or release concentrated sonic force. ordinary bards follow this performance tradition rather than a conventional spellcasting path.progression. bards use shared advancement and the adventurer chassis above. a bard's ordinary armed and unarmed attack speed is 1 unless an explicit weapon configuration, talent, or other rule increases it. bard performances use bard job level rather than caster level.starting packageequipment training. acquiring bard job level 1 grants training with culturally restricted equipment, or another specialist or item-specific training.performer's welcome. the bard gains +4 on charisma-based checks involving performers, entertainers, audiences, patrons, and establishments accustomed to hosting them. this familiarity does not guarantee employment, admiration, hospitality, payment, or safe passage.travelling repertoire. the bard gains +2 on intelligence-based checks to recall commonly circulated songs, stories, customs, genealogies, and local traditions. this is mundane learned knowledge and remains distinct from the supernatural lore talent.apprentice talent access. dance, hard trip, dirt kick, f minor, songs of antimagic, songs of protection, songs of war, and c major become available for purchase. no talent, direct note, or song pages.title: Bard Performances · Bard Performance DC
pages.text: classesbard45classes · bardbard performancesdance, the three direct notes, countersong, and every bard song are magical non-spell abilities. they are talents rather than spells. they require no spell slot, verbal / somatic / material component, spell speed, spell concentration, armor spell failure roll, defensive casting, combat casting, or counterspell procedure. being hit does not interrupt a performance, and beginning or maintaining one does not provoke an attack of opportunity.performances remain magical for magic resistance, magic protection, dispelling, antimagic, aura of negation, and another rule that explicitly affects magical non-spell abilities. magical sonic damage is reduced by magic protection. direct-note damage is also reduced by worn physical armor's dr as a flat value; do not compare penetration and armor grade for it.an ordinary bard has no bard spell list or caster-level progression. scrolls, staves, and wands become available only through their named talents. the true bards of creation and destruction are exceptional setting-scale practitioners outside this ordinary player job.bard performance dcwhen a bard performance calls for a save, start at 10, then add the bard's charisma modifier, half the bard job level rounded down, art, and any other modifiers that apply.this is a non-spell job dc, not a spell dc.class mastery: barddance, f minor, c major, b augmented sixth, countersong, and every bard song form class mastery: bard. these separately learned abilities may work together when their individual requirements permit. lore, persuade, juggle, tumbling, and ordinary nonperformance talents remain outside the package.using a direct note locks bard mastery for that round. a maintained song or dance requires bard mastery in every round in which it continues. selecting another job's class mastery immediately ends the bard's continuing song and dance. allies affected by a bard performance may use their own class masteries normally.

pages.title: Maintaining a Song · Dance
pages.text: classesbard46classes · bardmaintaining a songstarting a song uses the bard's main action and pays its starting me cost. maintaining it uses a free action each round. pay me only when the listed upkeep interval comes due: a per-minute song still requires the free action every round but does not charge me every round. a pulsing song applies its first pulse immediately; the bard must maintain it and pay the next upkeep before each later pulse.the bard may maintain only one song at a time. starting another immediately ends the former song. a song may begin during round 0.voice alone is sufficient. singing leaves the bard's hands free but prevents speech, warnings, commands, and verbal spell components. an instrument occupies the hands needed to play it but permits speech. switching between voice and instrument ends the performance; restarting requires another main action and starting cost.maintaining a song does not use spell concentration. damage alone does not end it. the bard may end it voluntarily. it ends automatically if the bard cannot continue performing, cannot take the maintenance free action, cannot pay the next upkeep, or becomes stunned, paralyzed, or unconscious.unless stated otherwise, a song has a continuously updating 60-foot radius centered on the bard. a creature is affected only while it remains in that area and can hear the song. losing either condition ends that creature's effect immediately.hearing is required for beneficial and hostile songs. covering the ears grants +2 on saves; effective earplugs ordinarily grant +4 to +8 according to quality and fit; deafness grants immunity. direct notes, songs of silence's field, and songs of antimagic's effect on existing magic are explicit exceptions.resolve a hostile song's applicable magic resistance and save once when a creature is first exposed. that result lasts for the continuous performance; leaving and returning does not grant another attempt. songs of antimagic's casting gate and songs of sleep's second save are explicit exceptions.identical songs do not stack; use the strongest.danceactivating dance uses movement and costs 2 pe. it lasts for a number of complete rounds equal to the bard's charisma modifier, with a minimum of one round. before it expires, the bard may renew it by spending movement and 2 pe again.dance is a sequence of strange, broken-rhythm movements that makes the bard difficult to read; it is neither ordinary social dancing nor required travel across the battlefield. the bard gains a +4 dodge-type bonus to dodge and +4 bluff. the dodge-type bonus does not stack with featherfoot or another dodge-type bonus; use the greatest applicable bonus. enhanced dodge expressly adds its +1.its dodge benefit is visual, mind-affecting misdirection. it provides no dodge bonus against a mindless attacker, an attacker immune to mind-affecting effects, or an attacker unable to perceive the movement. immobilization or an incompatible physical action ends dance.the bard may fold unusual movement into the sequence. if compatibility is genuinely uncertain, the dm may call for a performance check. dance itself permits that specific check without requiring a separately learned performance field and grants +4 on it. the bonus applies only to incorporating the uncertain action into dance; it does not improve another performance field, a song or direct-note dc, or another bard ability. dance may coexist with one song and activates that song's printed dance effect.direct noteseach direct note deals a number of d6 of magical sonic damage equal to half the bard job level, rounded down, with a minimum of 1d6. complete the nominal dice expression, roll no more than four damage dice, and replace each excess die with +2. bard level 30 therefore produces 4d6 + 22, not 15 rolled dice. converted +2 values remain part of the damage-dice subtotal for critical multiplication if an explicit later rule ever permits a critical; the direct notes themselves make no attack roll and cannot critically hit.magic resistance applies. magic protection and worn physical armor's flat dr reduce the damage. direct notes use no penetration / armor grade comparison, attack margin, or critical hit.

pages.title: Songs
pages.text: classesbard47classes · bardf minor. spend 1 pe and use a main action to affect one creature within melee reach. no attack roll or save is made.c major. spend 2 pe and use a main action to affect one creature within 60 feet. a successful fortitude save halves the damage. it does not provoke an attack of opportunity.b augmented sixth. spend 4 pe and use a main action. every other creature within 120 feet, including allies and enemies but excluding the bard, takes the damage; a successful fortitude save halves it. it does not affect objects unless an explicit rule says otherwise.songssongs of antimagic.cost: 3 me to start; 1 me per minute to maintain.reduce the effective caster level of every affected caster and ongoing spell effect by half the bard job level, rounded down. the reduction is at least 1 and at most 10, and it cannot reduce a caster level below 1. this changes caster-level-derived damage dice, durations, caster-level checks, and comparable values. it does not change spell access, spell circle, me cost, or spell speed. ordinarily it does not change spell dc.while dance is active, the reduction also lowers spell dc one-for-one. an affected caster must additionally succeed on a will save against the bard's performance dc before each casting attempt. failure spends the attempted main action but no me, and the spell does not begin. existing spell effects in the area are reduced without needing to hear the song.songs of protection.cost: 2 me to start; 1 me per minute to maintain.each hearing ally adds half the bard job level, rounded down, to worn armor's dr, with a minimum addition of +1. the addition cannot exceed that armor's own pre-song dr. this remains grade-sensitive armor dr. the song does not increase armor grade, armor hp, or another flat-dr source; a creature without worn armor gains no dr.while dance is active, each affected ally also gains magic protection equal to one-third of the bard job level, rounded down, with a minimum of 1.songs of war.cost: 2 me to start; 1 me per minute to maintain.each hearing ally gains a morale attack bonus equal to one-fifth of the bard job level, rounded down, with a minimum of +1 and a maximum of +6. while dance is active, the same morale bonus applies to rolled active and static defense, including dodge, parry, and block. dance also grants +0.5 attack speed through bard job level 19 or +1 at level 20 or later; apply it to the next round's schedule.the morale bonus does not stack with heroism, rallying cry, or another morale bonus; use the greatest. the attack-speed increase does not stack with haste, rallying cry, or another temporary effect-based attack-speed increase; use the greatest. allies retain their own class masteries.songs of healing.cost: 2 me to start; 1 me per round to maintain.each pulse restores hp equal to one-tenth of the bard job level, rounded up, with a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 3, to every living hearer, including the bard, allies, and enemies: 1 hp at bard levels 1–10, 2 at 11–20, and 3 at 21–31. armor-contributed hp belongs to the same hp pool and can be restored. the song does not restore lp or temporary hp. while dance is active, each pulse also restores 1 pe.for each listener, track how much hp and pe this bard has actually restored with songs of healing today. that bard can restore at most hp equal to the bard job level and, separately, pe equal to half that level rounded down to the same listener in one day. a pulse that reaches a remaining limit restores only the available amount; a full hp limit does not prevent legal pe restoration, or vice versa. restoration prevented by a full resource pool does not count toward the daily limit.countersong.cost: 2 me to start; 1 me per minute to maintain.choose one hostile song within 60 feet that the bard can hear. make an opposed d20 + bard job level + charisma modifier roll against its performer. countersong must win; a tie preserves the existing song. on a win, that song is suppressed while both performances continue and remain in range. on failure, the bard may restart countersong on a later turn by paying its starting cost again.

pages.title: Page 48
pages.text: classesbard48classes · bardcountersong occupies the bard's one maintained-song allowance. starting another song ends countersong, and starting countersong ends another song the bard was maintaining.while countersong is active, or when the bard has specifically readied it against sonic damage, reduce each sonic-damage result within 60 feet by a number of d6 equal to half the bard job level, rounded down, with a minimum of 1d6. damage cannot be reduced below 0. this is mitigation rather than damage, so the four-damage-dice conversion does not apply. magic protection reduces any remaining magical sonic damage normally. the mitigation is not retroactive. dance adds no further effect.songs of death.cost: 3 me to start; 1 me per round to maintain.each pulse deals flat magical hp damage equal to one-fifth of the bard job level, rounded down, with a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 6, to every living hearer, including the bard, allies, and enemies. a successful will save negates the entire performance for that creature, including dance's pe loss. magic protection applies; physical armor does not.the damage stops at 0 hp and never crosses into lp. the first time a creature reaches 0 hp from this continuous performance, it becomes unconscious and makes one fortitude save against the bard's dc. failure also makes it permanently deafened. this deafness prevents later pulses from affecting that creature but does not itself wake the creature. song-induced unconsciousness ends when the performance ends or the creature rises above 0 hp. while dance is active, each affected creature also loses 1 pe per pulse.songs of dancing.cost: 4 me to start; 1 me per round to maintain.the bard must already have dance active and maintain it throughout the song. every other hearer makes a will save. on failure, involuntary dancing consumes that creature's movement each round while the effect continues; it retains its main and free actions. this is mind-affecting. leaving the area, losing hearing, the song ending, or dance ending removes the effect.songs of silence.cost: 4 me to start; 1 me per round to maintain.this song creates a moving 60-foot field centered on the bard. sound created inside remains audible inside but does not ordinarily pass out. sound originating outside enters normally. very loud sound may escape at the dm's judgment. verbal spell components work inside the field. while dance is active, the outward boundary becomes absolute. the field is environmental and does not require hearing or a save.songs of sleep.cost: 4 me to start; 1 me per round to maintain.each enemy hearer makes an initial will save. on failure, first establish and cap the creature's legal full-attack schedule, then remove one retained attack, to a minimum of one remaining attack.

pages.title: Example: Maintaining a Song while Dancing
pages.text: classesbard49classes · bardalso add 1 pe to every action or reaction already costing pe; a 0-pe action remains free.while dance is active, an initial failure requires a second will save at the beginning of the creature's next turn. failure makes it sleep and become unconscious until damaged, unable to hear the song, or the song ends. success on the second save leaves the base penalties in place; waking from damage also leaves them while the performance continues. immunity to magical or mundane sleep blocks only the final sleep. complete mind-affecting immunity blocks the entire song.songs of magic.cost: 4 me to start; 1 me per round to maintain.every creature that hears the song, including the bard, allies, and enemies, increases effective caster level by one-third of the bard job level, rounded down, with a minimum increase of 1 and a maximum of 10. this changes caster-level-derived damage dice, durations, caster-level checks, and comparable values. it does not change spell access, spell circle, me cost, or spell speed. ordinarily it does not change spell dc.while dance is active, the increase also raises spell dc one-for-one, symmetrically with songs of antimagic. the increase applies to spells cast while hearing the song; it does not alter effects created before exposure.example: maintaining a song while dancinga bard uses movement and 2 pe to begin dance, then sings songs of healing by using the main action and 2 me. the song's first pulse occurs immediately. every living creature that can hear the bard within 60 feet—including enemies—recovers the listed hp, and dance's rider also restores 1 pe to each of them.the bard is singing, so both hands remain free, but the bard cannot speak, issue warnings or commands, or supply verbal spell components. playing an instrument would reverse that tradeoff: the required hands would be occupied, but speech would remain possible. switching methods during the performance would end the song and require a new main action and starting cost to begin it again.at the start of the next round, the bard selects bard mastery again, maintains the song with a free action, and pays its 1-me per-round upkeep before the next pulse. if the bard instead selects another job's class mastery, both the song and dance end immediately; neither remains dormant for a later round.

pages.title: Acolyte Jobs · Acolyte Chassis
pages.text: classesacolyte jobs50classes · acolyte jobsacolyte jobsacolyte chassisthe acolyte family contains the priest, shaman, paladin, and hellion jobs. all four use the universal base-save cap and acolyte save costs under shared advancement, together with the acolyte train caps and the permanent choice between hp, me, or balanced hp-and-me progression made upon acquiring the first acolyte-family job.master intervention. entering master at job level 21 grants the intervention feature named by the job. priest, paladin, and hellion grant divine intervention. shaman grants spirit bond. these features are automatic rather than purchased talents.divine intervention. a priest, paladin, or hellion with this feature may once during their lifetime petition their god concerning a matter of paramount importance to that god's doctrine when ordinary avenues are exhausted. there is no fixed roll, action, magnitude, or promised form; the god determines the answer and any demand or lasting consequence. making the petition consumes the one lifetime opportunity even when the answer is smaller, stranger, or more dangerous than requested. divine intervention is neither a spell nor a class mastery.job rank and religious standing are separate. reaching a rank in an acolyte-family job does not itself confer an ecclesiastical office or standing. each acolyte-family job supplies its own starting package, equipment training, talent access, spell access, religious requirements, armor-casting permission, and any class mastery. the family itself grants none of those features universally.

pages.title: Page 51
pages.text: classesacolyte jobs51classes · acolyte jobs

pages.title: Priest · Starting Package
pages.text: classespriest52classes · priestpriestidentity and role. priests are servants who answer a divine calling and receive formal investment from a faith. they are responsible for its rites, teachings, communities, and divine magic. their social authority and duties depend on the god and institution they serve, so two priests may share the same job while leading very different lives.progression. priests use shared advancement and the acolyte chassis above. a priest's ordinary armed and unarmed attack speed is 1 unless an explicit talent, weapon configuration, spell, or other rule changes it.starting packageequipment training. acquiring priest job level 1 ordinarily grants training with dagger, mace, sling, staff, and unarmed combat. it also grants training with light armor and the buckler. a faith may grant additional weapons, shields, or armor. if the faith explicitly withholds or forbids armor or shield training, that faith-specific rule controls those entries. culturally restricted, specialist, and item-specific equipment still requires its own training. ordinary unarmed training does not grant the self defense talent.rites and doctrine. the priest gains +2 on checks concerning their own faith's theology, scripture, rites, and religious law. the priest can perform the faith's ordinary ceremonies when circumstances and standing permit.clerical standing. the priest gains +4 on social checks involving followers of the same faith while acting within recognized priestly duties. this does not compel obedience, create supernatural authority, guarantee aid, or override a higher religious authority.apprentice talent access. scrolls and staves become available for purchase. neither talent is learned automatically.religious standingformal investment at priest job level 1 makes the character a follower: an acknowledged member of the faith. follower standing alone does not authorize divine spellcasting. the priest must attain high follower, the standing at which the faith entrusts divine spells, as well as the required priest job level before casting them.loss or demotion below high follower suspends priest spellcasting and faith-granted supernatural permissions. it does not erase priest job levels, learned spells, mundane equipment training, or ordinary learned talents. restoring high follower standing restores those permissions. high follower, high priest, and job rank are separate concepts.class talentsthe rank table below lists every talent available through the priest job. complete descriptions and xp costs for these generic talents appear in talents and feats; classes retains only the distinctions needed to read the priest profile.priest ranktalent accessapprenticescrolls; stavesjourneymanself during a round in which the character uses another job's class mastery, unless an ability says otherwise.

pages.title: Shaman · Starting Package
pages.text: classesshaman54classes · shamanshamanidentity and role. shamans are people whose magic is heard and answered by spirits older than organized human religion. training alone cannot establish this relationship: the spirits must accept the character, and taking the job requires dm approval. some shamans inherit bloodlines shaped by old pacts with animal spirits; others draw a spirit's favor through unusual circumstances of birth or later life that no institution can reliably predict or force. shaman is the rules title: one may be a formal court shugenja in nerina while another is an isolated spirit-worker.shamans have no follower, high follower, favored, or other religious-standing ladder. a character either possesses the spirit relationship that permits shaman training and spellcasting or does not.progression. shamans use shared advancement and the acolyte chassis above. a shaman's ordinary armed and unarmed attack speed is 1 unless an explicit talent, weapon configuration, spell, or other rule changes it.starting packageequipment training. acquiring shaman job level 1 ordinarily grants training with axe, dagger, flail, mace, sling, crossbow, staff, and unarmed combat, together with all ordinary shields. it grants no armor training. culturally restricted, specialist, and item-specific equipment still requires its own training. ordinary unarmed training does not grant self defense or brawling.spirit courtesy. the shaman gains +4 on social checks made directly with pre-human spirits and with communities that actively venerate them. this familiarity supplies neither a language nor automatic detection, obedience, aid, improved starting attitude, safe passage, or immunity from a spirit's nature and taboos. it does not apply to gods, divine servants, undead, ancestors, or creatures merely described as spirits unless an explicit rule places them in this tradition.spirit lore. the shaman gains +2 on checks concerning spirits, offerings, taboos, sacred places, and shamanic traditions.apprentice talent access. staves becomes available for purchase. it is not learned automatically.class talentsthe rank table below lists every talent available through the shaman job. complete descriptions and xp costs for these generic talents appear in talents and feats; classes retains only the distinctions needed to read the shaman profile.shaman ranktalent accessapprenticestavesjourneymanself defense; scrollsveterantranceexpertendurance; brawling; second attackmentorbrew; lucid dreamingmaster—entering master at shaman job level 21 grants spirit bond; it is not a purchased talent. brawling enables an unarmed full attack and adds +0.5 only to that unarmed method. second attack applies only to weapon full attacks.shaman has no class mastery. shaman spells, talents, job features, and spirit bond remain available during a round in which the character uses another job's class mastery, unless an ability says otherwise.spirit bondonce per year, the shaman may petition a spirit with whom they have an established bond and ask for aid. a shaman may maintain bonds with several spirits, but they all share this single use. the request is limited by the chosen spirit's nature, reach, willingness, and actual power.there is no fixed roll or guaranteed outcome. the spirit decides whether and how to answer and may require an offering, service, price, or other consequence. making the request expends the use even if the spirit refuses or its answer proves inadequate. spirit bond becomes available again after one full in-world year has passed. it is neither a spell nor a class mastery.

pages.text: classespaladin56classes · paladinpaladinidentity and role. paladins are rare divine champions chosen directly by ain, altair, or alshain. only a lawful good character directly chosen by a paladin-granting god may take this job, with dm approval. their martial power, miracles, and binding standard of conduct all follow from that divine choice. training and religious promotion can prepare a candidate, but neither can bestow the job.progression. paladins use shared advancement and the acolyte chassis above. a paladin's armed and unarmed attack speed is 1 unless a talent, weapon configuration, spell, or other rule changes it.starting packageequipment training. acquiring paladin job level 1 ordinarily grants training with dagger, flail, mace, polearm, sling, spear, staff, sword, crossbow, and unarmed combat. it also grants training with light, medium, and heavy armor and all ordinary shields. culturally restricted, specialist, and item-specific equipment still requires its own training. rifle and siege equipment are not automatic paladin training.divine grace. while conscious and able to act, the paladin may add their charisma bonus to any saving throw. decide separately for each save. this does not replace the save's ordinary ability modifier.aura of courage. the paladin is immune to fear while conscious. a conscious paladin can assert this aura whenever its effects become relevant, even after failing a fear save, without using movement or a main action. the aura requires no maintenance and remains active while the paladin is conscious. allies within 10 feet gain +4 on saves against fear while the aura operates. the aura is divine rather than enchantment magic.while the paladin wields a sword or spear that an item, spell, or faith rule explicitly identifies as holy, evil creatures within the aura take -2 attack and defense, and allies within it are immune to mind-affecting effects originating from those creatures. an ordinary enchanted weapon does not qualify unless its own rule identifies it as holy.smite evil. the paladin gains smite evil. its complete one-attack procedure appears under class mastery: paladin below.lay on hands. spend 2 pe to restore 1d6 hp plus half the paladin job level, rounded down, to a living creature. using lay on hands on another creature is a main action. using it on the paladin requires neither movement nor a main action. a living creature can benefit from this healing no more than three times per day, including self-healing, regardless of which paladin uses the ability.instead of healing, the paladin may spend 2 pe and deliver lay on hands to an undead creature through a successful melee touch attack. on a hit, it deals a number of d6 of damage equal to half the paladin job level, rounded down, with a minimum of 1d6 and no saving throw. roll no more than four damage dice and replace each additional die with +2. this use does not provoke merely because it is an unarmed touch.detect evil. while conscious, the paladin passively senses exceptional or supernatural evil. the sense reveals presence and approximate strength rather than exact identity, location, or intent. stronger evil can be sensed farther away, and an overwhelming presence may burden an inexperienced paladin as the dm judges. this feature does not replace a separately listed detect evil spell.apprentice talent access. rescue becomes available for purchase. it is not learned automatically.job featuresdivine health. at paladin job level 3, the paladin becomes immune to disease, including magical and supernatural disease. at level 15, the paladin may remove one nonmagical disease from a creature by touch once per week as a main action. at level 30, this may be done twice per week.

pages.title: Class Talents · Class Mastery: Paladin — Smite Evil
pages.text: classespaladin57classes · paladinclass talentsthe rank table below lists every talent available through the paladin job. complete descriptions and xp costs for these generic talents appear in talents and feats. the paladin's defining divine features and smite procedure remain complete in this profile.paladin ranktalent accessapprenticerescuejourneymanself defense; disarm; enhanced damageveterancombat casting; fast healingexpertsecond attack; endurance; brawlingmentortrance; third attackmaster—entering master at paladin job level 21 grants divine intervention as described in the acolyte chassis; it is not a purchased talent.class mastery: paladin — smite evilimmediately before resolving one otherwise legal physical attack, the paladin may spend 1 pe and declare that attack a smite. a physical attack for this purpose is a weapon or unarmed attack, not a spell or spell-like effect unless an explicit rule says otherwise. declaring a smite requires neither movement nor a main action, grants no extra attack, and changes none of the underlying attack's normal timing or requirements. the pe is spent whether the attack hits or misses.the declaration selects paladin mastery for that round if no mastery is already locked. a different locked mastery prevents smite. once paladin mastery is selected, any number of the paladin's remaining weapon or unarmed attacks that round may each become another smite by making another declaration and spending another 1 pe.against an evil target, the smite gains an attack bonus equal to half paladin job level, rounded down, and adds the paladin's charisma bonus as fixed raw damage before protection. double only that charisma addition against an evil outsider or undead creature. the attack bonus may increase damage through positive attack margin but is not also added directly to damage. the fixed charisma damage is not a damage die and is not multiplied by a critical hit.

pages.title: Hellion · Starting Package
pages.text: classeshellion60classes · hellionhellionidentity and role. hellion is the rules title for the martial knights of the imperial faiths; within the empire they are called dark knights. taking the job requires membership in an imperial faith and suitable admission and training. neither a priest's divine calling nor a paladin's direct divine choice is required. their faith-bound martial station joins heavy training to institutional service and, for those who gain sufficient standing, divine magic. some sincerely embody their patron god's cause; others preserve their position through useful service, outward conformity, and political skill.high follower standing is not required to possess hellion levels or use mundane hellion training. it is required to cast hellion spells and use presence.progression. hellions use shared advancement and the acolyte chassis above. a hellion's ordinary armed and unarmed attack speed is 1 unless a talent, weapon configuration, spell, or other rule changes it.starting packageequipment training. acquiring hellion job level 1 ordinarily grants training with axe, crossbow, dagger, flail, mace, polearm, sling, spear, staff, sword, and unarmed combat. it also grants training with light, medium, and heavy armor and all ordinary shields. culturally restricted, specialist, and item-specific equipment still requires its own training. rifle and siege equipment are not automatic hellion training.apprentice talent access. rescue, hide, and sneak become available for purchase. none are learned automatically.class talentsthe rank table below lists every talent available through the hellion job. complete descriptions and xp costs for generic talents appear in talents and feats. exploit weakness, hellion cleave, and presence remain complete below because they define how the job fights.hellion ranktalent accessapprenticerescue; hide; sneakjourneymanself defense; disarm; enhanced damageveterancombat casting; fast healing; haggle; exploit weaknessexpertsecond attack; endurance; brawlingmentortrance; third attack; hellion cleave; presencemaster—entering master at hellion job level 21 grants divine intervention as described in the acolyte chassis; it is not a purchased talent.class mastery: hellionexploit weakness and hellion cleave form one package and may combine when their requirements are met. neither ability grants the other, and neither places the separately catalogued sweeping slash feats inside hellion mastery. neither may be used during a round already locked to a different class mastery.exploit weakness. exploit weakness is an exclusive veteran talent. immediately before the hellion's first qualifying melee attack of a round, lock or choose class mastery: hellion if the round's mastery has not already been selected.the target must currently suffer an ongoing detrimental condition or penalty imposed by the hellion or one of the hellion's allies. intimidated, poisoned, weakened, blinded, and being overcome by presence are examples. an advantageous circumstance does not qualify merely because it makes the target easier to attack; the detriment must have been imposed. add half the hellion job level, rounded down, to every qualifying melee attack against such a target during that round. the bonus adds no fixed damage, but may increase damage through positive attack margin. later attacks cease to qualify once the target no longer suffers any qualifying imposed detriment.

pages.title: Presence
pages.text: classeshellion61classes · hellionhellion cleave. hellion cleave is an exclusive mentor talent. once per battle, the hellion may declare it for the first attack the hellion makes in that battle. that opening attack must be melee and use a slashing weapon physically capable of severing the target. declaring it selects class mastery: hellion if no mastery is already locked.on a hit, add the hellion job level as fixed raw damage before protection. this addition is not a damage die and is not multiplied by a critical hit. it may combine with exploit weakness when the target qualifies. a target currently overcome by presence uses static defense 10 against hellion cleave.if this attack causes an unprevented mortal wound, the dm may make it a severing injury when the weapon, anatomy, and circumstances make that plausible. preventing the mortal wound prevents the severing result.presencepresence is an exclusive mentor talent. it is a supernatural, divine, mind-affecting aura rather than a class mastery. it requires high follower standing and a conscious, willing hellion.the hellion may assert or suppress presence without using movement, a main action, pe, or me, and the aura has no upkeep cost. while asserted, the patron god's pressure is perceptible around the hellion.when an enemy within 30 feet of the hellion first attempts during its turn to attack the hellion or an ally within 30 feet of the hellion, it makes one will save against the hellion's charisma-based acolyte ability dc. on success, it may attack the protected group normally for the rest of that turn.on failure, the enemy is overcome by presence. the hellion may occupy 2 currently unoccupied concentration. if the hellion does so, the enemy loses the declared attack action, its turn ends, and it cannot attack the hellion or any ally currently within the aura while that concentration remains occupied. it may still take actions that do not attack the protected group. the state continues until the hellion releases that concentration or an ending condition below occurs.if the hellion cannot or will not occupy the concentration, the declared attack proceeds at -4 attack and no continuing overcome state remains. this fallback is momentary hesitation, not shaken, frightened, or panicked.

pages.title: Example: Presence setting up the Hellion Mastery
pages.text: classeshellion62classes · hellionwhen the hellion or one of the hellion's protected allies attacks an enemy overcome by presence, that attack resolves before presence ends, whether it hits or misses. the target defends normally unless the opening attack is the hellion's own hellion cleave; that cleave resolves against static defense 10. presence then ends for that target immediately on the same initiative. being overcome by presence counts as an imposed detriment for exploit weakness until it ends.suppressing the aura, losing consciousness, losing high follower standing, or voluntarily releasing the occupied concentration ends all affected enemies' ongoing presence states and releases concentration occupied by it.example: presence setting up the hellion masterya hellion who has purchased presence, exploit weakness, and hellion cleave has asserted presence before an enemy within 30 feet attempts its first attack of the turn against one of the hellion's allies. the enemy fails its will save. the hellion occupies 2 available concentration, so the declared attack is lost, the enemy's turn ends, and the enemy remains overcome by presence while that concentration is maintained.the hellion has not yet attacked during this battle. on the hellion's turn, the first attack is made with a slashing weapon capable of severing the target, so the hellion declares hellion cleave and selects class mastery: hellion. presence is outside that mastery, but being overcome by presence is an imposed detriment, so exploit weakness also applies. the hellion adds half their job level to the attack roll, and this hellion cleave alone is resolved against static defense 10.the cleave resolves before presence ends. on a hit, hellion cleave adds the hellion's full job level as fixed raw damage before protection. a severing injury remains possible only if the completed attack causes an unprevented mortal wound and the weapon, target, and circumstances make severing plausible. once the cleave resolves, hit or miss, presence ends for that enemy immediately. had the hellion declined or lacked the 2 concentration, the enemy's original attack would instead have proceeded at -4 and no continuing overcome state would have remained.

pages.text: classeshellion63classes · helliondivine spellcastinghellion caster level equals half hellion job level, rounded down. hellion spells use the character's one me pool and the ordinary spell dc. hellions learn eligible spells individually rather than preparing spell slots.a hellion must hold high follower standing in the patron imperial faith to cast hellion spells. losing that standing suspends casting without erasing spells already learned; pages.title: Mage Jobs · Mage Chassis
pages.text: classesmage jobs64classes · mage jobsmage jobsmage chassisthe mage family contains the sorcerer, warlock, and necromancer jobs. all three use the universal base-save cap and mage save costs under shared advancement, together with the mage train caps—including one art train per three mage job levels—and 1 me at every qualifying new overall level.shared metamagic. upon reaching mage job level 10, the character automatically learns one eligible metamagic ability. another is learned at mage job levels 14, 18, 22, 26, and 30. no more than two metamagic abilities may modify the same spell. individual metamagic procedures remain in spells and spellcasting.ritual spell eligibility. every mage job makes the character eligible to learn ritual spells, but grants no ritual automatically. spells and spellcasting gives the general eligibility boundary; each individual ritual supplies its own cost, casting time, participants, prerequisites, circle requirement, and procedure.each mage job has its own spell-circle schedule, equipment training, device access, armor permissions, and curated spell list. this chapter gives the job schedules and permissions. spells and spellcasting contains the spell lists, the complete rules for individual metamagic abilities, the general ritual spell boundary, and individual rituals; talents and feats contains the complete generic talent entries and xp costs.

taking the job later requires the aptitude to be established and follows the ordinary additional-job training procedure.progression. sorcerers use shared advancement and the mage chassis above. a sorcerer's ordinary armed and unarmed attack speed is 1 unless an explicit talent, weapon configuration, spell, or other rule changes it.starting packageequipment training. acquiring sorcerer job level 1 ordinarily grants training with dagger, staff, sling, crossbow, and unarmed combat. it grants no armor or shield training. culturally restricted, specialist, and item-specific equipment still requires its own training.apprentice talent access. wands, staves, and scrolls become available for purchase. none is learned automatically.class talentsthe rank table below lists every talent available through the sorcerer job. complete descriptions and xp costs for generic talents appear in talents and feats. arcane ward and mana shield remain complete below because they define how the sorcerer casts under pressure.sorcerer ranktalent accessapprenticewands; staves; scrollsjourneymanself defenseveterantranceexpertbrew; scribe; lucid dreamingmentorclarity; arcane wardmastermana shieldwands, staves, and scrolls are separate talents. brew and scribe follow the general talent rules in talents and feats. metamagic is absent from this purchased ladder because the mage chassis grants its selections automatically.sorcerer has no class mastery. sorcerer spells, metamagic, ritual spell eligibility, arcane ward, mana shield, and talents remain available during a round in which the character uses another job's class mastery, unless an ability says otherwise.mana shieldmana shield protects the sorcerer only during the interval in which the sorcerer is casting a spell. when the sorcerer would take damage during that interval, resolve applicable damage reduction and any pe mitigation first. before applying the remaining damage, the sorcerer may spend any amount of me; pages.title: Arcane Ward
pages.text: classessorcerer67classes · sorcererarcane wardusing arcane ward takes a main action. the sorcerer creates a visible, stationary arcane glyph filling the sorcerer's current space and hovering just above the supporting surface. it lasts for 1 minute.only the sorcerer who created the ward receives its benefits, and only while standing within it. leaving suspends those benefits; returning before it ends restores them. the glyph does not move with the sorcerer.spells cast from within the ward gain +2 to their spell dc and cost 2 less me, to a minimum cost of 1 me. the sorcerer need not commit concentration to begin one of these spells, but must still occupy and resolve any concentration required to maintain it. damage cannot interrupt a spell the sorcerer is casting from within the ward. the ward does not prevent attacks of opportunity, damage, grappling, forced movement, or any other consequence. the sorcerer may create another arcane ward 1 hour after the previous ward ends.

the spell must still appear on the sorcerer list and be learned normally.at job level 21, the sorcerer has caster level 10 and access through sixth-circle spells. suppose this sorcerer has purchased arcane ward and mana shield. the sorcerer spends a main action creating an arcane ward, then begins casting from inside it on a later turn. a spell that normally costs 5 me costs 3 me inside the ward and gains +2 to its spell dc. any initial concentration requirement is ignored, but concentration required to maintain the spell remains occupied normally.if an attack leaves 4 damage after damage reduction and pe mitigation while the sorcerer is casting, arcane ward prevents that damage from interrupting the spell but does not prevent the damage itself. the sorcerer may spend 4 me through mana shield to prevent all 4 damage. if forced outside the glyph, the ward's benefits are suspended while its duration continues. mana shield may still protect a later casting outside the ward; if it reduces the remaining damage to 0 there, the damage cannot interrupt that spell.related rulesarcane ward and mana shield are fully described in this profile and are listed by reference in talents and feats. that chapter also gives xp costs and complete rules for wands, staves, scrolls, self defense, trance, brew, scribe, lucid dreaming, and clarity. the sorcerer spell list and the other spellcasting rules named above appear in spells and spellcasting.
