pages.text: skillssense motive – additional skills and fields91skills · skill catalogue

pages.title: Talents and Feats · Talents
pages.text: talents and featstalentstalents and featstalents and feats are exceptional abilities learned beyond ordinary skills. ordinary talents are tied to jobs and their rank-access tables. feats are learned separately from job progression. grandmaster talents are the character-wide exceptional advancement available after the level-31 grand master gate and use their own procedure below.talentslearning talentsa talent is an ability made available by a job's rank-access table or by another explicit grant. reaching a listed rank permits the character to buy the talent; it does not grant every talent at that rank automatically.a talent is learned once. access to the same talent through another job does not grant a second copy, and it does not refund xp already spent. a talent creates numbered tiers or another exception only when its own entry explicitly says so.when a character's jobs offer the same talent at different ranks, use the earliest rank the character has already reached. this determines both access and xp price; the character's main job does not matter.earliest unlocked accessxp costapprentice or journeyman5 xpveteran or expert10 xpmentor, master, or champion15 xptalents available through expert rank may be self-trained when the character has the necessary time and opportunity. talents available at mentor rank or later require a willing instructor who knows the talent or is otherwise established as capable of teaching it. there is no single training time that applies to every talent.individual talent entries may impose additional prerequisites or restrictions. job access and xp payment do not waive them. an exclusive talent is available only through the named job unless another rule explicitly grants access.some starting packages or other rules grant a named talent automatically. an automatic grant costs no xp and does not become an additional copy if the character later finds purchase access through another job.grandmaster talentsgrandmaster talents, abbreviated gm talents, do not use the ordinary job-rank price table. a character becomes eligible after one job reaches level 31 and the dm recognizes the character as a grand master.record every gm talent on one character-wide known list. a new gm talent costs 10 xp for each gm talent the character will know after learning it: 10 xp for the first, 20 xp for the second, 30 xp for the third, and so on. every numbered entry is purchased and counted separately. there is no fixed maximum, shared tier sequence, capacity track, or separate grandmaster level.each entry states gm talent requirement: n, meaning the minimum number of other gm talents the character must already know. it also states its own prerequisites and training or achievement gate. gm talents are permanent and are not ordinarily retrained, exchanged, or refunded.the complete current engine and initial nineteen-entry catalogue belong to the separate gm and beyond expansion. the universal session-xp procedure remains dm-facing and is not repeated here.reading a talent entryevery talent entry begins with a classification label:talent identifies a talent whether it is purchased or granted automatically.mastery appears beside talent only when the ability is an explicit member of a class mastery. it does not mean master rank or skill mastery.job feature identifies an automatic job feature included here for discovery. it is not a purchasable talent merely because it appears in this chapter.an entry then gives the jobs that provide access, its xp price or automatic-grant status, any additional prerequisites, and its effect.job-defining abilities are reproduced here from classes. bard entries give each ability's own rules and link to the shared performance rules in classes. teaching examples remain in classes.92talents and feats · talents

pages.title: Talent Catalogue · Alertness
pages.text: talents and featstalent cataloguetalent cataloguealertnesstalentaccess: barbarian xp: 10 xpalertness gives the barbarian a supernatural awareness of danger. the barbarian cannot be surprised or made flat-footed unless the attacker is a rogue whose rogue job level is at least 5 higher than the barbarian's job level, or a scout whose scout job level is at least 5 higher and who uses ambush.when a concealed, potentially dangerous supernatural presence or effect is within 60 feet, the dm secretly makes a wisdom check for the barbarian. success reveals that something is wrong, but not its identity, nature, or location.invisible creatures, unseen magical forces, unnatural conditions, curses, hauntings, and magical traps may trigger this sense. ordinary mundane traps and harmless or beneficial magic do not. the dm determines when the hidden check is made.ambushtalent · masteryaccess: scout xp: 15 xpranged mastery, rapid fire, and ambush form one package. they may work together when their individual requirements are met. selecting another job's class mastery suppresses every scout-mastery benefit for that round. if ranged mastery or ambush first becomes relevant through an opening attack, lock or choose scout mastery immediately before that attack roll. ambush can therefore select scout mastery during round 0. rapid fire cannot operate during round 0 because it requires a full attack.ambush. ambush is a purchased master talent that may be used only on the scout's first attack attempt of a combat. before rolling, the scout may declare it for a ranged attack against a target within 60 feet that cannot perceive or anticipate the scout. add the scout job level to that attack roll. the bonus applies only to that attack and can increase damage only through positive attack margin. it does not apply to a rapid fire attack or another projectile. the opportunity is expended whether the attack hits or misses.scout camouflage can help establish ambush but is not required when the scout is otherwise genuinely unperceived and unanticipated. ambush may initiate combat during round 0 because it is a scout job mastery. the round 0 attack cannot receive the adventurer chassis's once-per-battle damage addition. an otherwise qualifying ambush in round 1 or later may receive that separate addition on its resulting damage roll.arcane wardtalentaccess: sorcerer xp: 15 xpusing arcane ward takes a main action. the sorcerer creates a visible, stationary arcane glyph filling the sorcerer's current space and hovering just above the supporting surface. it lasts for 1 minute.only the sorcerer who created the ward receives its benefits, and only while standing within it. leaving suspends those benefits; returning before it ends restores them. the glyph does not move with the sorcerer.spells cast from within the ward gain +2 to their spell dc and cost 2 less me, to a minimum cost of 1 me. the sorcerer need not commit concentration to begin one of these spells, but must still occupy and resolve any concentration required to maintain it. damage cannot interrupt a spell the sorcerer is casting from within the ward. the ward does not prevent attacks of opportunity, damage, grappling, forced movement, or any other consequence. the sorcerer may create another arcane ward 1 hour after the previous ward ends.aura of negationtalentaccess: barbarian xp: 15 xpafter connecting with a melee attack, the barbarian may spend 2 pe and activate aura of negation as part of that hit. resolve the attack's ordinary damage normally. the barbarian may instead use the main action to touch a willing adjacent creature.record the barbarian's total magic resistance, including trained and equipment magic resistance, then roll percentile dice against it. whether the roll succeeds or fails, the barbarian's magic resistance becomes 0 for 1 minute and then returns normally.on success, every ongoing beneficial or harmful magical effect on the touched creature is dispelled without a separate dispel check. enchanted equipment, permanent item properties, inherent abilities, and effects explicitly impossible to dispel are unaffected.93talents and feats · talent catalogue

pages.title: B Augmented Sixth · Backstab
pages.text: talents and featsb augmented sixth – berserkb augmented sixthtalent · masteryaccess: bard xp: 10 xpeach direct note deals a number of d6 of magical sonic damage equal to half the bard job level, rounded down, with a minimum of 1d6. complete the nominal dice expression, roll no more than four damage dice, and replace each excess die with +2. bard level 30 therefore produces 4d6 + 22, not 15 rolled dice. converted +2 values remain part of the damage-dice subtotal for critical multiplication if an explicit later rule ever permits a critical; the direct notes themselves make no attack roll and cannot critically hit.magic resistance applies. magic protection and worn physical armor's flat dr reduce the damage. direct notes use no penetration / armor grade comparison, attack margin, or critical hit.spend 4 pe and use a main action. every other creature within 120 feet, including allies and enemies but excluding the bard, takes the damage; a successful fortitude save halves it. it does not affect objects unless an explicit rule says otherwise.see classes — bard: shared performance rules.backstabtalent · masteryaccess: rogue xp: 5 xpsneak attack, backstab, hamstring, and dual backstab form one package. they may work together when their individual requirements are met. selecting another job's class mastery suppresses every rogue-mastery benefit for that round. finesse, quick draw, casing, underworld courtesy, skirmish, envenom, and other non-mastery features or talents remain available under their own rules.if sneak attack or backstab first becomes relevant through an opening attack, lock or choose rogue mastery immediately before that attack roll. rogue mastery may therefore be selected during round 0 when one of its abilities is otherwise legal.sneak attack and backstab each grant the same +1 pen increase. these increases do not stack: an attack qualifying for both gains +1 pen total, not +2.backstab. backstab is a purchased apprentice talent that modifies a melee attack made with a short, one-handed piercing weapon, normally a dagger, short sword, rapier, rondel dagger, tanto, or comparable weapon. the target must be genuinely unaware that they are in danger; merely being flat-footed is insufficient.on a successful backstab, add the rogue job level as fixed raw damage before damage reduction. this fixed damage is not multiplied by a critical hit or another dice multiplier. a qualifying backstab gains +1 pen, which does not stack with sneak attack's pen increase. backstab costs no pe, may operate during round 0, and is not automatically lethal damage. it may combine with sneak attack when that attack independently satisfies sneak attack's requirements.bashtalentaccess: mercenary; barbarian xp: 5 xponce per round, the character may spend 2 pe and replace one attack with bash. the attacker makes a roll-under strength check with bab against the defender's choice of a roll-under strength or dexterity check with bab.on success, the defender becomes prone. success by 8 or more also permits the attacker to begin a grapple immediately without another attack or pe cost. the attacker drops held objects, follows the defender down, and continues with the grapple procedure. failure by 8 or more makes the attacker prone.both participants must have their feet on the ground. a one-category creature-size difference grants +4 to the larger participant. bash cannot be used across a difference of two or more size categories. a trained bash failure does not provoke an attack of opportunity.see combat — hard trip and bash for the shared maneuver rules and untrained attempts.berserkjob feature · masterygrant: barbarian xp: noneberserk and fury are mutually exclusive states in one class-mastery package. activating or maintaining either state selects class mastery: barbarian for the round. if another class mastery has already been selected for the round, neither state can be activated during that round. an active berserk or fury must continue selecting barbarian mastery in later rounds. choosing another job's mastery while a state is active ends it immediately and invokes its catch-breath consequence. neither state automatically applies the separate frenzied condition.94talents and feats · b augmented sixth – berserk

pages.title: Blind Fighting
pages.text: talents and featsberserk – blind fightingusing berserk or fury. activating either state uses movement and costs 2 pe. every effect other than fury's attack-speed increase begins immediately. the state remains active through the activation round and for one plus the barbarian's constitution modifier complete rounds afterward, with a minimum of one complete round. after that free duration expires, spend 1 pe at the start of each subsequent round, before that round's attack schedule is established, to continue the state through that round. continuation does not refill temporary hp. neither state can be activated while berserk or fury is already active.when the state ends, the barbarian spends one complete turn catching breath. during that turn the barbarian cannot pages.title: Equipment · Equipment at a Glance
pages.text:
equipmentmoney, markets, and availability
  equipment
  equipment at a glancean equipment profile keeps an item's rules, handling, weight, typical value, and availability together. weapons list damage and armor penetration (pen); armor lists armor grade (grade), damage reduction (dr), and armor hp; shields list the defensive bonuses they provide. pen is compared with grade to determine how much physical armor dr applies, while armor hp increases the wearer's maximum hp rather than measuring the armor's structural durability. typical value is a comparison point, not a guaranteed shop price, and availability shows how readily an item can normally be found. a specific item's entry controls any exception to these general rules.
  money, markets, and availability
  
    silver-equivalent accountingten copper equal one silver, and ten silver equal one gold. equipment uses silver as its ordinary reference value, so prices, treasure, and foreign coins can be compared without requiring players to maintain several parallel accounting systems.
record the mint or origin of a character's money when it matters. the character may still total that money by its silver-equivalent value: a pouch can contain taslamaran crowns or imperial deniers while the character sheet records what the collection is ordinarily worth in silver.
silver-equivalent accounting does not guarantee that every coin will be accepted at that value. a merchant may weigh, discount, exchange, or refuse an unfamiliar or distrusted mint.
as approximate economic comparisons, one copper is about an ordinary laborer's daily earnings, one silver is about a skilled artisan's weekly earnings, and one gold is about ten weeks of skilled work. these are guides to scale, not fixed wages or modern-currency conversions.local currencies and foreign cointhe nations use their own coinage. these names use vanaheim's ordinary ten-to-one accounting ratio.
    nationgold coinsilver coincopper cointaslamarcrownshillingpennycathar-du empireaureusdenieroboluxmalbezantdenierpougeoise
uxmal's gold coinage is commonly considered less valuable because its gold has been debased with copper. this creates distrust rather than a permanent universal conversion: acceptance and discount depend upon the place and time.
zhenshi uses the mon as small coin and the ryō as high-value gold currency. the koku measures rice, income, taxation, and territorial wealth; it is not a coin.typical value and variable pricesan item's typical value is its expected silver-equivalent value under ordinary conditions. it is not a guaranteed shop price.
region, scarcity, war, quality, legality, demand, and coin reputation can change the actual price or make an item unavailable. the dm determines the local result from the situation; there is no universal market-price modifier table.
catalogue values are based on the labor, materials, construction, and availability appropriate to vanaheim.
  
140equipment · money, markets, and availability

pages.title: Availability and Scarcity · Reading Equipment Profiles
pages.text:
equipmentreading equipment profiles
  availability and scarcityequipment can carry one of four availability labels:
common: normally present in ordinary trade where the item is culturally and practically appropriate.limited: obtainable through the right market, craft, supplier, or modest search, but not reliably stocked everywhere.rare: normally requires a specialist source, connection, substantial search, or unusual opportunity.restricted: controlled, prohibited, politically sensitive, or limited to authorized buyers. an item can be restricted without being physically rare.
availability communicates an item's position in the market. it does not establish a public dc, settlement requirement, waiting period, or guarantee of access. when acquisition requires mechanical resolution, the dm may use a private contact, fixer, or fence procedure.
some exceptional armor and shields are marked nationally controlled instead of receiving an ordinary market label. they are priceless for catalogue purposes, have no public typical value, and cannot be acquired merely by offering sufficient silver.
  reading equipment profilesan equipment profile lists the values and exceptions needed to use an item. it does not repeat universal combat procedures, and it does not create a rule from a field that is absent.
  common profile fieldsfieldmeaningitemthe ordinary or proper name of the equipment.categorya formal equipment classification, such as a light, medium, or heavy weapon or armor. a category can establish baseline values and interactions.handlinghow the item is held, worn, carried, mounted, installed, loaded, or activated. weapon profiles use the separate hands field.damagethe item's listed damage dice or other explicit damage value. the complete damage procedure belongs to combat.armor penetration (pen)a weapon or attack's ability to defeat grade-sensitive physical armor.protection valuesarmor grade (grade) measures physical armor resistance; damage reduction (dr) subtracts from applicable damage; armor hit points (armor hp) increase the wearer's maximum hp while worn; a shield bonus contributes to block.range, capacity, and speedeffective range is the distance within which a ranged weapon attacks without a range penalty. capacity records ammunition, charges, fuel, or another finite supply. speed records movement supplied by an item, mount, or vehicle.typical valuethe item's expected value in silver under ordinary conditions, not a guaranteed local selling price.availabilitycommon, limited, rare, or restricted, as defined under money, markets, and availability.weightthe item's weight in pounds. a container's contents add their own weight.requirements and restrictionsconditions that govern who can use the item or how it can be used.propertiesdefined keywords or short item-specific rules that modify the ordinary procedure.
an item lists typical value, availability, and weight when those values are known and relevant. a blank or dash in one of these fields never means that the item is free, unrestricted, or weightless.
141equipment · reading equipment profiles

equipmentcarrying and handling equipment
  equipment categories and propertiesa category is part of the item's basic classification. for example, light, medium, and heavy establish the ordinary starting pen of a weapon and the ordinary starting grade of armor. a category does not automatically determine every other field.
a property is a defined rule attached to a particular item. it can supply special handling, an alternate use, a restriction, or an exception. a property changes only what its text states; its name does not imply additional rules.requirements and restrictionsa requirement identifies something needed for a listed use, such as a minimum ability, training, free hands, ammunition, or a particular situation. a restriction identifies a use that is unavailable, such as a bow that cannot be fired while mounted.
the item entry states the consequence of failing a requirement or meeting a restriction. only the listed consequences apply; an additional penalty or reduced-use option requires an explicit rule.item-specific exceptionsa specific item can override a general rule by stating the exception in its own profile. the exception is narrow: permission to use one bow while mounted does not change other longbows, and a weapon that qualifies for one special maneuver does not grant that qualification to its entire category.
when an item profile and a universal procedure appear to conflict, apply the item text only to the exact value or use it changes. the remaining universal procedure still applies.

pages.title: Readily Accessible Equipment
pages.text:
equipmentcarrying and handling equipment
  
    apply the creature's size multiplier to both values and round fractions down:
sizecarrying multipliertiny×1/4small×1/2medium×1large×2
an explicit creature or mount profile can replace these values. momentary lifting, pushing, dragging, leverage, assistance, terrain, and loads above maximum remain strength checks or dm adjudication rather than another universal table.
an encumbered character takes -2 attack and defense, -2 on reflex saves, and -2 on physical ability, physical skill, and combat-maneuver checks. encumbered does not reduce damage, fortitude saves, will saves, spell dcs, mental or social checks, or speed. it begins and ends immediately as carried weight crosses the threshold.
record equipment weight in pounds. worn armor, weapons, containers, and their contents all count. trivial objects and ordinary pocket money need not be counted individually. track large quantities of coins, ammunition, supplies, treasure, or other small objects when their combined weight becomes meaningful.readily accessible equipmenthalf the character's dexterity score, rounded down, is the practical guideline for how much equipment can be kept readily arranged on the body. treat this as a guideline, not an exact slot limit.
worn clothing and armor do not consume this capacity. weapons, component satchels, potion belts, packs, and comparable arranged equipment do. an ordinary item counts as at least one; a bulky or awkward item may count as two, three, or more at the dm's judgment and never counts as a fraction.
a suitable container counts according to its own bulk rather than making every small object inside it count separately. its contents are stored unless the container explicitly makes a particular item accessible. a backpack can count as more than one.

pages.title: Worn, Stored, and Secured Equipment · Drawing, Stowing, Retrieving, and Dropping Items
pages.text:
equipmentcarrying and handling equipmentworn, stored, and secured equipment
held: the item is already in hand and requires no retrieval.accessible: the item is arranged for immediate retrieval.stored: the item is inside an ordinary pack or container.secured: the item is locked, tied down, buried, or deeply packed. it is normally unavailable during combat without the time or circumstances the dm requires.drawing, stowing, retrieving, and dropping items
bringing one accessible item to hand uses movement and does not itself provoke an attack of opportunity. a character with bab +1 or higher may bring any one accessible item to hand as part of ordinary movement. without bab +1, bringing the item to hand consumes movement and provides no movement through that same allowance.
retrieving a stored item uses the main action and provokes an attack of opportunity while threatened. retrieving a secured item requires whatever additional time or circumstances the dm determines.
dropping an item held in hand is free. sheathing, holstering, or otherwise putting away a weapon uses movement and provokes an attack of opportunity while threatened. an explicit quick draw or item rule can create a narrower exception.144equipment · carrying and handling equipment

pages.title: Weapons · Reading a Weapon Profile
pages.text:
equipmentweapons · reading a weapon profileweapons
a weapon profile supplies the weapon's own dice, classification, handling, reach, and special rules. combat determines the attack roll, defense, margin of success, damage routing, and other universal resolution.
reading a weapon profile
weapon profiles use these fields:
fieldmeaningweaponthe weapon's name.categorylight, medium, or heavy. category establishes the ordinary baseline pen and can matter to explicit abilities.handswhether the weapon requires one hand or two hands for ordinary use.damagethe weapon dice rolled on a hit. combat adds the relevant ability modifier, explicit damage modifiers, and margin of success.penthe weapon's armor penetration. pen is printed explicitly even when it matches the category baseline.critical threatthe natural attack results that can produce a critical hit when the attack connects. 20 means only a natural 20; 19–20 includes either listed result. there is no confirmation roll.reachthe distance at which the weapon can attack and threaten. the entry states whether a reach weapon also threatens adjacent spaces.effective rangethe distance within which a ranged or thrown attack takes no range penalty. combat supplies the far and extreme bands.weightthe weapon's weight in pounds, including an ordinary sheath or scabbard where appropriate and a bow's working string, but excluding ammunition and separate containers.typical valuethe weapon's expected silver-equivalent value under ordinary conditions, not a guaranteed local price.availabilitythe weapon's ordinary market position: common, limited, rare, or restricted.loadingthe action or handling required to ready the weapon's next piece of ammunition.propertiesdefined alternate uses, qualifications, restrictions, or special handling.
critical threat has no multiplier field. a critical hit multiplies the weapon's complete damage-dice subtotal by 2 and adds non-dice modifiers once. complete critical-hit rules appear in combat; the general four-damage-dice rule is taught with damage scaling in spells and spellcasting.145equipment · weapons · reading a weapon profile

pages.title: Light, Medium, and Heavy Weapons · Armor Penetration (Pen)
pages.text:
equipmentweapon categories · one-handed and two-handed uselight, medium, and heavy weapons
light, medium, and heavy are formal weapon categories. their ordinary baseline pen values are:
weapon categorybaseline penlight1medium2heavy3
category and handedness are separate. a non-heavy weapon may still require two hands, and using two hands does not make it heavy. the item's profile supplies both fields. a heavy weapon made for the wielder's size occupies both hands in ordinary use; the weapon-size procedure below can change a wrong-sized weapon's hand requirement without changing its category.
a heavy weapon has no universal attack speed or parry penalty and is not restricted to full attacks. its usual tradeoffs are occupying both hands, its physical bulk, and the inability to use a shield at the same time. only a weapon formally classified as heavy and wielded in both hands qualifies for heavy attack.
armor penetration (pen)
armor penetration, abbreviated pen, measures a weapon's ability to defeat grade-sensitive physical armor. pen does not add directly to attack or damage.
each weapon entry lists its pen. light, medium, and heavy weapons ordinarily begin at pen 1, 2, and 3, but material, enchantment, construction, ammunition, or an explicit property can change the final value. heavy attack adds +1 pen for that attack.
compare final pen against the protection's armor grade using damage reduction, armor penetration, and armor grade in combat. grade-less protection such as energy armor and supernatural dr applies without this comparison unless its own rule says otherwise.one-handed and two-handed weapons
a one-handed weapon occupies one hand. wielding one leaves the other hand available for a shield, item, potion, spell component, or another legal use, but grants no universal numerical bonus.
a two-handed weapon made for the wielder's size requires both hands for ordinary use. it cannot be used at the same time as a shield, and using two hands does not by itself increase pen or make the weapon heavy. a two-handed weapon can make a single attack or a full attack normally. the weapon-size procedure below can change the hand requirement without changing category.
a long or two-handed weapon may be physically impractical in cramped surroundings. this is situational adjudication, not a universal weapon penalty. an explicit technique or item property may provide an exception.
the longsword is a trained exception. untrained two-handed use is medium and pen 2. a trained wielder may use it one-handed as medium and pen 2, or two-handed as heavy and pen 3, permitting heavy attack.
the elven thinblade is a separate exception. it is a medium, one-handed weapon with pen 2. using it in two hands raises its pen to 3, but it remains medium and does not permit heavy attack. the katana does not share either increase: training can permit one-handed use, but it remains medium and pen 2 in either grip.146equipment · weapon categories · one-handed and two-handed use

pages.title: Weapon Size and Oversized Weapons · Damage Dice and the Weapon-Size Progression
pages.text:
equipmentweapon size · damage dice · reachweapon size and oversized weapons
weapon category is not weapon size. light, medium, and heavy describe the weapon's rules category; an unusually large weapon is a separate question.
the core catalogue lists weapons made for medium creatures. a creature can ordinarily use a weapon made for a creature one size category larger or smaller, with the following changes:
a one-handed weapon made one size larger requires two hands. a weapon that already requires two hands becomes unusable unless an explicit ability permits its use.a two-handed weapon made one size smaller can be used in one hand. a one-handed weapon made one size smaller remains one-handed.a wrong-sized weapon applies -2 attack and -2 parry with that weapon. it does not penalize dodge or a shield block.a weapon made for a creature two or more size categories larger or smaller is unusable unless an explicit rule says otherwise.
changing weapon size changes its damage dice and ordinary hand requirement only. it does not automatically change category, pen, critical threat, reach, or eligibility for heavy attack. heavy attack still requires a formally heavy weapon wielded in both hands.
a specially constructed weapon, such as a giant hammer or cleaver, may list exceptional category, pen, reach, requirements, or other properties in its own profile. weapon size has no universal weight formula; use the printed item weight or the dm's ruling when the distinction matters.damage dice and the weapon-size progression
the damage field lists only the weapon dice. resolve ordinary weapon damage as:
weapon dice + relevant ability modifier + explicit damage modifiers + margin of success
use the following table when the same weapon is made for a creature one size category smaller or larger:
one size smallermedium-creature weaponone size larger1d31d41d61d41d61d81d61d82d61d81d102d81d101d123d61d62d42d61d102d63d62d62d83d8
a weapon whose starting dice or scale is absent from this compact table states its final damage in its own item or creature profile. do not extend the table by inference. size changes the weapon dice rather than adding a separate size modifier to damage.
a spell or magical effect uses this progression only when it explicitly changes the weapon's physical size. enlarging or reducing the wielder alone does not resize the wielder's equipment unless the effect says that it does. when both wielder and weapon change size together, the weapon uses its resized dice without becoming wrong-sized for that wielder.reach and threatened areas
a weapon's reach entry states the distance at which it can make its ordinary melee attack. a creature threatens the area it can presently attack in melee.
small and medium creatures ordinarily threaten adjacent spaces out to 5 feet. large creatures ordinarily have 10-foot natural reach, subject to their body shape and statistics. a reach weapon threatens the distance stated by its entry and ordinarily does not threaten adjacent spaces unless the weapon or an explicit ability says otherwise.
creature size, a talent, a spell, or another explicit effect can modify the final threatened area without changing the weapon's listed statistics.147equipment · weapon size · damage dice · reach

pages.title: Weapon Properties and Special Handling
pages.text:
equipmentweapon properties · vorpalweapon properties and special handling
properties record rules that do not belong in the core profile fields. each property must be defined before it is used in the catalogue.
a melee weapon with a thrown mode appears once in the melee catalogue. its property records the thrown effective range and any handling change. a qualification such as suitability for a mounted-charge damage benefit likewise applies only when the weapon or another explicit rule states it.
requirements involving strength, training, bracing, unusual ammunition, restricted grips, or special environments appear in the weapon's properties or dedicated entry. a historical weapon name alone establishes no additional requirement or handling rule.
trip +2 or disarm +2: add +2 to the wielder's adjusted roll-under threshold when using that weapon for the named maneuver. the property does not grant maneuver training or change the maneuver's action cost, pe cost, untrained penalty, or once-per-round limit.brace: when a readied attack with the weapon resolves against a creature charging the wielder and connects, double the weapon's damage dice for that hit. modifiers are not doubled.charge weapon: the weapon qualifies for doubled weapon dice after a straight, clear mounted charge of at least 30 feet. this is separate from the +1 pen applied to every legal mounted charge.thrown: a property such as thrown 20 lets the weapon make a ranged attack with an effective range of 20 feet. each thrown weapon must be brought to hand through the ordinary drawing rules or an explicit quick draw exception.trained: the listed use requires relevant weapon training from a class, ability, instructor, or established character training. it is not a universal feat category.vorpal
vorpal is a magical weapon property, not a material. the weapon retains its underlying material and every modifier supplied by that material. vorpal adds +3 pen to the finished weapon profile after the base weapon and material are resolved.
each vorpal weapon states its own magical attack and damage bonus and its vorpal trigger range. a +3 vorpal weapon has critical threat 17–20; its +3 attack and +3 damage are separate from the vorpal property's +3 pen.
when an attack with that +3 vorpal weapon connects on a natural 17–20, resolve its ordinary critical and then apply one vorpal result:
a medium or smaller creature with a severable head is beheaded.against a large or larger creature, add +50 flat damage to the attack instead of beheading it. this damage is part of the same hit, is not multiplied by the ordinary critical, and then follows the attack's normal protection and damage-routing procedure.a creature without a severable head cannot be beheaded; the vorpal property adds no substitute damage unless its own item entry says otherwise.
when a manufactured weapon successfully parries an attack made with a vorpal weapon or dimensional blade, its wielder makes a reflex save to protect the parrying weapon. no comparison between the two weapons' pen, grade, or material is required to trigger the save.
dimensional blade uses the caster's spell dc. vorpal uses the attacking wielder's standard non-spell dc:
10 + ability modifier governing that attack + half overall level, rounded down + art
resolve a failed save through the parrying weapon's underlying material:
an ordinary, masterwork, silver, cold-iron, or comparable steel weapon becomes broken.a tanso or mithril weapon becomes damaged and takes -2 attack. another failed save under this procedure while it remains so damaged makes it broken.an adamantine weapon is unaffected.
magical enchantment alone grants no material protection. a magical steel weapon remains steel for this procedure.
vorpal does not make the weapon's material irrelevant, grant unlimited pen, or by itself resize the weapon. a protection can name vorpal as an explicit bypass.
example: molydeus guardian axe.148equipment · weapon properties · vorpal

equipmentweapon groupsweapon groups
some abilities, including mercenary weapon mastery, apply to a weapon group. a material, masterwork, enchanted, or national version of a weapon remains part of the base weapon's group and is not listed separately. an alias printed in parentheses likewise uses the same entry. group membership does not itself grant weapon training.
daggers and knives: dagger, kukri, rondel dagger, tanto.
one-handed swords: short sword, arming sword, rapier, scimitar, elven blade, guardless elven blade, elven thinblade, cavalry sabre, katzbalger, longsword, katana, wakizashi, ninjato, parang.
two-handed swords: longsword, katana, falchion, greatsword, claymore, estoc, kriegsmesser, imperial flamberge, nagamaki, nodachi.
one-handed axes: throwing axe, handaxe, battleaxe, masakari.
two-handed axes: greataxe, ono.
sickles and hooked blades: sickle, kama.
one-handed bludgeoning: light mace, light hammer, sap, club, heavy mace, morningstar, warhammer, jitte, tonfa, tessen.
two-handed bludgeoning: quarterstaff, greatclub, goedendag, pole hammer, dai-tsuchi, tetsubo.
picks: light pick, war pick.
flails: flail, heavy flail.
spears and lances: shortspear, trident, longspear, spear, lance, pike, hammer lance, yari.
glaives and polearms: glaive, halberd, ranseur, guisarme, scythe, pollaxe, war bill, naginata, bisento.
whips: whip.
thrown weapons: dart, javelin.
slings: sling.
bows: shortbow, warbow, imperial longbow, daikyu, athani longbow, athani blackbow.
crossbows: light crossbow, heavy crossbow.
unarmed: unarmed attacks and any item whose own rule explicitly treats its attacks as unarmed.
longsword and katana belong to both sword groups. every other weapon listed above belongs to one group.149equipment · weapon groups

useful force against armor without requiring a large swing.sickle. a hooked agricultural blade adapted for close fighting and for catching an opponent's limb or footing.throwing axe. a small axe balanced for use in the hand or at short throwing distance.light hammer. a compact striking hammer that trades cutting damage for concentrated force against armor and may also be thrown.handaxe. a technique.elven thinblade. called simply the thinblade by elves, this narrow sword is designed to pierce heavier armor. it may be driven with both hands for pen 3, but remains medium and does not that concentrates its impact into a narrow point for penetrating armor.katzbalger. a short, broad infantry sword suited to close ranks and cramped fighting.longsword (bastard sword / hand-and-a-half sword). a versatile hand-and-a-half sword supported by an extensive body of guards, grips, thrusts, half-swording techniques, and strikes with the pommel or crossguard. its category and pen depend on pages.title: Armor and Shields · Reading an Armor or Shield Profile
pages.text:
equipmentarmor penalties, requirements, and movementarmor and shields
reading an armor or shield profilearmor remains light, medium, or heavy for training and category-dependent rules. its profile contains the following values:fieldmeaninggradethe armor grade used when an attack's pen is compared with the armor.drthe armor's grade-sensitive physical damage reduction after that comparison.armor hpthe amount the armor adds to the wearer's maximum hp while worn. this represents protected tolerance, not damage to the item.mobilitya penalty imposed where the armor interferes with movement or active physical response.spell failurethe chance that somatic casting fails when the caster's job, faith, talent, or other source does not permit that armor.weightthe armor's weight in pounds.typical valueits ordinary silver-equivalent comparison value, including the complete profile and initial fitting.availabilityits ordinary position in the market; this does not guarantee local access.
nationally controlled exceptional armor and shields deliberately omit typical value. their availability identifies the controlling nation or institution instead of implying an ordinary market.light, medium, and heavy armorlight armor begins at grade 1, medium armor at grade 2, and heavy armor at grade 3. a specific armor can depart from its category baseline without changing category.medium and heavy armor do not universally reduce speed. heavy armor limits an ordinary run to three times speed and retains the established grapple physical energy costs. armor creates no additional universal physical energy cost per round.armor grade (grade)armor grade, abbreviated grade, represents physical armor's resistance to penetration. compare the attack's pen with grade before applying the armor's dr, as described in combat. grade does not add directly to defense or armor hp.damage reductionan armor's dr is the physical damage reduction adjusted by the pen-versus-grade comparison. grade-less protection, such as energy armor or supernatural dr, follows its own flat procedure rather than using the worn armor's grade.armor hit pointsarmor hp increase the wearer's maximum hp while the armor is worn. once added, those points belong to the same pool as hp from jobs, training, and other sources: damage and healing do not track them separately. they are not structural damage to the armor.armor penalties, requirements, and movementmobility applies to dodge, reflex saves, the initial grab attack, and physical movement or dexterity-based checks when the armor materially interferes. it does not reduce ordinary speed.164equipment · armor penalties, requirements, and movement

pages.title: Armor Fitting, Donning, and Removal · Shields and Shield Bonuses
pages.text:
equipmentarmor and shield cataloguearmor training can come from a job, talent, faith, or instruction received in play. an untrained wearer doubles the armor's mobility penalty and applies that resulting penalty to attack and every active defense: dodge, parry, and block. the armor still supplies its grade, dr, and armor hp.spell failure applies when the character's casting source does not permit somatic casting in the worn armor. whether a particular job, faith, talent, or other source waives it belongs to that source. when spell failure occurs, the spell expends its magical energy and is lost.one worn armor profile supplies grade, dr, armor hp, mobility, and spell failure. its ordinary padding, mail joints, helmet, gauntlets, and other integrated components are already represented. multiple armor profiles do not stack unless an explicit item says otherwise.an armor profile assumes its ordinary head protection. a restrictive closed helmet gives -2 to sight- and hearing-based perception while closed. opening, closing, putting on, or removing that restrictive portion uses movement. helmets use no separate grade, dr, armor hp, hit-location, or called-shot-to-the-head rules.
armor fitting, donning, and removalarmor is fitted to its intended wearer. when an armor has a typical value, that value includes its complete listed profile and initial fitting. flexible armor may sometimes transfer between wearers of sufficiently similar build, at the dm's discretion. rigid or articulated armor—especially breastplates and plate harnesses—must be properly refitted before it provides its full listed profile to a different wearer. refitting time and cost depend on the item and circumstances; there is no universal refitting percentage or ill-fitting-armor penalty table.the following donning times assume a trained wearer and ordinary circumstances:armor categorydonremovelight1 minute1 minutemedium4 minutes1 minuteheavy10 minutes2 minutes
there is no separate hastily-donned procedure. assistance, unfamiliar armor, and exceptional circumstances remain subject to the dm.shields and shield bonusesa carried shield supplies its listed bonus to block and permits a separate base block use. projectile block is the shield's total block bonus against ordinary arrows, bolts, and similar projectiles; it replaces the normal shield bonus for that defense.add applicable bonuses from training, materials, and magical accuracy once each. a material bonus already included in a finished shield profile is not added again.a shield's reflex bonus applies when the wielder can reasonably interpose it against a directional effect. this does not spend a block use and provides no benefit when the shield cannot protect the wielder from that effect.a shield's printed mobility penalty follows the same application areas as armor mobility while the shield is carried.shields provide no inherent grade, dr, or armor hp and grant no universal shield-bash attack. a feat, talent, spell, or explicit item can create an exception. readying or removing a shield uses movement.shields may receive permanent improvements through the enchant and consecrate spell families. the individual spell determines the available benefits and how they apply.armor and shield catalogue165equipment · armor and shield catalogue

pages.text: equipmentadamantitethe dr added by mithril or adamantite becomes part of the armor's listed grade-sensitive dr. it is not a separate flat dr source. material bonuses do not change the item's light, medium, or heavy category.mithril and adamantite bonuses continue functioning in an antimagic field and are not dispellable magical bonuses. for a protection requiring a minimum weapon rating, a mithril weapon counts as +2 and an adamantine weapon as +3. this intrinsic weapon rating is separate from the enhancement bonus type used for attributes.an item's base profile, material, and successful permanent magical improvements form its finished statistics. apply each component once; a finished catalogue profile already includes its listed material and quality. an enchantment that permanently improves an item increases that recorded value, subject to its own procedure and limits.mithril weapons receive no direct damage bonus, although their +2 attack can increase damage through margin of success. adamantine weapons receive both the indirect benefit of +3 attack and their explicit +3 damage modifier.when a generic mithril armor requires calculation, increase armor hp by 20% and round the final armor hp to the nearest whole number. finished catalogue entries already include that increase.weapon and armor material comparisonsmaterial weaknessessilver and cold iron reduce the ordinary weapon profile's pen by 1, to a minimum of pen 0. they change neither category nor damage dice.elves, dark elves, and sprites possess cold-iron weakness. werewolves and creatures whose profiles identify the weakness possess silver weakness.when the appropriate material hits a creature weak to it:ignore any protection whose own rule names that material as its bypass.apply every other relevant dr normally.add half the remaining damage, rounding down.apply eligible physical energy mitigation.route the remainder through hp and lp normally.if dr reduces the damage to 0, the weakness creates no damage. other explicit material weaknesses can use the same procedure.tanso steeltanso is a refined vanaheim crucible steel. it is more homogeneous, lighter, and more durable than ordinary steel and accepts enchantment readily.tanso equipment is frequently masterwork, but the material does not automatically confer that quality. its increased physical durability can matter when exceptional harm threatens the item; tanso otherwise uses the normal damaged and broken rules.mithrilmithril is well suited to fine edges, flexible armor, and curved weapons. a functional mithril item requires specialized tools, furnaces, and exceptional skill; producing one ordinarily takes about twice the work of a comparable steel item. the extra work affects value and availability but sets no fixed crafting time.mithril shields gain +2 block and +2 projectile block. they weigh half as much as ordinary shields and, because they are automatically masterwork, improve mobility by 1 toward 0. mithril grants no additional reflex bonus.adamantiteadamantite requires extraordinary heat comparable to an arc furnace. losache keep and major dwarven forges can produce it repeatedly at their limited scale. exceptional elven magic may create the necessary conditions for an individual work without creating an ordinary production industry.adamantine armor retains ordinary weight because the finished harness uses less material to achieve its protection. adamantine shields gain +3 block and +3 projectile block. they retain ordinary weight and mobility. adamantite grants no additional reflex bonus.173equipment · adamantite

pages.title: Item Quality · Energy Armor, Supernatural DR, and Special Construction
pages.text: equipmentenergy armor, supernatural dr, and special constructionadamantite is not ordinarily destructible through direct destruction, disintegration, or material-transformation magic. unless an effect explicitly overrides this protection, an effect that would destroy or transform an ordinary item instead damages only an adamantine surface layer and cannot make the item broken. such an effect can still affect an unprotected creature within adamantine armor when the creature is independently a legal target.crystalbrittle supplies one explicit implementation: it forms a brittle crystalline coating and applies one nonstacking damaged result without transforming, breaking, killing, or destroying the adamantite subject. disintegrate supplies the other current implementation: it can destroy a legal creature target inside adamantine armor, but the adamantine item receives only one nonstacking damaged result and cannot become broken or be destroyed without a more specific explicit override.the armor catalogue above already includes the final grade, dr, armor hp, mobility, and weight of each finished exceptional-material armor. the general adjustments remain available for unusual or unique equipment, but players need not calculate percentages during ordinary equipment selection.item qualitymasterwork describes exceptional steel or tanso-steel construction. it is a material quality rather than a magical enhancement.producing such an item requires skill mastery in the applicable craft field. the mastery permits the attempt; the work still requires appropriate materials, tools, facilities, and time, and an ordinary craft check resolves uncertainty.a masterwork weapon gains +1 attack. it gains no separate damage bonus, though attack margin may increase.masterwork armor improves mobility by 1 toward 0.a masterwork shield improves mobility by 1 toward 0. masterwork quality by itself grants no additional block, projectile block, or reflex bonus.masterwork quality does not alter pen, grade, dr, armor hp, damage dice, or weight.mithril and adamantine items automatically count as masterwork. when the material rules specify an attack or mobility result, that result already includes or overrides masterwork quality and does not stack with the ordinary adjustment. mithril armor therefore improves mobility by 2 total, while a mithril shield uses the stated one-point improvement. adamantine armor and shields receive no mobility improvement.working mithril or adamantite requires the relevant craft skill mastery in addition to every material-specific requirement. mastery alone does not grant access to either material.use ten times the comparable ordinary item's typical value as the normal comparison point for a functional masterwork steel or tanso-steel item. this is a reference for commissioning exceptional work, not a guaranteed quote or access to a willing craftsperson. a famous maker, political access, unusual commission, elaborate decoration, collector provenance, or court prestige can raise the actual price to one hundred times ordinary value or more. expense beyond the functional masterwork reference provides no further mechanical benefit unless the item explicitly says otherwise.rare materials, exceptional construction, and special facilities can increase the price beyond the functional masterwork benchmark when an item participates in ordinary commerce. if a finished item has an ordinary market value, its entry lists that final typical value; do not multiply an already finished masterwork or exceptional-material value again. nationally controlled exceptional armor and shields have no public typical value and cannot be priced from this benchmark.energy armor, supernatural dr, and special constructionenergy armor and supernatural dr are grade-less special protections, not materials in the ordinary hierarchy. their listed dr applies flat without comparing pen and grade. material and other pen bonuses grant no special bypass unless the protection explicitly says otherwise.energy armor can be carried by a flexible garment while still applying its printed flat dr; damage that exceeds the protection still reaches the wearer. armor made from supernatural hides, dragon scales, or comparable substances uses the explicit profile created for that item. exceptional thresholds, immunities, and unusual construction belong to that profile rather than a universal material formula.skinning governs recovering monster hides with their exceptional protective properties intact and preserving those properties through crafting. ordinary collection of scales or other material does not itself retain the creature's supernatural dr. the finished item still uses its own protection profile.174equipment · energy armor, supernatural dr, and special construction

pages.title: Damaged and Broken Equipment
pages.text: equipmentdamaged and broken equipmentexceptional elven, dwarven, mithril, and adamantine armor and shields are nationally controlled and have no public typical value. other unusual constructions use their own entries. weapon and ammunition weights and values appear in their catalogue rows.damaged and broken equipmentequipment does not normally degrade through ordinary use. when an exceptional area effect or a severe material mismatch threatens an item being carried, worn, or wielded, the dm may require the character to make a saving throw, usually reflex, to protect it. material, construction, the effect, and the circumstances determine whether a save is required and its dc.on a failure, the item may become damaged. the dm chooses the affected function; a -2 or -4 penalty to one or more relevant item statistics is typical. record separate instances of damage when the dm applies them. there is no fixed number of damaged results before an item fails. when the dm judges that the accumulated damage or event has made the item nonfunctional, it becomes broken and cannot be used for its ordinary purpose.there is no general sunder action. a deliberate attempt to break an item is resolved by the dm or by the explicit rule that permits it.175equipment · damaged and broken equipment

pages.title: Combat · Combat at a Glance
pages.text:
combatcombat at a glance
combatcombat at a glancevalues used in combatthis section is a map of the combat system. the later sections supply the complete procedures and exceptions.ability modifierthe modifier derived from an ability score. combat formulas use the modifier unless a rule explicitly calls for the full score or a roll-under ability check.main job and job leveleach job keeps its own level. the highest-level job is the main job; if several are tied, the one acquired first remains main. an ability tied to a particular job uses the level of the job that granted it.base attack bonus (bab)the character's core combat bonus. bab contributes to attack, dodge, parry, block, and many combat maneuvers.initiative1d20 + dexterity modifier + explicit initiative modifiers. initiative establishes the order in which combatants act.round and initiative passa round contains one or more sweeps through initiative order. the first sweep is the first initiative pass; later passes resolve additional attacks. spells complete at their scheduled initiative values.movement and main actionseparate allowances normally used on the first pass. a main action may be a single attack, full attack, spell, or another legal action.primary attackyour character's primary method of attacking. choose it when declaring a full attack; it supplies that full attack's ordinary attacks. unless stated otherwise, attack speed increases apply to the primary attack.attack speedthe number of attack passes supplied by the primary attack during a full attack. fractional speeds alternate between a higher and lower round, beginning every combat with the higher round.single attack and full attacka single attack uses the main action for one attack. when declaring a full attack, choose its primary attack and optional abilities; the resulting attacks form its schedule. the full attack spends 1 pe and ordinarily resolves no more than five attacks.attack and defensethe attacker rolls against the defender's declared dodge, parry, or block. the defender may instead use passive defense: 10 + bab + applicable passive magical defensive modifiers. the choice is made before either combat roll. an attack that meets or exceeds defense connects.margin of successattack - defense. a tied result hits with margin 0. a positive margin is added to damage.armor penetration (pen) and armor grade (grade)pen measures an attack's ability to defeat physical armor. grade measures how difficult that armor is to defeat. for armor with a grade, compare them to determine how much of its listed dr applies.damage reduction (dr)protection subtracted from damage before physical energy mitigation and before damage reaches hit points or life points.hit points (hp) and life points (lp)hp are one protective pool increased by jobs, training, worn armor, and other effects. temporary hp is separate only when its source says so. lp represent bodily survival. ordinary damage depletes hp before reaching lp.physical energy (pe) and magical energy (me)pe pays for strenuous physical options, including a full attack. me pays spell costs. neither pool may be spent for a purpose unless a rule permits it.
186combat · combat at a glance

pages.title: The Combat Sequence
pages.text:
combatcombat at a glance
arta trained value added to every difficulty class the character creates.saving throw and difficulty class (dc)a save is 1d20 + base save + governing ability modifier + explicit bonuses against the effect's dc. meeting the dc succeeds; the effect states what success accomplishes.roll-under and opposed checksroll 1d20 equal to or below the adjusted threshold. check margin is threshold - roll. when a combat procedure opposes two such checks, compare check margins and favor the defender on a tie.advantage, disadvantage, and rerollsadvantage rolls 2d20 and keeps the higher die; disadvantage keeps the lower. sources cancel one for one, and any remainder applies only once. a reroll normally replaces one die; a luck reroll keeps the more favorable original or revised result.spell speedthe delay between beginning a spell and its completion. spell completion is scheduled within the initiative countdown independently of attack speed.surprised and flat-footeda surprised creature is genuinely unaware of an attack or danger. a flat-footed creature has become aware too late for a complete defensive response. both use restricted static defenses described under beginning combat.domain rankthe d/c/b/a/aa/s scale of the value governing an offense, defense, check, or other opposed effect. rank gaps add their own modifier without changing the underlying statistic or its ordinary modifier; the complete procedure appears under power scale and domain ranks.the combat sequenceuse this sequence for an ordinary encounter:begin combat. a hostile action starts mechanical combat. the dm determines who is involved, who perceives the danger, and who is surprised or flat-footed.roll initiative. every current participant rolls initiative. a character drawn into combat during a round rolls to enter on the next round.resolve round 0 when needed. eligible aware creatures receive either movement or one main action that is not a full attack. if everyone expected the fight, begin with round 1 instead.establish current attack modifiers. apply any attack-speed changes that begin this round. when a character declares a full attack, choose its primary attack and optional additions, then establish that full attack's exact schedule.resolve the first initiative pass. act from highest initiative to lowest. each combatant may use movement and one main action, subject to conditions and other restrictions. a full attack costs 1 pe and begins its sequence of attacks. a maneuver may replace the main action or an attack only when its own procedure permits it.resolve each attack. declare the target and attack. the defender declares a legal active defense or passive defense. roll attack and any active defense, calculate margin of success on a hit, and calculate raw damage. compare pen with grade when the armor has a grade, apply the resulting dr and any flat dr, apply eligible pe mitigation, then route the remainder through hp and lp.resolve later passes. return to the top of initiative for combatants with unresolved full-attack passes. later passes normally grant no movement or unrestricted main action. resolve scheduled spell completions at their proper initiative values.end the round. after every attack pass and scheduled completion has resolved, apply anything timed for the end of a turn or round. begin the next round and advance any fractional attack speed schedule.
187combat · combat at a glance

pages.title: Example: One Complete Ordinary Combat Round
pages.text:
combatcombat at a glance
example: one complete ordinary combat rounda mercenary and a guard expect a fight, so there is no round 0. the mercenary has initiative 17, attack speed 1.5, strength modifier +3, and a medium 1d8 sword with pen 2. the guard has initiative 12, attack speed 1, a sword and shield, medium armor with grade 2, dr 2, and armor hp 6, and 8 hp before armor. the worn armor therefore raises the guard's maximum hp to 14.first pass, initiative 17. the mercenary moves 20 feet into reach, declares a full attack, and spends 1 pe. because this is the first round of combat, attack speed 1.5 provides two attack passes. the guard declares dodge before the dice are rolled.the mercenary's attack total is 24 and the guard's dodge is 20. the attack connects with margin 4. the sword rolls 5 damage, producing 5 + 3 strength + 4 margin = 12 raw damage. pen 2 equals grade 2, so the armor's normal dr 2 reduces this to 10. the damage reduces the guard's 14 hp to 4 hp. the armor hp is part of that same hp total rather than a separately tracked damage pool.first pass, initiative 12. the guard uses the main action for one attack. the mercenary declares parry. the guard's attack is 18 and the mercenary's parry is 21, so the attack misses.second pass, initiative 17. only the mercenary has another attack pass. no ordinary movement is available. the guard declares block. attack and block both total 20, so the attack connects with margin 0. the sword rolls 4, producing 4 + 3 strength + 0 margin = 7 raw damage. dr 2 reduces this to 5. the guard's remaining 4 hp are removed and the final 1 damage reaches lp.no other combatant has an attack pass or scheduled completion, so the round ends. in round 2, the lower side of the mercenary's attack speed 1.5 schedule provides one attack pass.
188combat · combat at a glance

pages.title: Beginning Combat · When Combat Begins and Who Participates
pages.text:
combatbeginning combat
beginning combatcombat begins when a hostile situation enters structured rounds. awareness determines who can act during the opening moments and what defenses are available before everyone can respond normally.when combat begins and who participatesinitiative begins when someone declares or begins an action that starts mechanical combat. tension, threats, visible weapons, nearby danger, or the dm's private knowledge of an enemy do not place the table into combat by themselves.the initiating action does not need to inflict damage. during a hostile confrontation, casting an overt spell, activating a protective effect, making a threatening movement, or taking a similar action may be enough. the dm decides whether the action begins combat from the circumstances.use the following order:declare the initiating action.determine each creature's awareness and whether anyone is surprised.identify the creatures currently involved.roll initiative before resolving the initiating action.resolve surprise round 0 if one is required; otherwise begin round 1.every creature the dm considers part of the initial hostile exchange rolls initiative, including a creature that is surprised. when everyone involved understands that violence is beginning, skip round 0 and begin round 1. combatants who have exchanged threats, approached with weapons, formed battle lines, or otherwise expected the fight defend normally from the opening attack. losing initiative in an expected confrontation does not by itself make a creature flat-footed.an attack prepared before initiative is not a readied action and does not grant a free attack before combat. everyone currently involved still rolls initiative. credible preparation may receive a situational initiative bonus or lead the dm to resolve the opening through round 0. when the prepared attack occurs, it uses the attacker's normal main action.awareness and surprisethe dm determines awareness separately for each creature. perception, concealment, deception, stealth, speed, preparation, and the surrounding circumstances may call for checks, but there is no universal surprise roll.use the following awareness ladder:a creature that cannot perceive the hostile creature, attack, or danger at all is surprised.a creature that knows an unseen attacker is present but cannot locate or anticipate that attacker is flat-footed against that attacker.a creature that can perceive, locate, or otherwise anticipate an attacker is neither surprised nor flat-footed merely because it cannot see the attacker.invisibility and blindness do not determine awareness automatically. sound, movement, behavior, special senses, blind fighting, and the circumstances determine what a creature can perceive or anticipate.

pages.title: Surprise Round 0 · Surprised, Flat-Footed, and Unseen Attackers
pages.text:
combatbeginning combat
a blinded creature is therefore surprised only by a danger it cannot perceive, rather than by every attack.surprise round 0if at least one current participant is aware of the opposition while another is genuinely unaware, resolve a special surprise round 0 before round 1.round 0 is a brief reaction phase, commonly representing only two or three seconds. only creatures aware enough to participate may act, in initiative order. each eligible creature receives either:its movement; orone main action that is not a full attack.the creature never receives both. it may make one weapon attack, begin casting a spell, give a meaningful warning or order, or perform another legal single action. round 0 never grants a full attack, additional attack passes, or an additional action from haste.brief speech directly accompanying an action may be free. a warning, order, or other communication that gives someone usable information consumes the round 0 action.drawing or readying an ordinary accessible weapon uses the creature's movement. the creature can draw and attack during round 0 only when an explicit quick draw permission applies to that weapon.a spell begun during round 0 spends its full magical energy (me) and follows its normal spell speed. only eligible round 0 participants take actions while the countdown advances. a numeric spell speed can continue below initiative 0 and still complete during round 0; a casting time measured in full rounds or longer units may continue into round 1 or later according to the spell.the once-per-battle abilities granted by the warrior and adventurer chassis are unavailable during round 0. they become available when round 1 begins.round 0 is separate from round 1. it does not consume the front-loaded round of a fractional attack speed schedule. when round 1 begins, per-round dodge, parry, block, and attack-of-opportunity allowances refresh even if they were used during round 0.surprised, flat-footed, and unseen attackerssurprised means that a creature is genuinely unaware of an attacker or danger. a surprised creature receives no movement or main action during round 0.against an attack it has not perceived, the creature cannot choose or roll an active dodge, parry, or block. its defense is:10 + base attack bonus (bab) + applicable passive magical defensive modifiersthe creature rolls no d20 and receives no dexterity modifier. it cannot spend physical energy (pe) to improve this defense, suppress a defensive penalty, restore dexterity, gain a defense roll, or remove the static restriction. after being hit, it may still use any otherwise eligible pe option that reduces damage or prevents a mortal wound.surprise can continue after round 0 if the creature still has not perceived the danger. once it becomes aware but has not yet taken its first action, it is normally flat-footed instead.flat-footed means that a creature has become aware too late to make a complete defensive response. a creature that detects a sudden, concealed, or unexpectedly fast hostile action can avoid being surprised but remain flat-footed if the attacker acts before it. this state normally ends when the creature takes its first action.a flat-footed creature may choose an otherwise legal dodge, parry, or block, but resolves it as a static defense:10 + bab + applicable bonuses for the chosen defense + applicable magical defensive modifiersthe creature rolls no d20 and adds no dexterity modifier. parry may retain applicable weapon or strength-based bonuses, block may retain applicable shield bonuses, and dodge retains only applicable non-dexterity bonuses. a chosen static dodge, parry, or block still consumes one use of that defense.a flat-footed creature cannot make attacks of opportunity unless an explicit ability permits it. it cannot spend pe to improve the static defense or suppress another defensive penalty, although otherwise eligible post-hit damage-mitigation and survival options remain available.

pages.title: Joining Combat and Giving Warnings
pages.text:
combatbeginning combat
when a creature knows an unseen attacker is present but cannot locate or anticipate that attacker, it remains flat-footed against that attacker for as long as the attacker remains unlocatable and unanticipatable. taking an unrelated action does not end this attacker-specific state.uncanny dodge prevents ordinary surprise or acting later in an unexpected opening from making the character flat-footed. the character retains dexterity, may roll an otherwise legal active defense, and may make otherwise legal attacks of opportunity before taking a first action. a genuinely unaware character remains surprised and receives no round 0 action; uncanny dodge supplies only the involuntary defensive response. it does not create awareness, and blindness or other applicable sensory penalties still apply.if flat-footed overlaps the static parry or block restriction caused by an attacker at least five experience levels higher or two size categories larger, use the stricter defense:10 + bab + applicable passive magical defensive modifiersneither surprise nor flat-footed automatically makes an attack a critical hit or lethal damage.joining combat and giving warningsa creature that is completely unaware and not yet involved does not roll initiative merely because combat is occurring elsewhere. it rolls when it is alerted, directly attacked, or otherwise drawn into the encounter.round 0 does not automatically alert everyone nearby. sleeping creatures, distracted bystanders, and creatures unable to perceive a concealed attack may remain unaware after it ends.a meaningful warning or order can alert such a creature and bring it into initiative. during round 0, that warning consumes the speaker's action. it does not grant the newly alerted creature an action during the round 0 already in progress. a creature made aware during a round rolls initiative to enter combat in the next round.

pages.title: Initiative, Rounds, and Attack Speed · Initiative and Ties
pages.text:
combatinitiative, rounds, and attack speed
initiative, rounds, and attack speedinitiative establishes when creatures act. initiative passes distribute repeated attacks through the round, while spell speed schedules spell completion independently of those passes.initiative and tieswhen combat begins, every current participant rolls:1d20 + dexterity modifier + explicit initiative modifiersthe total establishes initiative order for the encounter. strength does not affect initiative. an explicit feat, talent, spell, item, or circumstance may still modify the roll according to its own text.when initiative totals tie, the creature with the higher initiative modifier acts first. if both the total and modifier remain tied, allied creatures may choose their order. opponents and other non-cooperating creatures act simultaneously; neither action preempts the other.rounds and initiative passescombat proceeds in rounds. an initiative pass is one sweep through the initiative order, from highest to lowest.every participant receives a first initiative pass in an ordinary round. after all first-pass actions resolve, participants entitled to another attack pass act again in initiative order. continue through the third, fourth, and later passes until nobody has another pass.attacks made on separate passes resolve sequentially. they do not become simultaneous merely because they belong to the same character's full attack.ordinary movement and the main action begin on the first pass. later passes normally supply the remaining attacks of a full attack. they are not additional unrestricted turns, although an explicit rule may replace an attack or permit another use.resolve every numeric spell speed completion scheduled during the current pass before beginning the next initiative pass. do not begin the next round until every attack pass and every numeric completion scheduled for the current round has resolved.
192combat · initiative, rounds, and attack speed

pages.title: Attack Speed and Primary Attacks · Example: Mercenary and Swashbuckler Attack Speed
pages.text:
combatinitiative, rounds, and attack speed
attack speed and primary attacksyour character's primary attack is their primary method of attacking. choose it when declaring a full attack; it supplies that full attack's ordinary attacks. unless stated otherwise, attack-speed increases supply attacks only with the primary attack.when declaring a full attack, choose its primary attack and any optional abilities you will use. the resulting attacks form that full attack's schedule.a whole-number attack speed grants that many attack passes every round. a half-step alternates between a higher and lower round. attack speed 1.5 follows 2, 1, 2, 1...; attack speed 2.5 follows 3, 2, 3, 2.... every combat begins with the higher number.a fractional cycle advances at the end of every combat round, even when the character makes no full attack during that round. final attack speed cannot be reduced below 1.an attack-speed increase granted by a particular weapon applies only to attacks made with that weapon. a generally applicable attack-speed increase applies to the primary attack unless a rule permits another allocation.an attack-speed change takes effect at the start of the next round. if the new value is fractional, that round begins with the higher number.a full attack can contain no more than five attacks in one round unless an effect explicitly raises that limit.example: mercenary and swashbuckler attack speedmercenary. a mercenary wielding a two-handed mastered weapon begins with attack speed 1. second attack raises it to 1.5, third attack raises it to 2, and weapon mastery iii raises it to 2.5. the mercenary therefore makes three attacks in the first round, two in the second, then repeats that cycle. every attack uses the two-handed primary attack.swashbuckler. a swashbuckler with dual wield makes one primary and one offhand attack in each paired pass. second attack grants a second paired pass, producing four attacks each round. at full greased lightning buildup, the swashbuckler gains one additional unpaired attack and reaches five attacks.spell speed and scheduled completionspell speed is a delay measured down the initiative count. it is not an attack pass.calculate the completion count when casting begins:completion count = initiative count when casting begins - spell speedall ordinary actions assigned to the completion count finish before the spell resolves. the spell takes effect at the end of that initiative number. if several spells complete on the same count, they resolve simultaneously and all their effects occur; one does not preempt another merely because it is narrated first.a numeric spell speed can continue below initiative 0 without entering another round. count every integer, including initiative numbers on which no creature acts. casting times written in full rounds, minutes, hours, or another unit follow their stated duration instead.the caster pays the spell's full magical energy when casting begins, and the spell remains in progress until it completes. spellcasting in combat governs interruption, failed spells, and invalid targets.example: spell speed across initiative countsa speed 3 spell begun at initiative 25 is scheduled for initiative 22. every ordinary action at 22 resolves first, then the spell completes at the end of that count. a speed 2 spell begun at initiative 24 also completes at the end of 22, so both spells resolve simultaneously. if a speed 30 spell begins at initiative 5, it completes at initiative -25 during the same round; passing initiative 0 does not move a numeric spell speed into the next round.delay, ready, and pre-combat preparationwaiting and delay. when the character's first initiative pass arrives, the character may delay the entire turn instead of acting and re-enter later in the initiative order. individual later attack passes cannot be delayed separately. delay cannot interrupt an action already in progress. once the character acts, that later position becomes the character's initiative for the rest of the encounter.
