pages.title: Page 194
pages.text:
combatinitiative, rounds, and attack speed
delay never grants an additional turn. if the character delays into the next round and acts before the former initiative position returns, that delayed action is the character's turn for the new round.ready. a character may ready only after initiative has begun. ready consumes the main action and prepares one eligible main action against an observable trigger. the character must state both the prepared action and its trigger. one weapon attack, beginning a spell, or another eligible main action may be prepared; a full attack cannot be readied.if the trigger occurs before the character's next turn, the prepared action begins immediately before the triggering action. the triggering creature resumes afterward if still able. resolving the readied action moves the readying character's initiative immediately before the triggering creature for the rest of the encounter. if the trigger does not occur before the character's next turn, the prepared action is lost.a readied action retains all its ordinary costs, risks, and consequences. it may still provoke an attack of opportunity. ready grants no separate movement.readied spells. a readied spell is not cast in advance and held. casting begins when the trigger occurs: the caster pays its magical energy and starts its normal spell speed countdown. the casting begins before the triggering action, but a spell with nonzero spell speed may finish after that action and other later events.preparation before initiative. an attack or action prepared before combat is not a readied action and grants no automatic free action before initiative. current participants still roll initiative. credible preparation may receive a situational initiative bonus or affect whether surprise round 0 occurs, as decided by the dm. when the prepared action occurs, it consumes the character's normal main action.drawing or bringing a weapon to hand is equipment handling, not the formal ready action described here.if delay or ready changes the initiative of a character who shared an initiative position through a formation or group rule, that character leaves the former shared position.

pages.title: Actions in Combat · Movement and Main Actions
pages.text:
combatactions in combat
actions in combateach character normally receives one movement and one main action each round. movement determines whether the character moves or handles equipment. the main action determines what the character does: make a single attack, begin a full attack, cast a spell, or perform another legal action. additional initiative passes from attack speed belong to the same full attack; they are not additional unrestricted turns.movement and main actionsmovement and the main action are separate allowances. movement does not consume an attack, and using the main action does not ordinarily consume movement.a single attack, a full attack, spellcasting, and other ordinary main actions are alternatives. choosing one gives up the others unless an explicit rule permits a combination.movement and the main action normally begin during the character's first initiative pass. later passes provide only the unresolved attacks of a full attack or another use explicitly permitted during an attack pass.physical energy costs and reaching zerophysical energy cannot fall below 0. a character may use an action, maneuver, response, or ability with a pe cost only when able to pay the full cost.add together every pe cost within the same action or sequence. for example, a full attack containing hard trip costs 1 pe for the full attack and 2 pe for hard trip, for a total of 3 pe. there is no general limit on how much pe a character may spend during one round.an action that spends the character's final pe resolves completely. immediately afterward, the character becomes exhausted. if that action is a full attack, its continuing sequence resolves normally unless something else interrupts it; exhausted begins when that sequence ends.exhausted sets and locks pe at 0. each round, the character may take either half movement or one main action, never both. that main action may be one ordinary attack, a spell, or another action that costs no pe; it cannot be a full attack. the character cannot run, charge, or use any pe-costing option, and takes -6

combatactions in combat
to attack rolls, defense rolls, saving throws, skill checks, and ability checks. defenses and reactions remain available when they require no pe. recovery from exhausted is explained under combat conditions and recovery and aftermath.a character may spend 1 pe to ignore one chosen negative numeric modifier for one parry, block, dodge, comparable physical defense, fortitude save, or reflex save. this can be used only once on a given roll, does not suppress any other penalty, and does not remove the source or duration of the chosen modifier. it cannot be used on a will save, attack roll, or unrelated check. a surprised or flat-footed character cannot use it on the defense affected by that state; it cannot restore dexterity or permit an active defense where a static defense is required.single attacks and full attacksa single attack uses the main action to make exactly one attack, regardless of the character's attack speed. a single attack has no general pe cost.a full attack is a main action that resolves every attack in the character's current full-attack schedule, subject to the full-attack limit. its attacks resolve sequentially on the character's scheduled initiative passes. a full attack is one continuing action, not a separate main action on every pass.a full attack always costs 1 pe total, whether it produces one attack or many. a character unable to pay that cost may still make a legal single attack. heavy and two-handed weapons may make either kind of attack normally.movement before and after attacksa character making a single attack may complete movement before or after the attack. movement cannot be divided around that attack unless an explicit rule permits it.a character making a full attack must complete all ordinary movement before the first attack. once the full attack begins, the character cannot use ordinary movement afterward or during a later pass. a character who wishes to attack and then move must choose a single attack.an explicit ability may override these restrictions according to its own text.replacing attacks during a full attacka full attack normally contains only melee or ranged weapon attacks. an unused attack cannot be converted freely into inventory use, spellcasting, conversation, or another unrelated action.an action may replace one or more attacks only when a maneuver, talent, spell, item, equipment feature, or other explicit rule permits it during a full attack. pay its listed attack cost from the attacks that remain unused that round. if an option supplies no full-attack substitution procedure, it cannot be inserted into the sequence.a permitted substitution may occur on any chosen pass unless its own timing says otherwise. several different substitutions may be used during the same round when each is permitted, every cost is paid, and every usage limit is obeyed.the dm may allow a narrow exception for something immediately combat-related, physically local, and sensible within the attack sequence. picking up a weapon at the character's feet may cost one attack. retrieving something that requires movement is unavailable after the full attack begins. drinking a potion requires it to be already held or made immediately accessible by suitable equipment.a dual-wielding swashbuckler's ordinary pass contains both weapon attacks as one paired pass. replacing that pass forfeits both attacks; neither hand can pay a substitution cost independently. a genuinely unpaired extra attack may pay a one-attack cost on its own.casting a spell normally uses the entire main action. combat casting or another explicit permission is required to combine spellcasting with melee attacks in the same round.later passes and changing targetslater full-attack passes are not locked to the first target. on a later pass, the attacker may choose any legal target that can be attacked from the character's current position, including a target within current melee reach or legal ranged range.changing targets grants no movement. if the original target dies, teleports, moves away, or otherwise becomes unavailable and no other target can be legally attacked from the current position, the remaining attacks are wasted.

pages.title: Drawing, Dropping, and Putting Away Equipment
pages.text:
combatactions in combat
only an explicit ability can provide movement or preserve those attacks under different conditions.drawing, dropping, and putting away equipmentbringing one accessible item to hand uses movement. an item in a pack or ordinary closed container is stored rather than accessible; a locked, tied-down, buried, or deeply packed item is secured. equipment defines those access states and the additional handling they require.a character with bab +1 or higher may bring any one accessible item to hand while using ordinary movement, then use the main action normally. a character without bab +1 spends the movement allowance to bring the item to hand and gains no movement from that allowance. drawing an accessible weapon follows this general procedure.dropping an item held in hand is free.sheathing, holstering, or otherwise putting away a weapon uses movement and provokes an attack of opportunity while threatened. drawing an accessible weapon does not provoke.bows and crossbows use the same drawing procedure. loading, cocking, ammunition retention, and other weapon-specific handling are described by their equipment rules.an explicit quick draw permission allows its named weapon to be drawn without spending movement. it does not accelerate sheathing or another equipment action unless its own text says so.drawing a weapon is equipment handling. it is not the ready action and establishes no trigger.

pages.title: Movement and Position · Speed, Squares, and Diagonal Movement
pages.text:
combatmovement and position
movement and positionmovement determines where a character can act, which enemies can be reached, and who threatens whom. unless an explicit rule says otherwise, ordinary movement occurs during the character's first initiative pass.speed, squares, and diagonal movementspeed is the distance a character can cover with ordinary movement. an ordinary medium humanoid has speed 30 feet.when a grid is used, each square represents 5 feet. count diagonal movement by alternating 5 feet, then 10 feet, repeating for each diagonal step along the path. the rules still operate in feet and do not require a grid.size alone does not determine speed. a race, creature, mount, spell, condition, or item states any value that differs from the ordinary speed above.a character who still has both movement and the main action may spend both on ordinary movement during the first initiative pass to move up to twice speed. this double movement grants no special protection from attacks of opportunity. it does not allow a character limited to one action to exchange that action for twice the normal distance.difficult terrain and occupied spaceseach foot crossed through difficult terrain costs twice as much movement. difficult terrain prevents run and charge unless an explicit rule says otherwise.a character may move through a willing ally's space but cannot ordinarily end movement there. moving through an enemy's space requires a legal maneuver, an explicit ability, or situational permission from the dm.vanaheim has no general five-foot step. a character cannot use a small free movement to avoid the ordinary consequences of leaving a threatened space.run, charge, and withdrawrun. running consumes both movement and the main action. the character moves up to four times speed along a reasonably straight, unobstructed route. heavy armor or being encumbered reduces this to three times speed.a running character loses the dexterity modifier from defense until the character's next turn. a character may run for consecutive rounds equal to the constitution score without an additional cost. each further consecutive round costs 1 pe. spending the final pe completes that round's run before the character becomes exhausted. a fatigued or exhausted character cannot run.an explicit run ability may change the multiplier or allow the character to retain dexterity according to its own text.charge. charging consumes both movement and the main action. the character moves at least 10 feet and up to twice speed along a straight, clear route toward a target, then makes one melee attack. difficult terrain or another obstruction prevents an ordinary charge.the attack gains +2 attack, and the charger takes -2 defense until the charger's next turn. charge movement can provoke attacks of opportunity. a charge never produces a full attack unless an explicit ability says otherwise. a fatigued or exhausted character cannot charge.withdraw. withdrawing consumes both movement and the main action and allows movement up to twice speed. against visible opponents, treat the character's starting space as unthreatened for this movement. leaving any later threatened space still provokes normally.an unseen opponent may still make an attack of opportunity because the withdrawing character could not deliberately avoid that threat. a blinded character cannot withdraw.a character limited to one action may use that action to withdraw up to the character's current speed.reach and threatened areasreach is the distance at which a creature can make a melee attack. a creature threatens every space it can presently attack in melee, even outside its own turn.small and medium creatures ordinarily have 5-foot reach. a large creature ordinarily has 10-foot reach, subject to its body shape and individual statistics.

pages.title: Attacks of Opportunity · Flanking, Higher Ground, and Cramped Spaces
pages.text:
combatmovement and position
a reach weapon threatens the distance stated in its equipment entry. it ordinarily does not threaten adjacent spaces unless that weapon or an explicit ability says otherwise.a creature without a weapon, natural attack, or an explicit ability that treats its unarmed attacks as armed does not normally threaten an area.attacks of opportunityan attack of opportunity is an immediate melee attack against an enemy who leaves an opening while threatened. making one is voluntary.the following general actions provoke:moving out of a space threatened by an enemy; entering a threatened space does not provoke;making a ranged weapon attack while threatened;making an unarmed attack against an armed target when no rule treats the attacker as armed;beginning to cast a spell or use a spell-like ability while threatened, unless a defensive-casting rule prevents the opportunity;drinking a potion, applying an oil, or reading a scroll while threatened;standing from prone while threatened;running while threatened;trying to control a frightened mount while threatened;helping another creature perform an action that would itself provoke while threatened;using medicine to stabilize another creature, or using another skill that requires comparable sustained attention, while threatened;retrieving a stored item, picking up an item, moving a heavy object, sheathing or holstering a weapon, loading a crossbow, lighting a torch, preparing a splash weapon, or performing comparable distracting equipment handling while threatened; andmissing with a heavy attack made with a heavy weapon wielded in both hands, which provokes only from the opponent who successfully defended, or failing an untrained hard trip or bash, as defined by those maneuvers; andperforming any action whose own rule states that it provokes.bringing an accessible item to hand, dropping a held item, speaking briefly, delaying, declaring ready, and making an ordinary melee attack or full attack do not themselves provoke. a readied action still provokes when the action it executes normally would.a specific action, maneuver, item, or ability may add, remove, or change a trigger. combat maneuvers do not provoke merely because they are maneuvers: each maneuver's own entry controls. disarm failure does not otherwise provoke, and the defender's free attack against some grab attempts is a separate procedure rather than an attack of opportunity.resolve the attack of opportunity immediately, before the triggering action or movement finishes. afterward, the interrupted action continues if it remains possible.the attack is one ordinary melee attack resolved through the normal attack, active defense, margin of success, damage, and protection rules. it consumes one attack-of-opportunity allowance, not movement, the main action, or a scheduled attack pass.a character normally has one attack-of-opportunity allowance per round, regardless of how many opportunities occur. an explicit ability may grant additional allowances. a character may use the allowance even after attacking during the character's own turn.even with additional allowances, one triggering opportunity permits only one attack. separate triggers may permit separate attacks when the character still has allowances available.moving out of several spaces threatened by the same enemy during one continuous movement creates only one opportunity for that enemy. different enemies may each respond if they threaten the movement and possess an available allowance.a flat-footed character cannot make attacks of opportunity unless an explicit ability permits it. uncanny dodge permits otherwise legal attacks of opportunity before the character's first action.there is no five-foot-step exception to these rules.flanking, higher ground, and cramped spacestwo allies flank an enemy when they threaten it from opposite sides. flanking grants both allies +2 attack against that enemy. it does not generally remove the enemy's dexterity modifier from defense. an

combatmovement and position
ability such as rogue sneak attack may use flanking as its own activation condition.a combatant on higher ground gains +2 attack and +2 defense against a lower opponent.a combatant materially restricted by cramped surroundings takes -4 attack and -4 defense. a long, heavy, or two-handed weapon may also be physically impractical in a particular space, but such a weapon suffers no additional universal attack speed or parry penalty merely for being heavy.magical flightwhile airborne through personally controlled magical flight, a character with the flight feat takes -2 to all attack and active defense rolls; a character without it takes -8 instead. these penalties apply to rolls, not passive defense. the feat's full entry in talents and feats — flight owns untrained speed, control checks and endurance.grounded maneuvers, including bash, trip / hard trip and dirt kick, cannot be used while flying, even with the feat. other maneuvers retain their own requirements. natural flight and riding flying mounts remain governed by their own rules.restricted movement and dodgedodge requires somewhere to evade. the available space and the shape of an incoming attack can penalize dodge, commonly by as much as -8.when there is physically nowhere to evade, the defender does not roll dodge. use:static dodge = 10 + bab + dexterity modifier + applicable passive magical defensive modifiersrelevant cover still applies. a passive ability contributes only when its own text applies to that attack; static dodge does not create additional class benefits.this is separate from static parry or block against a sufficiently superior or oversized attacker. those rules do not make dodge static while physical evasion remains possible.

pages.title: Attacking and Defending · Declaring and Resolving an Attack
pages.text:
combatattacking and defending
attacking and defendingan attack is resolved against one chosen defense. the attacker declares what is being attempted, the defender commits to a legal response, and the two totals determine whether the attack connects and how cleanly it lands.whenever a defender is permitted to choose a defense, they may decline an active defense and use passive defense:10 + bab + applicable passive magical defensive modifierspassive defense is chosen before either combat roll. it rolls no d20 and spends no dodge, parry, or block use. a condition that permits no defensive choice and supplies a stricter value, such as helpless, still uses its own procedure. a golem frame uses the profile-based passive defense defined by its own subsystem.declaring and resolving an attackresolve an ordinary attack in this order:the attacker declares the target and describes the attack clearly enough for the defender to understand what is coming.the defender chooses an otherwise legal dodge, parry, or block, or uses passive defense, before either combat roll is made. the defender does not see the attack die or final attack total before choosing.roll the attack and any chosen active defense, or use passive defense or the appropriate static defense.if attack is lower than defense, the attack misses. if attack meets or exceeds defense, it connects.calculate the margin of success and pass the result to damage and protection.the physical attack determines which defenses are legal. a shield can answer some attacks that cannot reasonably be parried, and dodge requires somewhere to evade.attack rolls and natural resultsan attack roll is:1d20 + bab + relevant ability modifier + applicable feat, talent, magical, weapon, and situational modifiers
201combat · attacking and defending

pages.title: Dodge, Parry, and Block · Defense Uses and Additional Attempts
pages.text:
combatattacking and defending
ordinary melee attacks normally use strength, and ordinary ranged attacks normally use dexterity. a weapon, attack, feat, talent, spell, or other explicit rule may use a different ability.apply a modifier only when it is relevant to the attack being made. a bonus written only for damage is not an attack modifier, and a bonus written only for a particular weapon, method, or circumstance does not apply outside it.a natural 1 on the attack die is an automatic miss.a natural 20 is not an automatic hit. it must still meet or exceed the chosen defense. if a connecting result lies within the attack's critical threat range, resolve it through the current critical-hit rules; there is no confirmation roll.natural 1 and natural 20 have no automatic effect on an active defense roll. resolve the defense total normally.dodge, parry, and blockdodge is:1d20 + bab + dexterity modifier + applicable dodge and situational modifiersdodge requires enough physical room to evade the attack and can be penalized or denied by the situation.parry uses the character's attack calculation with the parrying weapon, retaining only modifiers relevant to defense. offensive-only bonuses do not apply. defensive bonuses and penalties do. a character without a suitable weapon has no ordinary parry.block is:1d20 + bab + strength modifier + shield bonus + applicable defensive modifiersuse the shield's block value, or its projectile block value against a qualifying projectile. applicable defensive modifiers include bonuses from enhanced block, weapon focus (shields), shield material, and magical accuracy. add each bonus once, accounting for any material bonus already included in the shield's printed profile.an explicit feat, talent, or ability may substitute dexterity or another ability for strength. a character without a suitable shield has no ordinary block. a shield may block some attacks that cannot reasonably be parried.an explicit unarmed-defense ability may permit defenses without a weapon or shield according to its own rules.defense uses and additional attemptsa character begins each round with one penalty-free dodge. a suitable weapon supplies one penalty-free parry, and a suitable shield supplies one penalty-free block. dodge, parry, and block are separate pools.a second suitable weapon supplies one additional base parry, which must be made with that weapon. enhanced parry adds its additional uses once to the shared parry pool; wielding more weapons does not multiply them.enhanced dodge, enhanced parry, and enhanced block are separate feats. each grants additional penalty-free uses of its defense according to bab:babadditional penalty-free uses+3 to +51+6 to +82+9 to +113+12 to +144+15 or higher5after all penalty-free uses of one defense category are spent, the character may make up to three further attempts of that category during the round:the first additional attempt takes -4;the second takes -8; andthe third takes -12.no further attempt of that category is possible after its -12 attempt. dodge, parry, and block track their uses and escalating penalties separately. passive defense remains available.a static dodge, parry, or block still consumes one use from its category. if its penalty-free pool is already exhausted, apply the appropriate -4, -8, or -12 penalty to the static value. passive defense consumes no use.
202combat · attacking and defending

pages.title: Example: Tracking Defense Uses · Margin of Success
pages.text:
combatattacking and defending
example: tracking defense usesa bab +9 sword-and-shield fighter with enhanced parry begins the round with four penalty-free parries: one from the weapon and three from enhanced parry. the shield supplies one separate penalty-free block, and the fighter also has one penalty-free dodge. a fifth parry takes -4. before any attack, the fighter may choose passive defense instead and spend none of these uses.if the same fighter wields two suitable weapons instead, each weapon supplies one base parry and enhanced parry adds three more to the shared pool, producing five penalty-free parries rather than eight.margin of successwhen an attack connects, calculate:margin of success = attack - defenseattack equal to defense is a hit with a margin of success of 0. add the final margin directly to the attack's damage under damage and protection.an attack-only bonus can therefore improve damage indirectly by increasing margin of success. do not add it to damage a second time unless its own rule also grants an explicit damage bonus.advantage, disadvantage, and rerollsadvantage means rolling 2d20 and keeping the higher die. disadvantage means rolling 2d20 and keeping the lower die. the rule granting advantage or disadvantage identifies which roll it affects; it does not automatically apply to every related d20 roll.the dm may assign advantage or disadvantage when circumstances materially favor or hinder a roll. neither makes an impossible action possible; the dm may rule that an attempt simply cannot succeed.count advantage and disadvantage sources against one another one for one. equal numbers cancel completely. if any advantage remains, roll with advantage once. if any disadvantage remains, roll with disadvantage once. additional uncancelled sources do not add more dice.a reroll applied to an advantaged or disadvantaged roll normally rerolls one chosen die from the two-die pool. replace that die, then determine the result from the revised pool. an explicit reroll ability may state a different procedure.a character with an available luck reroll may spend it after seeing one of their own d20 results. reroll and keep the result more favorable to the character. on an advantaged or disadvantaged roll, reroll one chosen die, resolve the revised pool, then keep the more favorable of the original and revised results.before making a disadvantaged roll, the character may instead spend one luck reroll to cancel the remaining disadvantage and roll one ordinary d20. luck rerolls are a limited per-story-arc resource. damage dice and other non-d20 rolls are not universally eligible.weapon configurations and two-weapon fightingweapon configurations are physical equipment choices. each configuration grants only the benefits listed below and in the relevant equipment rules.wielding one one-handed weapon grants no universal numerical bonus. its benefit is leaving the other hand free.wielding a weapon and shield grants the ordinary properties of that weapon and shield, including separate parry and block uses. the arrangement grants no additional implicit modifier.wielding a two-handed or heavy weapon grants only that weapon's written properties and access to heavy attack when its requirements are met. it receives no universal attack speed, parry, or mandatory-full-attack penalty for being heavy.any further benefit requires an explicit weapon, feat, talent, class feature, or technique.when fighting with a weapon in each hand without dual wield, choose one as the primary attack. the second weapon grants one separate, unpaired offhand attack pass every two rounds. place that pass in the round with fewer primary attacks; if both rounds contain the same number, place it in the first round.attacks and parries made with either weapon take -4. if the offhand weapon is light, this penalty becomes -2. dodge is unaffected.each suitable weapon supplies one base parry use made with that weapon. a single-attack main action still makes only one attack.a character with dual wield uses that talent's procedure instead.
203combat · attacking and defending

pages.title: Example: Ordinary Two-Weapon Fighting · Static Defenses and Overwhelming Opponents
pages.text:
combatattacking and defending
example: ordinary two-weapon fightinga character with primary attack speed 1.5 makes three primary attacks across two rounds. fighting with a second weapon adds one offhand attack during that cycle, producing two attacks in each round. if both weapons can parry, each also supplies one base parry use; the ordinary two-weapon penalty applies to both.static defenses and overwhelming opponentsa static defense uses a fixed value instead of rolling a d20. unlike passive defense, it remains a chosen dodge, parry, or block and spends that defense's uses. use the following established procedures:situationdefense procedurethe defender is genuinely surprised by the attack.no active defense is chosen. use 10 + bab + applicable passive magical defensive modifiers.the defender is flat-footed.choose an otherwise legal defense, but do not roll or add dexterity. use 10 + bab + applicable non-dexterity bonuses for the chosen defense + applicable magical defensive modifiers.there is physically nowhere to dodge.use 10 + bab + dexterity modifier + applicable passive magical defensive modifiers.the attacker is at least five experience levels higher.parry or block becomes 10 + bab + applicable passive magical defensive modifiers.the attacker is at least two size categories larger.parry or block uses the same superior-attacker static value above.choosing a static dodge, parry, or block still consumes one use and applies any -4, -8, or -12 additional-attempt penalty already reached for that category.dodge remains available against a superior or oversized attacker when physical evasion is possible. a one-category size difference does not invoke the oversized static-defense rule.when flat-footed overlaps the superior-level or oversized-attacker rule, the stricter superior-attacker formula controls and the chosen defense contributes no ordinary weapon or shield bonus. other unusual overlaps involving restricted dodge, cover, concealment, surprise, or flat-footed remain subject to the established procedures and the physical situation rather than a new universal combined formula.level or size superiority does not by itself make an attack lethal.
204combat · attacking and defending

pages.title: Unarmed Attacks
pages.text:
combatattacking and defending
unarmed attacksan ordinary bare unarmed attack uses the normal melee attack roll with strength. it deals 1d4 bludgeoning damage, has pen 0, reaches 5 feet, and uses critical threat 20 with the universal x2 weapon-dice critical. strength, margin of success, and other applicable melee modifiers affect it normally. a bare unarmed attack is not automatically lethal damage.bare unarmed attacks belong to the unarmed weapon group but are not light, medium, or heavy weapons. an effect restricted to one of those weapon categories does not apply to a bare hand unless it also explicitly permits unarmed attacks.without self defense, a character may make one bare unarmed attack as a main action. the character cannot include one in a full attack, make an unarmed attack of opportunity, or use a bare hand to parry. the attack provokes an attack of opportunity from an armed opponent or an opponent possessing self defense, but not from another opponent who is likewise unarmed and lacks self defense.unarmed combat training is training in the unarmed weapon group. it permits trained use of the fist weapons listed in equipment and allows the group to be selected for abilities such as weapon mastery. training alone does not grant self defense, brawling, or wild fighting, treat bare hands as armed, or remove any of the bare-hand restrictions above.self defense retains the ordinary 1d4, pen 0 bare-hand profile while granting the options stated by that talent. bare-handed brawling instead deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage with pen 0; a qualifying fist weapon uses its printed profile. bare-handed wild fighting deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage with pen 2; a qualifying fist weapon uses its printed damage die and damage type with pen at least 2. talents and feats owns the remaining procedures and restrictions of those abilities.
205combat · attacking and defending

pages.title: Saving Throws and Magical Resistance · Saving Throws
pages.text:
combatsaving throws and magical resistance
saving throws and magical resistancesaving throws resist harmful effects that use a difficulty class. magic protection and magic resistance are separate magical defenses: magic protection reduces spell damage, while magic resistance can resist magic completely.saving throwswhen an effect allows a saving throw, roll:d20 + base save + governing ability modifier + explicit bonusesa base save is the character's permanent purchased fortitude, reflex, or will value before its governing ability modifier and other bonuses. use the save named by the effect:saving throwgoverning abilitycommon purposefortitudeconstitutionendure effects through bodily resilience.reflexdexterityevade or react physically to an effect.willwisdomresist effects through awareness and force of will.compare the final total with the effect's difficulty class, or dc. meeting or exceeding the dc succeeds.a natural 1 is not an automatic failure, and a natural 20 is not an automatic success. add the save normally and compare its final total with the dc.there is no universal result for a successful saving throw. the effect must state whether success negates it, halves it, reduces it, delays it, or changes it in some other way. an effect that calls for a save but gives no result for success is incomplete.effect and spell dcsan effect with its own complete dc formula uses that formula. when a non-spell talent, maneuver, song, or other ability calls for a saving throw without supplying a complete dc, use:10 + relevant ability modifier + half the granting job level, rounded down + art + any other explicit modifiersuse the ability named by the effect. if none is named, use charisma. the granting job level is the character's level in the job that granted the ability, not adventure level or an unrelated job. art applies to every dc the character creates.this default formula creates only the dc. the effect must still identify the required save and the result of success. it does not replace an ability's established roll-under or opposed-check procedure.
206combat · saving throws and magical resistance

pages.title: Magic Protection and Magic Resistance
pages.text:
combatsaving throws and magical resistance
the default spell save dc is:10 + caster level + charisma modifier + artcaster level is normally half the character's level in the relevant caster job. a class, spell, or ability may state an exception.magic protection and magic resistancemagic protection (mp) is a passive, flat reduction against spell damage. subtract the target's mp from applicable spell damage. for example, mp 4 reduces 10 spell damage to 6.mp is not magical energy. it cannot be spent, reserved, recovered, drained as payment, or used as an ability cost. magical costs and recovery use magical energy (me).magic resistance (mr) is a percentile chance to resist magic completely. when mr applies, roll percentile dice. a result within the listed percentage succeeds; for example, mr 20% succeeds on 01-20. successful mr completely resists the magic for that creature.mr is not a saving throw and does not add to one. mp, mr, and saving throws remain separate defenses. a successful mr check leaves no spell damage for mp to reduce; when mr does not resist the magic, resolve any applicable saving throw and mp normally.when several defenses apply to the same hostile spell, resolve mr first, then ongoing spells that absorb, turn, reflect, deflect, or otherwise prevent the spell, then the spell's saving throw, then mp, other applicable dr, and damage-reducing spells. apply eligible pe mitigation afterward, then route the remaining damage to temporary hp, hp, and lp. if a successful save halves damage, halve the raw damage and round down before applying mp or other protection. when several ongoing protective spells apply at the same stage, resolve the highest-circle spell first and continue downward unless a spell says otherwise.
207combat · saving throws and magical resistance

pages.title: Ranged Combat · Ranged Attacks and Defenses
pages.text:
combatranged combat
ranged combatranged attacks use the ordinary attack and defense procedure, modified by the weapon's equipment range bands, nearby allies, cover, concealment, and the weapon being used.ranged attacks and defensesa ranged weapon attack normally uses dexterity as its relevant attack ability. the weapon must be ready, the target must be within the weapon's maximum range, and total physical cover must not prevent direct targeting. the equipment chapter defines the weapon's effective, far, and extreme distance bands. apply the appropriate band, firing-into-melee, cover, and other relevant modifiers before resolving the ordinary attack and defense rolls.dodge can defend against a projectile when physical evasion is possible. a suitable shield can block ordinary arrows, bolts, and comparable projectiles. parrying a projectile requires an explicit ability or exceptional permission.making a ranged weapon attack while threatened provokes an attack of opportunity. resolve the attack of opportunity immediately before the ranged attack, then resume the ranged attack if it remains possible.a ranged full attack follows the ordinary full attack rules. drawing a bow or crossbow follows the ordinary weapon-drawing procedure. ammunition, loading, cocking, each weapon's range, and other weapon-specific handling belong to its equipment entry.firing into meleefiring or throwing at a target engaged in melee with the attacker's ally imposes -4 attack.reduce the penalty to -2 when the target is two size categories larger than the nearest ally.remove the penalty when the target is at least three size categories larger than the nearest ally.remove the penalty when the aimed target, or the part of the target being aimed at, is at least 10 feet from the nearest ally.precise shot removes the penalty according to its own text.an ordinary miss while firing into melee does not create a random attack against an ally.
208combat · ranged combat

pages.title: Cover and Concealment · Example: Cover and Concealment
pages.text:
combatranged combat
cover and concealmentcover is physical protection between an attack or effect and its target.coverbenefitordinary cover+4 defense and +2 reflex against attacks or effects crossing the cover.improved cover+8 defense and +4 reflex against attacks or effects crossing the cover.total physical coverprevents direct targeting.concealment makes the target difficult to see without necessarily placing a physical barrier in the way. ordinary concealment gives a 20% miss chance. total concealment gives a 50% miss chance.before rolling concealment's miss chance, the defender chooses whether to commit a defense or trust the concealment through passive defense.commit a defense: resolve the chosen dodge, parry, or block normally, including any required static form. if the attack connects, roll the concealment miss chance. the defense use is spent even if concealment then negates the attack.trust the concealment: use passive defense, then roll the applicable miss chance if the attack connects. no defense use is spent. if concealment does not negate the attack, the defender cannot declare an active defense retroactively.cover and concealment are separate. when both apply, add the cover bonus to the applicable defense and resolve concealment through its miss chance.example: cover and concealmenta guard stands behind ordinary cover in thick smoke, gaining +4 defense from cover and a 20% concealment miss chance. against the first arrow, the guard commits block and adds the cover bonus. the arrow connects, but concealment negates it; the block use is still spent. against the next arrow, the guard trusts concealment instead, using passive defense with the +4 cover bonus. if the arrow connects and the miss chance fails, the guard cannot declare an active defense afterward.
209combat · ranged combat

pages.title: Damage and Protection · Calculating Damage
pages.text:
combatdamage and protection
damage and protectiondamage first meets protection, then passes through the target's protective pools toward actual bodily harm. this section uses six related terms:raw damage is the complete damage total before any protection is applied.damage reduction (dr) is a numeric protection subtracted from damage when that protection applies.armor penetration (pen) measures an attack's ability to defeat physical armor through piercing, cutting, crushing, or overwhelming force.armor grade (grade) measures how difficult physical armor is to defeat before applying that armor's listed dr.hit points (hp) are one protective pool increased by jobs, training, worn armor, and other explicit effects. temporary hp is separate only when its source says so.life points (lp) represent the character's actual bodily survival. lethal damage bypasses hp and reaches lp directly, but applicable dr and physical energy mitigation still resolve first.calculating damageordinary weapon damage is:weapon dice + relevant ability modifier + explicit damage modifiers + margin of successuse the ability modifier specified by the weapon or attack. margin of success is the amount by which the attack total met or exceeded the defense; a tied attack and defense therefore add 0 damage from margin while still producing a hit.a bonus that applies only to the attack roll can increase damage indirectly by increasing margin of success. do not add it directly to damage a second time unless its source explicitly grants a damage bonus as well.size supplies no separate universal damage modifier. larger creatures normally express their power through attributes, larger weapon dice, or explicit abilities. weapon dice and the weapon-size progression belong to equipment.a heavy attack is a special maneuver made only with a heavy weapon wielded in both hands. it normally consumes two attacks to deliver one blow; its complete action and damage procedure appears under combat maneuvers, while its interaction with physical protection is defined below.
210combat · damage and protection

pages.title: Damage Resolution Order · Damage Reduction, Armor Penetration, and Armor Grade
pages.text:
combatdamage and protection
damage resolution orderresolve each damage result in this order:calculate raw damage, including weapon dice, the relevant ability modifier, explicit damage modifiers, margin of success, and any critical or other dice modification.apply and combine all applicable dr after resolving any armor penetration, armor grade, material, heavy attack, magical, supernatural, or critical adjustments. ordinary dr can reduce damage to 0.once the post-dr result is known, the target may apply one eligible pe damage-mitigation option.route the remaining damage through any applicable temporary hp, then hp and lp. if the damage is lethal, route it directly to lp instead.actual damage is the final amount remaining after dr and any eligible pe mitigation that is routed into hp or lp. it includes damage absorbed by hp and is not limited to damage that reaches lp.unless a rule explicitly states otherwise, round fractions down at every stage.when several ordinary multipliers apply to the same base value, start at x1, then add the amount by which each multiplier exceeds x1.two x2 multipliers therefore become x3, while x4 combined with x3 becomes x6. an explicit rule may define a separate operation instead.damage reduction, armor penetration, and armor gradedr subtracts its value from damage when its source protects against that damage. worn physical armor uses grade: the relationship between the attack and the armor determines how much of its listed dr applies. natural armor, scales, hides, physical fortifications, and similar barriers use grade when their own entry assigns one.the compact labels pen and grade below refer to armor penetration and armor grade. pen does not add directly to attack or damage, and grade does not add directly to dr.light, medium, and heavy remain weapon and armor categories with their own additional rules. their ordinary starting values are:categoryweapon armor penetrationarmor gradelightpen 1grade 1mediumpen 2grade 2heavypen 3grade 3whether a weapon uses one or two hands is a separate property. using two hands does not by itself increase pen, and a non-heavy two-handed weapon does not become heavy.creatures of large size or greater generally have at least medium natural armor when their natural protection is grade-sensitive. a creature's protection may instead be explicitly supernatural and therefore flat.resolve grade-sensitive physical protection in this order:establish the attack's pen from its weapon, material, enchantment, and other explicit modifiers.establish the protection's grade from its category, material, construction, and other explicit modifiers.if the attack is a heavy attack, add +1 pen.compare final pen with final grade and apply the result below to that protection's listed dr.comparisongrade-sensitive physical armor drpen is at least 2 higher than gradeignore that drpen is 1 higher than gradeapply half drpen equals gradeapply normal drpen is 1 lower than gradeapply normal dr plus half drpen is at least 2 lower than gradeapply double dr
211combat · damage and protection

pages.title: Example: Reading Pen and Grade · Physical Energy Damage Mitigation
pages.text:
combatdamage and protection
round fractional dr down. the general comparison never increases dr beyond double and never makes armor automatically impenetrable. an armor, creature, or other protection ignores physical weapon damage below a stated pen only when an explicit special quality says so.energy armor and supernatural dr are grade-less flat protections. magic protection, energy protection, barbarian toughness, class-granted flat dr, and comparable protections likewise apply their listed dr without comparing pen against grade. heavy attack, weapon material, and other pen modifiers grant no special bypass against flat dr unless that protection explicitly says otherwise.when several protections apply, resolve the pen and grade comparison separately for each affected grade-sensitive physical source, retain every applicable flat source at its normal value, and then combine the resulting dr. armor may provide both dr and armor hp: resolve its dr here before damage reaches hp. the armor's printed armor hp increases the wearer's maximum hp while worn and does not represent the armor's structural condition.example: reading pen and gradea medium weapon with pen 2 striking heavy armor with grade 3 and dr 9 is one point lower, so the armor applies dr 13: its normal 9 plus half of 9, rounded down to 4. a heavy weapon normally has pen 3; heavy attack raises it to pen 4, which applies half dr against heavy grade 3 armor and ignores the dr of medium grade 2 armor.physical energy damage mitigationafter dr has produced a known result, the target may use one of the following options:costmitigation4 pehalve the post-dr damage, rounding down. this can reduce 1 damage to 0 and may be used once per encounter.3 pe per 1d6subtract 1d6 per 3 pe, to a maximum of 3d6 for 9 pe. this option cannot reduce the result below 1 damage.these options cannot be combined against the same damage result. the character must pay the complete cost, and pe cannot fall below 0. spending the character's final pe completes the mitigation before the character becomes exhausted.these options resolve before damage enters hp or lp, including when the damage is lethal. a surprised or flat-footed character may still use an otherwise legal post-hit damage-mitigation option.hit points and life pointsa character's base lp equals the constitution score, plus any explicit racial or class lp bonuses. jobs, classes, purchased training, worn armor, and other sources all contribute to the character's single hp pool.an armor's printed armor hp is the amount it adds to maximum hp while worn. those points are not separately damaged, tracked, or healed, and losing hp does not damage the armor. an effect that explicitly grants temporary hp tracks that temporary pool separately because its own rule says so; temporary hp cannot be healed.when damage is not lethal, deplete any applicable temporary hp, then hp, and then lp. damage left after one pool reaches 0 overflows into the next applicable pool.
212combat · damage and protection

pages.title: Example: Damage from Attack Roll to Life Points · Nonlethal Damage
pages.text:
combatdamage and protection
example: damage from attack roll to life pointsan attack of 24 meets defense 20 with margin 4. the weapon rolls 8, then adds +4 strength, +4 explicit damage, and +4 margin for 20 raw damage. the weapon has pen 2 and the armor has grade 2 with listed dr 4. equal pen and grade leave that dr unchanged, reducing the damage to 16. the defender spends 4 pe to halve that result to 8. the defender has 2 temporary hp and 5 hp remaining, so the damage removes both temporary hp and all 5 hp; the final 1 point reaches lp. if the same final result were lethal damage, it would bypass both hp pools and remove 8 lp instead.nonlethal damagenonlethal damage, sometimes called subdual damage, follows the ordinary damage sequence through hp and lp. it causes no wound when it reaches lp. a creature reduced to 0 lp by nonlethal damage becomes unconscious instead of dying.lethal damagelethal damage follows the normal dr and pe-mitigation sequence, then bypasses temporary hp and hp and applies directly to lp.a deliberate attack that genuinely connects with a bound, sleeping, or otherwise helpless body ordinarily deals lethal damage. a surprise killing strike may also be lethal when the attacker's training, method, and circumstances support it. ordinary combat sneak attacks are not automatically lethal, and surprise or flat-footed status alone is insufficient. a deliberately nonlethal method may remain hp damage when that result is physically plausible.superior level or size does not automatically make an attack lethal. falling damage is an exception to the ordinary sequence: it ignores dr, may still be reduced by eligible pe mitigation, then bypasses hp and reaches lp. an overwhelming projectile may be lethal when the dm judges that its actual effect warrants it.the dm classifies lethal damage from the physical circumstances, attacker competence, declared intent, and nature of the attack. armor and magical defenses can influence whether that classification makes sense; once damage is classified as lethal, hp does not protect against it.
213combat · damage and protection

pages.title: Critical Hits · Example: Critical Damage and Multiple Multipliers
pages.text:
combatdamage and protection
critical hitsan attack that connects within its critical threat range is a critical hit. there is no confirmation roll. a natural 20 must still connect and is not an automatic hit.determine the attack's complete damage-dice expression, apply the four-damage-dice conversion, roll the remaining dice once, and multiply the entire damage-dice subtotal by 2. converted +2 values remain part of that subtotal. do not roll a second set. add non-dice modifiers such as strength and margin of success only once.apply critical multiplication after rolling the damage dice. first determine the ordinary weapon dice after effects that change their number, such as a straight, clear mounted charge of at least 30 feet made with an appropriate weapon; convert every damage die beyond the fourth to +2, roll the remaining dice once, include those converted values, then multiply that subtotal by 2.critical hits bypass most dr; any applicable magical dr is halved. a critical hit does not bypass hp by default. it reaches lp directly only when an explicit critical result or an independent lethal-damage classification says so.a critical hit may cause a deadly or lasting wound when the circumstances or an explicit result require one.example: critical damage and multiple multiplierstwo ordinary x2 multipliers applied to the same value combine into x3, not x4. effects that change the number of weapon dice happen before a critical instead. a qualifying mounted charge changes a 1d8 weapon to 2d8; if those dice roll 11 on a critical hit, double that one rolled result to 22, then add +3 strength and +4 margin once for 29 damage. do not double the strength or margin.creature size and unnatural toughnesscreature lp is calculated as:(constitution score + 10 per unnatural toughness rank) × size multipliersizelp multipliertiny / small / normal / medium×1large×2huge×4unnatural toughness may be applied more than once. add 10 lp for each rank before multiplying for size. size does not separately add damage; its offensive effect is represented through attributes, weapon dice, and explicit abilities.gargantuan-scale creatures are not normally treated as conventional combat opponents. ordinary weapon combat against a building-scale creature is handled through exceptional magic, special circumstances, or scenario adjudication rather than a general lp multiplier.
214combat · damage and protection

pages.title: Wounds, Dying, and Death · Wound Bands and Wound Penalties
pages.text:
combatwounds, dying, and death
wounds, dying, and deathinjury is tracked through three separate systems:an lp wound band measures the severity of the character's current positive lp and supplies wound penalties.a mortal wound is a distinct, lasting injury tracked separately from lp. active mortal wounds count toward their own death limit.bleeding is an independently tracked source of continuing lp loss.these systems interact only where a rule explicitly says that they do. a mortal wound does not automatically cause bleeding, bleeding does not automatically cause a mortal wound, and restoring lp does not by itself remove either one.wound bands and wound penaltiescount the character's positive lp downward from maximum lp and divide it into three bands. assign half the maximum lp to light, rounding up. divide the remaining points between serious and critical, assigning any extra point to serious.current wound bandportion of positive lpeffectlightfirst half, counted downward from maximum lpno wound penalty.seriousnext quarter-2 wound penalty.criticalfinal positive quarter-4 wound penalty, cannot run, and -0.5 primary attack speed.the serious and critical values are total penalties for the current band; they do not stack with one another. apply the current wound penalty to attack rolls, rolled active defenses, reflex saves, ability checks, skill checks, and maneuver checks. do not apply it to fortitude saves, will saves, damage rolls, dcs, dr, or static values.the critical-band attack speed penalty cannot reduce primary attack speed below the general minimum of 1. exactly 0 lp is outside all three positive wound bands.example: dividing an odd life point totala character with maximum lp 17 assigns 9 points to light, leaving 8. those remaining points divide evenly into 4 serious and 4 critical. the exact bands are therefore light at 17 through 9 lp, serious at 8 through 5, and critical at 4 through 1. at 4 lp the character takes the total -4 wound penalty, cannot run, and loses 0.5 primary attack speed; an attack speed of 1 remains 1 because it cannot fall below the general minimum.zero and negative life pointsat exactly 0 lp, or at any survivable negative lp value, a character becomes unconscious. negative lp is the deadly wound band; exactly 0 is neither a positive wound band nor part of the deadly band.the character is helpless: they fall prone, drop everything held, cannot move, speak, act, or make active defenses, and use this static defense:10 + applicable passive magical defensive modifiersdo not add bab, dexterity, weapon or shield bonuses, or another active-defense benefit. the complete unconscious condition appears under combat conditions.
215combat · wounds, dying, and death

pages.title: Death Thresholds · Mortal Wounds
pages.text:
combatwounds, dying, and death
entering or remaining at negative lp does not automatically remove another lp, require recurring death checks, or create a countdown. the character remains at the current lp until healing, further damage, bleeding, another explicit ongoing effect, or a concrete physical circumstance changes it.a character made unconscious by 0 or negative lp regains consciousness upon reaching at least 1 lp unless another condition independently prevents it.death thresholdsthe negative-lp boundary uses half the constitution score, not the constitution modifier. halve the constitution score, round down, and make the result negative. the exact boundary is survivable; falling one point below it kills the character.constitutionsurvives atdies at16-8-917-8-918-9-1019-9-10a character can also die from accumulating mortal wounds. an active mortal wound is one that has not been successfully removed. every character survives one active mortal wound, plus one for each point of positive constitution modifier. the next mortal wound beyond that allowance kills the character. a constitution modifier of 0 or less therefore still allows the character to survive one and die upon receiving the second. removing a mortal wound removes it from this count.the negative-lp boundary and the active-mortal-wound allowance are independent routes to death. reaching either death condition kills the character regardless of the other count.mortal woundswhen one source of damage moves a character from 0 or positive lp into negative lp, it normally causes one mortal wound. a single source of damage can cause no more than one mortal wound, even when it could inflict several distinct injuries or satisfies more than one mortal-wound trigger.
216combat · wounds, dying, and death

pages.title: Preventing a Mortal Wound with Physical Energy · Example: Entering Negative LP and Preventing a Mortal Wound
pages.text:
combatwounds, dying, and death
one attack that inflicts actual lp damage greater than half the target's maximum lp may cause a mortal wound even while the target remains above the negative-lp death threshold. actual lp damage is the amount truly removed from lp after dr, pe mitigation, and applicable hp have resolved; separate attacks are not added together for this threshold. exactly half the target's maximum lp does not meet it. a spell or another effect can also cause a mortal wound.further damage suffered while already at negative lp may cause another mortal wound, but does not do so automatically. judge the result from the attack, the injury, and the circumstances. a deliberate lethal attack against an unconscious character will often kill by crossing the negative-lp threshold directly.bleeding is an explicit exception: entering negative lp through bleeding does not itself cause a mortal wound.to determine a mortal wound's broad location, roll d8:d8location1upper torso2middle torso3lower torso4left arm5right arm6left leg7right leg8headroll d20 for severity. a result near 1 can represent a minor permanent scar or similar consequence; a result of 20 is extremely severe. the dm determines the exact injury from the attack, location, damage, depth below 0 lp, and fictional circumstances. greater depth below 0 makes the result more severe, but there is no fixed numerical modifier or universal consequence table.for an arm or leg, the dm may roll an additional d10 to refine where along the limb the injury falls. for an arm, 1 is near the shoulder and 10 is near the fingers; other precise results remain situational.preventing a mortal wound with physical energywhenever a character would receive a mortal wound, the character may spend 5 pe to prevent that one wound. the character must be able to pay the complete cost.each payment prevents one mortal wound. separate mortal wounds caused by separate sources require separate 5-pe payments.if the prevented mortal wound would be caused by entering survivable negative lp, the character instead falls unconscious at -1 lp and receives no mortal wound. this does not permit survival when the damage has already carried the character below the death threshold.if the mortal wound is caused independently of entering negative lp—such as by an attack dealing more than half maximum lp, a spell, or another effect—prevent only that mortal wound; all other damage and consequences remain in place. spending the character's final 5 pe completes this response before the character becomes exhausted.the response to first entering survivable negative lp is paid before the resulting unconscious condition takes effect. an unconscious character cannot spend pe and therefore cannot use this response against a later mortal wound.example: entering negative lp and preventing a mortal wounda constitution 18 character at 8 lp takes 12 actual lp damage from one attack. the attack would leave them at -4 and satisfies both entry into negative lp and the greater-than-half-maximum-lp trigger, but one source can cause no more than one mortal wound. if the character can spend 5 pe before becoming unconscious, they instead fall to -1 lp and receive no mortal wound.if the same character begins at 18 lp and loses 10 lp from one attack, they remain at 8 lp but have lost more than half their maximum. if the dm applies a mortal wound, spending 5 pe prevents that wound without restoring the 10 lp. no 5-pe response can save the character from damage that has already carried them to -10 lp, one point below their survivable boundary.
217combat · wounds, dying, and death

pages.title: Bleeding
pages.text:
combatwounds, dying, and death
bleedingbleeding uses light / moderate / serious severities. these names are separate from the light / serious / critical / deadly lp wound bands.each bleeding wound is one independent bleeding instance. instances stack, remain separately tracked, and never combine into a higher severity.bleeding severitydirect lp losslight bleeding1 lp per minutemoderate bleeding3 lp per minuteserious bleeding1 lp per round, equivalent to 10 lp per minutebleeding bypasses hp and reduces lp directly. each active instance inflicts its full loss. bleeding continues through negative lp and can kill by carrying the character below the negative-lp death threshold.bleeding loss is not an incoming damage result. the general 4-pe halving and d6 pe damage-mitigation options cannot reduce it.in initiative, apply bleeding loss at the end of the affected character's turn when that loss comes due. serious bleeding comes due every turn. light and moderate bleeding come due after each complete minute; when tracked in initiative, apply the due loss at the end of the affected character's turn. outside initiative, apply each loss after its stated interval.crossing from 0 or positive lp into negative lp through bleeding does not cause a mortal wound, and later bleeding losses do not create mortal wounds. the original injury that caused bleeding may have caused one normally. restoring lp does not itself stop bleeding.mundane treatment. treatment addresses one bleeding instance at a time and requires suitable medical supplies. field medic is specialized urgent-care training used for the more dangerous procedures.targeted instancerequired treatmentlight bleedingone round and a successful medicine check. field medic is not required.moderate bleedingfield medic, one minute, and a successful medicine check.serious bleedingfield medic, ten minutes, and a successful medicine check.for moderate or serious bleeding, make the medicine check when treatment begins. success immediately suppresses that instance while treatment continues without interruption; completing the full treatment removes it. failure provides no suppression, so the target continues losing lp. every other untreated instance continues at its normal rate.magical treatment. cure spells remove bleeding as follows:spellbleeding removedcure lightone light bleeding instance.cure serious woundsone moderate bleeding instance and every light bleeding instance.cure critical woundsone serious bleeding instance and every moderate and light bleeding instance.
218combat · wounds, dying, and death

pages.title: Stabilization and Urgent Treatment
pages.text:
combatwounds, dying, and death
a higher-tier spell still removes its listed lower-tier bleeding when the target has no matching higher-tier instance. the amount of lp restored by the spell remains part of that spell's own rules.stabilization and urgent treatmentat negative lp, stabilization stops a specific injury, effect, or circumstance that is causing or threatening continued deterioration. negative lp alone does not deteriorate and does not require stabilization.a character trained in medicine may attempt stabilization. the attempt takes one round and consumes the responder's main action for that round. it requires a medikit or other suitable supplies. battlefield pressure, filth, inadequate tools, and the nature of the injury may modify the medicine check; there is no universal stabilization dc.success stops only the deterioration that the treatment can physically address. it does not remove a mortal wound, restore lp or missing anatomy, erase lasting consequences, or automatically stop a bleeding instance. a stabilized character at 0 or negative lp remains unconscious until reaching at least 1 lp.healing magic and other plausible solutions can stabilize an injury when their own effects or the circumstances support that result.field medic treatment. removing a medically removable mortal wound requires the field medic feat, a medikit or suitable supplies, 15 minutes of treatment, and a successful medicine check at -4. treatment must begin within 10 minutes of the injury.success removes that mortal wound from the active count when the injury can be medically treated. it does not regrow a severed limb or automatically erase the wound's physical consequences. long-term lp recovery and sustained care are explained under recovery and aftermath.
219combat · wounds, dying, and death

pages.title: Spellcasting in Combat · Casting a Spell and Paying Magical Energy
pages.text:
combatspellcasting in combat
spellcasting in combatany character able to cast a spell may do so during combat. ordinary spellcasting uses the main action and cannot be combined with a full attack. combat casting is the established procedure for combining a spell with later melee attacks in the same round and for gaining its other listed protections.individual spells define their own magical energy costs, targets, ranges, areas, durations, components, saving throws, and effects. this section governs the shared combat procedure: paying for a spell, completing or losing it, casting while threatened, and casting while involved in a grapple.casting a spell and paying magical energyspell costs use magical energy (me), never magic protection (mp). before beginning, the caster must have the spell's required components—its listed speech, gestures, or materials—and enough unoccupied concentration capacity, the intelligence-modifier limit on committed spell focus. both are detailed below. declare the spell and its target or area as its rules require, then pay its full me cost when casting begins.once casting begins, schedule and resolve the spell under spell speed and scheduled completion. the spell remains in progress until that completion. a readied spell begins and pays its me only when its trigger occurs, as explained under delay, ready, and pre-combat preparation.a caster who cannot pay the full me cost cannot ordinarily begin the spell. as a last resort, the dm may permit voluntary spending into negative me and may require a will save. each complete 2 me reached below zero causes 1 lp damage: reaching -1 me causes none, reaching -2 causes 1 lp, and reaching -4 causes another 1 lp. such use may permanently damage the caster's maximum me at the dm's discretion. ordinary me-draining effects stop at 0 unless they explicitly say otherwise.if the spell's target dies or otherwise becomes invalid before completion, the spell is wasted. it produces no effect, and all me paid for it remains spent.spell interruption and failed spellsthe casting interval begins when the caster pays the spell's me and ends when the spell completes. a successful hit interrupts casting only if at least 1 actual damage remains after dr and pe mitigation. if either reduces the result to 0, the spell is not interrupted. a missed or successfully defended attack likewise does not interrupt.a successful grab—the non-damaging initiation that establishes grapple control—against a caster during this interval is also a physical interruption. other effects interrupt only when their own rule or the circumstances establish that they physically disrupt the casting.without combat casting, an interrupting hit or successful grab automatically ruins the spell. no check is made.when casting through combat casting, either trigger requires a d20 roll equal to or below half the caster's wisdom score. a fractional half is effectively rounded down because the roll is a whole number. success preserves the spell; failure ruins it.
220combat · spellcasting in combat

pages.title: Damage and Maintained Spells · Defensive Casting
pages.text:
combatspellcasting in combat
another physically disruptive effect follows its own explicit interruption rule or dm adjudication.a ruined or failed spell produces no effect. its full me cost remains spent. a readied action can interrupt a spell only if its attack or effect actually reaches the caster during the casting interval.damage and maintained spellsconcentration capacity is not itself a check, but actual damage can break spells occupying that capacity. whenever at least 1 actual damage from one result reaches a caster's temporary hp, hp, or lp, every spell that caster is maintaining through concentration is at risk. damage reduced to 0 creates no check and ends no maintained spell.without combat casting, the qualifying damage ends all such maintained spells. a character who knows combat casting instead rolls d20 equal to or below half wisdom for each qualifying damage result. success preserves the maintained spells; failure ends them. this preservation roll does not require beginning combat casting's 4-pe combined sequence.this is separate from interruption during the casting interval. damage cannot retroactively ruin a completed spell, but it can end a completed spell that remains active through maintained concentration.defensive castingbeginning an ordinary spell while threatened provokes an attack of opportunity as described under attacks of opportunity. the caster begins the spell and pays its costs before those attacks resolve. a successful hit from an attack of opportunity can therefore interrupt the spell normally.combat casting permits the caster to attempt defensive casting instead:declare defensive casting before beginning the spell.pay combat casting's 4 pe and the spell's full me cost.roll d20 equal to or below the caster's adjusted intelligence score.on success, beginning that spell does not provoke an attack of opportunity. on failure, the spell is lost and its me remains spent; it does not continue as an ordinary provoking cast. the paid pe is not refunded. defensive casting prevents only the opportunity attack caused by beginning the spell. a later hit during the casting interval can still interrupt it.the defensive casting check uses the caster's intelligence score. it is separate from the half-wisdom roll used to preserve a combat casting spell after a hit and from the intelligence modifier used for concentration capacity.combat castingcombat casting costs 4 pe total for its combined casting-and-attack sequence, in addition to the spell's me cost. do not add the ordinary 1-pe full attack cost. combat casting is the established procedure for casting a spell and making melee attacks in the same round; another explicit ability may state its own exception.use the following sequence:complete any ordinary movement before casting. the caster cannot cast, move, and then make the later attacks.if the caster intends to make follow-up attacks, they must be within melee reach when the casting sequence begins.use the first initiative pass to begin the spell, paying combat casting's 4 pe and the spell's me.choose one qualifying one-handed melee weapon when the sequence begins. each of its remaining attack passes that round may be used for one melee attack with that weapon.combat casting does not create attack passes. if the caster has no later pass, it grants no follow-up attack.the combat casting procedure also permits defensive casting, changes successful-hit interruption from automatic failure to the half-wisdom check, protects maintained spells through the same half-wisdom target, and supplies the somatic-component exception described below while controlling a grapple or being grappled. it does not grant an additional spell.
221combat · spellcasting in combat

pages.title: Example: Combat Casting Through Multiple Passes · Components, Concentration, and Grappling
pages.text:
combatspellcasting in combat
example: combat casting through multiple passesa caster chooses a one-handed melee weapon whose current attack speed is 3. they move into melee before beginning the sequence, then use the first pass to cast, paying 4 pe plus the spell's me cost. the second and third passes may each make one attack with that weapon. do not add the ordinary 1-pe full attack cost. if a hit during the casting interval is reduced to 0 actual damage by dr or pe mitigation, it does not interrupt; if at least 1 actual damage remains, the caster must pass the half-wisdom preservation roll.components, concentration, and grapplingspell components use these letters:v — verbal: the caster must be able to speak.s — somatic: the caster must be able to perform the spell's gestures.m — material: the caster must have access to and use the listed material, commonly from a component satchel. the material is expended only when the component or spell says so.concentration capacity measures how much spell focus a caster can commit at once. capacity is not itself an interruption check, although actual damage can break maintained spells under damage and maintained spells above. capacity equals the caster's intelligence modifier, and a spell writes its requirement as initial/maintenance:the first number is the unoccupied capacity required to begin casting.the second number is the capacity that remains occupied while the spell is maintained.do not add the two numbers during casting. the capacity that meets the initial requirement can immediately become the maintained capacity.1/- requires 1 free capacity to cast and occupies none afterward.a bare entry such as 1, or an entry written as 1/, is read as 1/- unless an explicit rule supplies a maintenance requirement.for example, a caster with intelligence 12 has concentration capacity 1. after casting and maintaining a 1/1 spell, that capacity is occupied and the caster cannot begin another spell requiring 1 free capacity until it becomes available.a caster may voluntarily release one or more maintained spells as a free action during that caster's own turn, never off-turn as a reaction. unconsciousness, death, or becoming stunned ends all maintained spells. paralysis alone does not. if concentration capacity falls below the amount occupied, enough maintained spells end to fit the new capacity. a spell, condition, or other explicit rule may provide a more specific ending condition.in a grapple, the controller maintains the hold and the grappled target is held; the complete procedure appears under grab and grapple. without combat casting, either participant may cast only a spell that requires no somatic component. combat casting permits the caster to omit the somatic component while controlling a grapple or while grappled, but it does not waive verbal or material components. a grapple option, the spell's own text, or another condition may impose further restrictions.a grab that establishes control over a spell already in progress uses the interruption procedure above. being a controller or grappled does not create a separate intelligence check to maintain a spell.
222combat · spellcasting in combat

pages.title: Combat Maneuvers · Roll-Under and Opposed Checks
pages.text:
combatcombat maneuvers
combat maneuverscombat maneuvers use attacks, leverage, and trained techniques to do more than inflict ordinary weapon damage. the relevant feat, talent, or class feature determines whether a character is trained in a maneuver. this section supplies the shared resolution procedure; equipment determines weapon properties, and talents and feats determines access to trained use.roll-under and opposed checksskills — attribute checks and skill checks owns the universal roll-under procedure, while skills — opposed checks and check margin owns the general opposed-check and check-margin procedure. the compact calculation below is retained here so the combat maneuvers can be resolved in place. a maneuver's stated threshold, bab contribution, cost, result, and exceptional margin remain specific to that maneuver.disarm, hard trip, and bash use roll-under checks based on raw ability scores rather than ability modifiers. build the threshold named by the maneuver:adjusted threshold = relevant ability score + bab when stated + applicable modifiersroll d20. a result equal to or below the adjusted threshold succeeds. bonuses raise the threshold; penalties and difficulty lower it. natural 1 and natural 20 have no separate automatic effect on a roll-under check; compare the die with the threshold normally. when the rules say to beat an ability check, they mean to roll equal to or below this threshold. routine actions without meaningful pressure may require no roll, and an unmodified threshold of 20 cannot fail an ordinary d20 check.the result's check margin is:check margin = adjusted threshold -
