d20 resultin an unopposed check, a margin of 0 or more succeeds. in an opposed check, both participants roll and the higher check margin wins, even when both margins are negative. a tie favors the defender.when an opposed result succeeds or fails by 8 or more, the winning check margin exceeds the losing margin by at least 8. in an unopposed check, failure by 8 or more means a check margin of -8 or lower. check margin is distinct from an attack's margin of success.example: opposed roll-under marginsan attacker with adjusted threshold 20 rolls 23, producing check margin -3. the defender with threshold 18 rolls 20, producing margin -2. both missed their thresholds, but -2 is the higher and therefore less severe failure, so the defender wins. if both margins had been -2, the defender would also win because opposed ties favor the defender.maneuver costs and limitsa character is trained when a named talent, feat, class feature, or other explicit ability grants trained use of that maneuver. a character without that permission is untrained when the maneuver allows an untrained attempt.maneuvertrained useuntrained usedisarm1 pe and one attack1 pe, the entire main action, and -4 to the thresholdhard trip2 pe and one attack2 pe, the entire main action, and -4 to the thresholdbash2 pe and one attack2 pe, the entire main action, and -4 to the thresholda cost of one attack consumes one available attack pass. a trained maneuver can replace an attack during a full attack, and any other passes remain available. add its listed pe cost to the full attack's ordinary 1 pe cost. an untrained attempt cannot be inserted into a full attack.each distinct named combat maneuver can normally be attempted only once per round unless its own rule says otherwise. different maneuvers may be combined in the same round when the character can pay every cost and has the necessary attacks.
223combat · combat maneuvers

pages.title: Disarm · Hard Trip and Bash
pages.text:
combatcombat maneuvers
for disarm, hard trip, and bash, a difference of one creature-size category grants +4 to the larger participant's threshold. when the defender does not roll, apply every defender-favoring size, weapon, or situational modifier as an equal penalty to the attacker's threshold; never apply both sides of the same modifier. at a difference of two or more categories in either direction, these maneuvers are unavailable; use an action suited to the scale difference instead.combat maneuvers do not provoke attacks of opportunity merely because they are maneuvers. each maneuver states any trigger it creates.disarmdisarm attempts to force a held weapon from an opponent's grasp. use the attacker's and defender's training to determine the check:attackerdefenderdisarm checktraineduntrainedunopposed dexterity-score check; do not add babtrainedtrainedopposed dexterity score + bab checksuntraineduntrainedunopposed dexterity score - 4 check; do not add babuntrainedtrainedthe attempt cannot succeed; the dm may conceal this behind a rollthe -4 in the untrained-versus-untrained row is the general untrained penalty already included; do not apply it twice.on success, the defender drops the targeted weapon in the same 5-foot square they occupy.apply the shared creature-size modifier and these weapon advantages:the holder of the heavier weapon gains +2, regardless of how many weapon-category steps separate the weapons.a participant wielding their weapon in two hands against a participant who is not gains +4.these two bonuses stack.apply any situational modifier to only one participant's threshold. in an unopposed check, use the shared defender-modifier procedure above. magic, unusual equipment, locked gauntlets, immunity, and other explicit circumstances may modify or prevent the attempt.if the attacker fails disarm by 8 or more, the attacker drops their own weapon unless a specific protection prevents it. disarm failure does not otherwise provoke an attack of opportunity.hard trip and bashhard trip and bash knock an opponent prone. resolve them as opposed roll-under checks:maneuverattacker's thresholddefender's thresholdattacker winsdefender wins by 8 or morehard tripstrength or dexterity score + babstrength or dexterity score + babdefender becomes proneattacker becomes pronebashstrength score + babstrength or dexterity score + babdefender becomes proneattacker becomes prone
224combat · combat maneuvers

pages.title: Heavy Attack · Example: Paying for a Heavy Attack
pages.text:
combatcombat maneuvers
for hard trip, attacker and defender choose strength or dexterity independently. both combatants must have their feet on the ground. a bash attacker always uses strength; its defender chooses strength or dexterity.a tie favors the defender. if the defender wins by less than 8, the attempt has no additional result. becoming prone immediately applies the complete prone condition, including its effect on unresolved attack passes.if a bash attacker wins by 8 or more, they may also initiate a grapple immediately without another attack or pe cost. the attacker drops held objects and follows the target down; resolve the initiation and all later control under grab and grapple.only a failed untrained hard trip or bash provokes an attack of opportunity. a trained failure and a successful untrained attempt do not provoke.heavy attacka heavy attack is a special maneuver made with a weapon formally classified as heavy and wielded in both hands. a non-heavy two-handed weapon does not qualify.heavy attack has no separate maneuver pe cost. it is performed as a full attack and therefore costs the ordinary 1 pe, including when using the one-attack fallback below.normally, heavy attack consumes two unused attacks from the current round but resolves as one attack during one chosen pass:choose a pass while at least two attacks remain unused.consume the current attack and one other unused attack from the round.make one attack at -2 attack.a character with two attacks must therefore heavy attack on the first pass. a character with three attacks may attack normally on the first pass and heavy attack on the second, consuming the final two attacks.if the character began the round with only one attack, they may instead make a heavy attack at initiative count 0 with -5 attack instead of -2. this fallback is unavailable when the round began with two or more attacks and the character merely spent or lost attacks until only one remained.on a hit:double the number of the weapon's damage dice: 2d6 becomes 4d6, and 1d12 becomes 2d12.do not double fixed damage modifiers.increase the attack's effective margin of success by 4, then apply that margin once through the ordinary damage calculation.add +1 pen, then resolve armor penetration, armor grade, material modifiers, and unaffected flat dr under damage reduction, armor penetration, and armor grade.if the heavy attack misses, only the opponent who successfully defended against it may make an attack of opportunity. that response uses the defender's ordinary attack-of-opportunity allowance and procedure.example: paying for a heavy attacka character beginning the round with three attacks may attack normally on the first pass, then declare heavy attack on the second. that one heavy attack consumes both remaining attacks and is rolled at -2 attack. a 2d6 heavy weapon becomes 4d6; if the dice total 15, strength is +4, and the ordinary margin is 3, heavy attack raises the effective margin to 7 for 26 raw damage. the weapon's pen 3 becomes pen 4. against heavy armor with grade 3 and listed dr 9, this applies half dr, rounded down to 4, leaving 22 damage before pe mitigation and hp.a character who began with only one attack may instead make the heavy attack at initiative 0 with -5 attack. a character who began with two attacks must use heavy attack on the first pass.
225combat · combat maneuvers

pages.title: Grab and Grapple · Starting a Grab
pages.text:
combatgrab and grapple
grab and grapplea grab is a non-damaging melee attack used to establish physical control. once control is established, the combatants take two roles:the controller maintains the hold.the grappled target is the creature being held. the controller is not themselves grappled.standing or ground position is descriptive unless an effect such as takedown applies prone.starting a grabnormal grab is available without special training. improved grapple requires an explicit feat, talent, or class feature.methodpe costaction costattack modifiernormal grab1 peentire main action-2 attackimproved grapple1 pereplaces one attackno penaltyimproved grapple can replace an attack during a full attack. its 1 pe cost is added to the full attack's ordinary 1 pe cost, and later attack passes may be used for grapple options. normal grab consumes the main action and provides no later attack passes unless an explicit rule says otherwise.a grab attack uses the ordinary armed or unarmed melee attack formula, followed by the grab modifiers in this section. it can only be dodged; it cannot be parried or blocked. an unarmed grab attack requires at least one free hand. an armed grab attack can begin with the weapon used for the grab in hand, subject to the weapon rules below.a grab attack deals no damage. a specific creature ability may instead deal damage and establish control together.when a bash succeeds by 8 or more and grants its free grapple initiation, proceed directly to the post-contact strength contest. do not make another grab attack and do not grant the defender the special free attack described below.weapon edge and establishing controlweapon edge applies when the defender has a ready weapon whose reach or threat is clearly superior to the attacker's means of approach. treat weapon edge as one -4 circumstance; do not add separate handedness, reach, or weapon-category modifiers. it stacks with normal grab's -2.resolve a grab in this order:resolve the defender's free attack. normal grab grants one special free attack to an armed defender before the grab attack. improved grapple prevents this attack unless the defender has weapon edge. this is a special free weapon attack resolved normally, not an attack of opportunity, and it does not use the defender's attack-of-opportunity allowance. if it deals at least 1 actual damage, the grab attempt ends. a hit that results in 0 actual damage does not stop the attempt.make the grab attack. resolve the non-damaging attack against dodge. a smaller target gains +2 dodge per creature-size category against the grab attack.set the attacker's weapons. if the grab attack connects, the attacker drops every non-light weapon before the post-contact contest. the attacker may retain one light weapon.contest control. both participants make opposed roll-under checks using strength score + bab. the larger participant gains +8 to their threshold per creature-size category. compare check margins as described under roll-under and opposed checks. the higher margin wins, and a tie favors the defender. dexterity cannot substitute unless an explicit ability permits it.assign the roles. if the defender wins, the grab ends and control does not reverse. if the attacker wins, the attacker becomes the controller and the defender becomes the grappled target.
226combat · grab and grapple

pages.title: Example: Establishing Grapple Control · Maintaining and Moving a Grapple
pages.text:
combatgrab and grapple
the same +8 per category applies to escape, takedown, pin, and other post-contact strength contests. at a difference of two or more categories, the smaller participant cannot win an ordinary post-contact grapple contest without exceptional, magical, or outside assistance.armor provides no universal modifier to a post-contact strength contest. an explicit armor or equipment rule may modify the initial grab attack.example: establishing grapple controlan unarmed character uses normal grab against a ready spearman. normal grab applies -2 attack, weapon edge adds another -4, and the spearman receives the special free attack. the free attack hits, but after applicable dr its final damage is 0, so the grab continues. the adjusted grab attack is 21 against dodge 18 and connects.the attacker then checks strength score + bab with threshold 24 and rolls 10, giving margin 14. the defender has threshold 20 and rolls 9, giving margin 11. the attacker wins and becomes the controller. improved grapple against a defender without weapon edge would remove the normal grab penalty and special free attack, replace one attack, and cost 1 pe in addition to any full attack cost.maintaining and moving a grapplea grappled target cannot use ordinary movement independently and cannot use a medium, heavy, or two-handed weapon. the controller cannot retain or use a non-light weapon while maintaining control. neither participant suffers an additional blanket dexterity or attack penalty merely because of the grapple.a controller who entered through normal grab must spend one attack at the beginning of each later round to maintain control. improved grapple maintains control without this attack cost. there is no general maintenance pe cost beyond the heavy-armor rule.each heavy-armored participant spends 1 pe immediately when control is established and again at the start of every later round in which they grapple.a heavy-armored controller unable to pay releases control.a heavy-armored grappled target unable to pay cannot attempt escape or oppose an optional controller maneuver during that round. the controller must still succeed on the resulting unopposed check; the maneuver does not succeed automatically.the controller may release the target freely during their own turn or as a reaction before resolving an incoming attack, effect, save, or defense. release immediately ends control.during first-pass movement, the controller may drag a same-size or smaller grappled target at half speed. one controller cannot drag a larger target. the dm may allow several assistants to drag a larger target.controller and grappled-target optionsthe controller may spend remaining attack passes on the options below. unless stated otherwise, each option costs one attack. each distinct named maneuver can be attempted once per round; strike is an ordinary attack and may repeat when the participant has further attacks.controller optionprocedurestrikemake an ordinary unarmed attack or an attack with one retained light weapon.constrictonce per round, deal damage equal to the controller's strength modifier. this bypasses physical armor dr, but not magical or supernatural protection, and follows the normal hp-to-lp order.takedownonce per round, make opposed strength score + bab checks. a tie favors the grappled target. on success, the target becomes prone and control continues. failure does not end or reverse control.
227combat · grab and grapple

pages.title: Pin and Choke
pages.text:
combatgrab and grapple
the grappled target has the following options:grapple-target optionprocedureescapeonce per round, spend one attack and contest strength score + bab against the controller's strength score + bab. a tie favors the controller. dexterity cannot substitute without an explicit ability. success ends control.strikemake an unarmed or retained light-weapon attack at -4 attack. the controller may release as a reaction to avoid the attack.spell or abilityuse it only when its own action, component, and grapple permissions allow it.speechbrief speech, cries, and similar vocal activity require no special grapple action unless pin, choke, or another explicit effect prevents them.pin and chokepin is a controller maneuver that costs one attack and can be attempted once per round. make opposed roll-under checks:controller: strength score + bab - 4grappled target: strength score + baba tie favors the grappled target. on success, the target is pinned by the pin maneuver and may only attempt escape or perform a mental or verbal action that is explicitly permitted. a failed pin does not end ordinary grapple control.pin must be maintained in each later round. an action that explicitly requires or uses pin counts as that round's pin maintenance. if the controller performs no such action, they must spend one attack solely to maintain pin.an attack spent maintaining pin, establishing choke, or continuing choke also maintains the underlying normal grab for that round. these costs do not stack. improved grapple removes only the ordinary grab-maintenance cost; it does not remove pin or choke maintenance.choke can be established only after the controller has successfully pinned a target with compatible vulnerable anatomy and a relevant need for circulation or respiration. exceptional anatomies are adjudicated by the dm.establishing choke costs one attack.continuing choke costs one attack in each later round.establishing or continuing choke also maintains pin for that round.ongoing pin and choke therefore cost one attack total per round.establishing both pin and choke in the same round costs two attacks, one for each initial maneuver.the choke dc is:10 + half the controller's main job level, rounded down + strength modifier + artif several jobs are tied for highest level, the first-acquired job is main.resolve choke in this order:maintain choke through one complete round.at the end of the target's next turn, the target makes the first fortitude save. meeting the dc succeeds.repeat the save at the end of every later turn while choke remains maintained. the first save has no elapsed-time penalty. the second suffers -4, the third -8, and each later save suffers another cumulative -4. apply this penalty to the save; do not also increase the dc.the first failed save renders the target unconscious. the target remains grappled while control continues.if choke is released, an otherwise unharmed target remains unconscious for 1d4 rounds, then wakes unless another injury or condition prevents it.if choke continues after unconsciousness, the target's next turn is a complete maintained grace round and causes no lp loss. the target loses the first 1 lp at the end of the following turn, then another 1 lp at the end of every later turn while choke remains maintained. this damage bypasses hp and physical dr. ordinary negative-lp, mortal wound, and death rules then apply.
228combat · grab and grapple

pages.title: Example: Maintaining Grapple, Pin, and Choke · Outside Attacks, Area Effects, and Spellcasting
pages.text:
combatgrab and grapple
example: maintaining grapple, pin, and chokea character with attack speed 3 begins a full attack and spends 1 pe. the first pass uses improved grapple, costing another 1 pe and establishing control. the second pass successfully establishes pin; the third establishes choke. establishing pin and choke requires two separate attacks.in the next round, spending one attack to continue choke also maintains pin and the underlying grapple. at the end of the target's turn, they make the first fortitude save with no elapsed-time penalty. if choke continues, the next save is at -4 and the third is at -8. suppose the target fails the second save: they become unconscious. if released, they wake in 1d4 rounds unless something else prevents it. if choke continues, the target's next turn is the grace round with no lp loss; the first 1 lp is lost at the end of the following turn.a controller who intends to use only the one attack required to maintain choke need not declare a full attack. to maintain the hold and use later attack passes for additional strikes or other grapple options, the controller declares a full attack and pays its ordinary 1 pe.outside attacks, area effects, and spellcastingwhen an outside attacker attacks either participant, the attacker declares the intended target and the controller chooses whether to maintain or release control before the attack resolves.choiceresolutionmaintain controluse static defense 10 + controller bab + applicable passive defensive modifiers; do not roll an active defense. add magical and other always-active defense bonuses, but not dexterity, active dodge, or weapon/shield parry or block bonuses. no active-defense use is spent. on a miss, neither participant is hit. on a hit, roll an equal 50/50 chance to determine which participant receives that same hit, margin of success, and damage.release controldo not make the 50/50 roll. the attack resolves normally against its declared target, which is no longer part of a grapple.area effects affect both participants normally and never use the 50/50 procedure. the controller may release as a reaction before making an applicable save or defense.a grab that establishes control over a caster during a casting interval is a physical interruption resolved under spell interruption and failed spells. casting while controlling or grappled follows components, concentration, and grappling. being in a grapple creates no separate intelligence check to maintain a spell.example: attacking someone in a grapplean archer targets the controller, whose grapple defense is 15. the controller maintains control; the archer's attack 19 connects with margin 4, then a 50/50 roll determines whether the controller or grappled target receives that same hit, margin, and damage. if the controller releases before the attack, the archer instead attacks the declared target normally and no 50/50 roll occurs. a fireball or another area effect affects both participants and never uses the 50/50 procedure.

pages.title: Mounted Combat · Basic Mounted Combat
pages.text:
combatmounted combat
mounted combata mounted pair consists of a rider and mount while the rider remains mounted. the pair shares the rider's initiative, moves together during first-pass movement, and uses the mount's speed. ride governs ordinary mounted control; mounted combat and mounted archer provide the trained combat permissions summarized here.basic mounted combatdo not roll a separate ordinary initiative for the mount. the pair follows the normal movement and main action sequence, using the mount's movement. after the rider is dismounted, the mount behaves as the dm judges appropriate for that creature and situation.the procedures below begin with a rider trained in ride.rider trainingmounted melee allowanceride onlyat most one melee attack per round, using a one-handed weapon. additional mounted melee attacks and a mounted melee full attack automatically fail.mounted combatuse normal melee attack speed and action rules. a melee full attack is permitted and costs the ordinary 1 pe.the rider may defend normally at either tier.mounted combat also automatically redirects an attack aimed at the mount to the rider.
230combat · mounted combat

pages.title: Mounted Charges · Remaining Mounted After Damage
pages.text:
combatmounted combat
mounted chargesa mounted charge follows the ordinary charge procedure: it consumes movement and the main action, follows a straight and clear route, permits one melee attack rather than a full attack, and may provoke attacks of opportunity during movement. a fatigued or exhausted rider cannot charge.every legal mounted charge adds +1 pen to its melee attack. this is a situational modifier and does not change the weapon's printed pen.for a rider with mounted combat, use the following situational attack bonuses:mounted melee attacktargetmounted combat bonusordinary attackmounted opponent or large or larger creature+0ordinary attackmedium or smaller opponent on foot+4mounted chargemounted opponent or large or larger creature+4mounted chargemedium or smaller opponent on foot+8the mounted-charge +4 replaces the ordinary charge's +2; it does not stack with that +2. the separate +4 against a medium or smaller opponent on foot does stack with the mounted-charge +4, producing the +8 shown above. the mounted-charge +4 applies to every legal mounted charge and does not require 30 feet of movement or a particular weapon.a rider with mounted combat does not suffer the ordinary charge's -2 defense during a mounted charge.if the charge travels at least 30 feet along a straight, clear line and uses a weapon explicitly qualified for mounted charges, double the number of that weapon's damage dice. this requirement affects only the doubled weapon dice; it does not determine either attack bonus. add fixed damage modifiers once.equipment determines which weapons qualify for the doubled-dice benefit.remaining mounted after damagewhen one damaging event deals a mounted rider at least 10 actual damage, immediately make one roll-under ride check. the ride score is the rider's dexterity score plus any explicit ride modifiers, reduced by 1 for every point of actual damage beyond 10.at exactly 10 damage, the check has no damage penalty. eleven damage imposes -1, twelve imposes -2, and each further point of damage imposes another -1. this is one ride check, not a dexterity check followed by a second skill check.on failure, the rider is dismounted and becomes prone immediately. this procedure causes no additional universal falling damage. the mount then behaves as the dm judges appropriate.mounted ranged combatuse the mount's greatest movement during the round to determine the penalty, and apply that penalty to every ranged attack the rider makes during that round.rider trainingmount stationaryordinary movementdouble movementrunrider's ranged attacksride only+0-2-4unavailableat most one; no full attackmounted combat+0+0-2-4at most one; no full attackmounted archer+0+0-2-4normal ranged attack speed; full attack permitted
231combat · mounted combat

pages.title: Example: Mounted Ranged Combat · Mounted Archer and Mounted Weapons
pages.text:
combatmounted combat
stationary means that the mount does not move during the round. unavailable means that a ride-only rider cannot make a ranged attack during a round in which the mount runs.the mount's movement determines the table result without consuming the rider's permitted ranged main action. this is a specific exception that allows a mounted combat or mounted archer rider to fire after the mount runs. it does not grant another main action, full attack, or personal movement.mounted combat alone continues to permit only one mounted ranged attack. mounted archer requires trained ride and mounted combat, permits normal ranged attack speed, and permits a ranged full attack. that full attack costs the ordinary 1 pe. all mounted movement must finish before its first attack; its attacks cannot be distributed along the mount's route.example: mounted ranged combata rider with mounted combat may let the mount use ordinary movement and then make one ranged attack at no movement penalty, but cannot make a ranged full attack. a mounted archer with attack speed 2.5 on the high side of the schedule may finish a double movement, spend 1 pe, and then make three ranged attacks at -2 each. a ride-only rider cannot make a ranged attack during a round in which the mount runs.mounted archer and mounted weaponswithout mounted archer, ordinary legal mounted-ranged examples include a shortbow, a suitable thrown weapon, and an already-loaded crossbow, subject to their equipment entries.a warbow cannot be used while mounted, even with mounted archer. a purpose-built mounted bow may explicitly override this restriction in its equipment entry.an already-loaded crossbow can be fired while mounted. reloading a crossbow while mounted:consumes the rider's main action and entire personal effort for the round;prevents the rider from also attacking or casting that round;requires the rider not to be engaged in melee; andrequires the mount to be stopped while the crossbow is actually being reloaded. the mount may use ordinary movement before or after the reload.mounted archer does not automatically improve mounted crossbow reloading. a feat, talent, or weapon may supply a specific exception.the complete mounted combat and mounted archer entries belong in talents and feats. equipment owns mount statistics and speed, qualifying mounted-charge weapons, mounted bows, and weapon-specific loading exceptions.example: firing and reloading a mounted crossbowa rider may fire an already-loaded crossbow as their permitted ranged attack. reloading it on a later round consumes the main action and prevents attacking or casting. the mount may move before or after the reload, but must be stopped while the crossbow is actually being reloaded.
232combat · mounted combat

pages.title: Golem Frame Combat
pages.text:
combatgolem frame combat
golem frame combatan elven-interface golem frame is the pilot's constructed combat body. pilot and frame share one initiative position, one movement, and one main action; the frame is not a separate creature receiving another turn. use the complete golem frames chapter for qualification, profile values, formulas, awareness, magical energy costs, system damage, and repair.the universal combat engine remains in force with these bridges:initiative and movement: frame initiative uses pilot wisdom, the printed frame initiative modifier, and golem piloting competence. use the frame's speed, size, reach, physical attributes, and domain ranks.attacks and attack speed: the pilot supplies bab. the frame supplies physical str or dex, weapons, damage, pen, and frame attack speed. personal attack speed and personal attack engines do not transfer unless a frame rule expressly permits them.exertion: a frame has no pe or constitution-based endurance. full attack, run, charge, and permitted maneuvers spend pilot me as stated in the subsystem. pilot pe cannot reduce frame damage.defenses: an aware pilot may roll a profile-listed aware defense or choose passive defense. a failed broader-awareness check and operational flat-footed state use passive defense. genuine surprise uses surprised defense. an inert frame, or a frame lacking a conscious physically capable operator, uses no-bab inert defense. ordinary defense declarations, legal responses, use counts, and escalating -4/-8/-12 penalties otherwise remain unchanged.damage: ordinary attack, margin, pen, grade, dr, and critical-dice procedures apply. a frame critical that loses at least 1 lp invokes system damage, and its remaining critical damage bypasses frame hp for frame lp. frames have no lethal damage category.effects and conditions: determine whether an effect legally targets the pilot, frame, or both, then resolve each legal target separately. frames gain no blanket monster golem or construct immunities.treat a frame pilot as mounted only when an effect meaningfully applies to fighting from a larger carried combat body, substituting golem piloting for ride when mounted control is required. do not apply ordinary mount attack redirection, separate mount initiative or actions, dismount-on-damage, or mount morale.
233combat · golem frame combat

pages.title: Groups and Combat Units · Outnumbering
pages.text:
combatgroups and combat units
groups and combat unitsoutnumberinga combatant facing more than one effective opponent in melee takes -2 attack and -2 defense for each effective opponent beyond the first, to a maximum penalty of -8.effective oppositionattack and defense penalty1:102:1-23:1-44:1-65:1 or worse-8in group-versus-group combat, the dm compares the meaningful local numbers and converts that ratio into effective opponents per defender. minor differences that do not create a meaningful local advantage are ignored; ten combatants against eight ordinarily causes no outnumbering penalty.only opponents who can meaningfully bring their numbers to bear count toward the penalty. creating this pressure requires no special feat, and no current feat automatically removes the resulting penalty.character-scale combat unitsa combat unit represents at least four broadly similar combatants as one character-scale formation. it makes one aggregate attack instead of rolling once per member. its effective strength provides its melee formation bonus, its contributors determine impact and the contribution bonus, and the target defends once. meeting the unit's attack removes 1 impact, and every additional full 4 points of defensive margin removes 1 more. the remaining impact determines how many sets of weapon damage dice are rolled.the unit uses one representative profile, one initiative, ordinary movement, one main action, and attack speed 1. it cannot full attack unless an explicit unit rule permits it. with fewer than four current members, the survivors act individually.effective strength equals current membership, to a maximum of 20.actual membership may exceed 20. surplus members are casualty buffers and replacements: they do not increase that unit's formation bonus, available contributors, impact, or contribution bonus. those values begin declining only when membership falls below 20. a 30-member unit therefore retains effective strength 20 until it falls to 19 members. a larger body may instead be divided into several combat units, each acting and calculating its values separately.unit valuecalculationmelee formation bonus+1 attack per two points of effective strength, rounded down, to a maximum of +10. this applies only in melee.impact1 per two effective contributors assigned to the target, rounded up. an aggregate attack cannot use more contributors than the unit's effective strength.contribution bonus+2 attack per impact after the first, to a maximum of +8.do not also apply outnumbering from the same members against the unit's aggregate attack.
234combat · groups and combat units

pages.title: Page 235
pages.text:
combatgroups and combat units
choose contributors and attack:melee: choose one unit member touching the target as the lead attacker. the lead attacker and every unit member touching the lead attacker may contribute, regardless of ordinary reach. a member may contribute against only one target during that aggregate attack. roll 1d20 + representative attack bonus + melee formation bonus + contribution bonus.ranged: assign each participating shooter to one target before rolling; every assigned shooter must be able to make the shot. roll one shared d20 + representative attack bonus, then add each target's own contribution bonus. each target defends and takes damage separately. twenty archers concentrating on one target still make only one attack roll.resolve the attack:the target makes one normally legal defense roll.if defense is lower than attack, remove no impact. if defense meets or exceeds attack, remove 1 impact, plus 1 additional impact for every full 4 points by which defense exceeds attack.combine one complete set of the weapon's damage dice per remaining impact into one damage-dice expression. apply the four-damage-dice conversion once to that complete expression, then roll it. add the representative fixed damage modifiers once and any positive attack margin of success once.use the representative weapon's pen for the whole aggregate attack; impact never increases it. compare pen with each target's grade, apply that target's grade-sensitive and flat dr once to the combined damage, then route it through hp and lp. because this is one damage result, existing pe mitigation applies normally.combat units cannot score critical hits.
235combat · groups and combat units

pages.title: Example: Combat Unit Formation and Defense · Relationship to Mass Combat
pages.text:
combatgroups and combat units
example: combat unit formation and defenseformation example. a twenty-member veteran warrior unit has bab 6 and a +3 ability modifier, giving it a +9 representative attack before equipment. its melee formation bonus is +10. five contributors produce 3 impact and +4 contribution, so it attacks at +23 before the d20. if it rolls 12, its total attack is 35. against defense 31, all 3 impact remain and its positive attack margin is 4. with 1d8 + 3 weapons, the combined damage is 3d8 + 3 + 4. if those weapons have pen 2 and the target has grade 2 armor with dr 4, equal pen and grade leave dr 4 unchanged; subtract it once from the combined result, not once per impact.if the defense were instead 40, meeting attack would remove 1 impact and the first full 4 points within its defensive margin of 5 would remove 1 more. the remaining 1 impact would deal 1d8 + 3: meeting the aggregate attack always removes the first impact, and every additional full 4 points removes another.successful dodge example. twenty archers focus on aslan, producing 10 impact. their total attack is 20 and aslan's dodge is 28. meeting attack removes 1 impact, and his defensive margin of 8 removes 2 more, leaving 7, so the successful dodge still leaves damage to resolve. their 1d8 bows produce a combined 7d8 damage-dice expression, which becomes 4d8 + 6 before the roll. add the representative fixed damage modifier once, and add no attack margin because their attack did not exceed his defense. compare the representative bow's pen with aslan's grade once, then apply his resulting grade-sensitive and flat dr once to that combined damage. this is seven weapon-dice sets combined into one converted damage result, not seven copies of one archer's complete damage total.relationship to mass combatcharacter-scale combat units, small-unit tactics, and mass combat are three separate systems:character-scale combat units compress several similar combatants into one initiative and aggregate attack within ordinary character combat.small-unit tactics provides command points for tactical coordination and leadership within ordinary character combat.mass combat resolves battles at command scale.do not transfer actions, bonuses, command points, or procedures between these systems unless an explicit rule says otherwise.
236combat · groups and combat units

pages.title: Recovery and Aftermath · Rest Periods
pages.text:
combatrecovery and aftermath
recovery and aftermathrest periodsvanaheim uses the following rest terms throughout this chapter:short rest: a pause that the dm judges sufficient for short-rest recovery in the current circumstances. no universal duration has been established. it permits the hp recovery described below and the deliberately flexible short-rest pe recovery; it does not automatically remove fatigued or exhausted.complete rest: rest without strenuous activity for whatever period a rule specifies. complete rest describes the quality of the rest, not a separate fixed duration. the one-hour recovery steps for exhausted and fatigue-induced unconsciousness use complete rest.long rest: eight hours of complete rest. earlier rules may call the same recovery period a full rest. a long rest restores all naturally restorable hp, restores all pe, and removes the entire fatigue ladder. it does not automatically restore lp.reasonable interruptions during a long rest are adjudicated by the dm. these rules do not require minute-by-minute tracking or add separate recovery periods to the same eight hours.hit point recoveryafter a qualifying short rest, recover hp according to the character's main job family. use the main job's level, count no more than 20 levels, round every fractional number of dice up, and add the constitution modifier once.main job familyshort-rest hp recoverylevel-20 resultwarriorroll one d6 for every 2 main job levels, rounding up; add the constitution modifier once.roll ten d6 and add the constitution modifier once.adventurerroll one d6 for every 2 main job levels, rounding up; add the constitution modifier once.roll ten d6 and add the constitution modifier once.acolyteroll one d6 for every 3 main job levels, rounding up; add the constitution modifier once.roll seven d6 and add the constitution modifier once.mageroll one d6 for every 5 main job levels, rounding up; add the constitution modifier once.roll four d6 and add the constitution modifier once.recovery cannot exceed the character's missing restorable hp. if the total after applying the constitution modifier is 0 or less, no hp is restored; there is no separate minimum recovery.a long rest fully restores the character's hp to the current maximum. recovery does not distinguish whether that maximum was increased by a job, training, worn armor, or another source.temporary hp cannot be healed or restored through rest. any other special hp buffer follows the recovery rules given by the effect that grants it. mage armor, for example, must be renewed rather than healed.short-rest hp recovery does not replace or determine the separate, flexible short-rest pe recovery.
237combat · recovery and aftermath

pages.title: Life Point Recovery and Long-Term Care
pages.text:
combatrecovery and aftermath
life point recovery and long-term carelp recovery depends on the character's current wound band. use the faster rate only after recovery has moved the character into that less severe band.current wound bandrest without sustained caresustained competent carelight1 lp per dayconstitution modifier in lp per day (minimum 1)serious1 lp per 3 daysconstitution modifier in lp per 3 days (minimum 1)criticalno natural recoveryconstitution modifier in lp per 7 days (minimum 1)at exactly 0 lp or any survivable negative lp value, use the critical recovery rate. the character cannot recover lp without sustained competent care and recovers lp equal to the constitution modifier every seven days with that care, to a minimum of 1 lp. this borrows only the recovery rate: exactly 0 remains outside the positive wound bands, and negative lp remains the deadly wound band.a character trained in medicine can provide sustained competent long-term care. the dm determines whether the care qualifies and whether the circumstances require or modify a medicine check. hospitals, field conditions, weather, and available supplies may matter; there is no universal check dc or check cadence.field medic is not required for sustained long-term care. it remains the specialized urgent-care feat used for eligible mortal wound treatment and the dangerous bleeding procedures described under wounds, dying, and death.a character recovering at 0 or negative lp remains unconscious until reaching at least 1 lp, unless another condition independently prevents consciousness. restoring lp does not automatically stop bleeding, remove a mortal wound, restore missing anatomy, or erase another lasting consequence.cure spell eligibility. cure tiers are cumulative for lp wounds: a higher-tier spell can heal its own wound tier and every lower tier.spelllp wound severities it can healcure lightlightcure serious woundslight and seriouscure critical woundslight, serious, critical, exactly 0 lp, and deadly (negative lp)a lower-tier cure cannot restore lp while the target is in a more severe wound band. cure critical wounds is therefore required at 0 or negative lp. this table determines eligibility only; the spell's own entry determines how much lp it restores.when a cure spell can restore both hp and eligible lp, roll its healing amount once for that recipient. the result is one shared healing pool. each point restores either 1 missing hp or 1 eligible lp and can be spent only once; combined hp and lp restoration cannot exceed the roll. there is no required hp-first or lp-first order, and any points that cannot or need not be spent are unused. the pool does not produce a second copy of the roll for lp and does not automatically restore all eligible lp. cure light wounds, mass rolls once for the casting and gives each chosen living recipient a separate pool equal to that one result rather than dividing one pool among the group.
238combat · recovery and aftermath

pages.title: Example: One Shared Cure Pool · Example: Recovering Through Multiple Wound Bands
pages.text:
combatrecovery and aftermath
example: one shared cure poolcure serious wounds rolls 9 for a living recipient at full hp and 9/12 lp in the light band. spend 3 points to restore the recipient to 12/12 lp; the remaining 6 points are unused.if a cure spell instead rolls 9 for a recipient missing 4 hp and 7 eligible lp, it could restore 4 hp and 5 lp, 2 hp and 7 lp, or another legal combination totaling no more than 9. it cannot restore 9 hp and then also restore lp from a second copy of the roll.bleeding uses its separate light / moderate / serious severity scale and treatment rules. cure serious wounds can heal a serious lp wound but cannot remove serious bleeding; that bleeding tier requires cure critical wounds.example: recovering through multiple wound bandsa character with maximum lp 15 and constitution modifier +2 begins at -1 lp under sustained competent care. after seven days they recover to 1 lp and wake. seven days later they reach 3 lp, and after another seven days they reach 5 lp and enter the serious band. their faster serious rate now applies: three days later they reach 7, and three days after that they reach 9 and enter light. the light rate then applies, restoring another 2 lp after one day of care.cure critical wounds is required while the character is at -1 through 3 lp. cure serious wounds or cure critical wounds can heal them at 5 through 7, and any cure tier can heal them after they reach the light band at 9 lp.
239combat · recovery and aftermath

pages.title: Physical Energy and Fatigue Recovery
pages.text:
combatrecovery and aftermath
physical energy and fatigue recoverya short rest restores a substantial amount of pe chosen for the circumstances. common table results are 1d6, 2d6, or full recovery; there is no universal short-rest pe formula. refresh and other abilities restore pe according to their own rules.a long rest restores all pe. the same eight hours of complete rest also removes the entire fatigue ladder, so the character does not need one period to clear the condition followed by another period to recover pe.pe cannot fall below 0. an action that spends the character's final pe finishes before its zero-pe consequence begins. the character then becomes exhausted, which sets and locks current pe at 0. while exhausted, the character cannot recover pe through a short rest, refresh, or another ordinary pe-restoration effect. exhausted must first end or become fatigued.once reduced to fatigued, the character may recover and spend pe normally. recovering pe does not itself remove fatigued, and refresh does not remove either fatigued or exhausted unless an explicit rule says otherwise.for fatigue-induced conditions, complete rest reduces the ladder as follows:current statecomplete restresultunconscious from a third fatigue application1 hourbecomes exhausted; pe remains locked at 0.exhausted1 hourbecomes fatigued; pe may now be recovered and spent.fatigued8 hoursfatigued ends.eight hours of complete rest remove any of these fatigue states directly and restore all pe. do not add the one-hour recovery steps to those eight hours.restoring hp or lp does not wake a character made unconscious by fatigue. another source of unconsciousness follows its own recovery rule.
240combat · recovery and aftermath

pages.title: Combat Conditions · General Condition Rules
pages.text:
combatcombat conditions
combat conditionsgeneral condition rulesthe effect applying a condition normally determines its duration and removal. when a condition is inherently persistent and no ordinary duration makes sense, it continues until something actually changes that state.if the applying effect gives no duration or removal procedure, use the condition's own rules.receiving the same condition again has no additional effect unless that condition or its source explicitly provides ranks, stacking, escalation, or another reapplication rule.fatigued and exhaustedfatigue escalates through three applications:a character who newly receives fatigue becomes fatigued.a fatigued character who receives fatigue becomes exhausted instead.an exhausted character who receives fatigue becomes unconscious.reaching 0 pe bypasses the first step and makes the character exhausted after the action spending the final pe finishes. an effect that directly applies exhausted invokes the complete exhausted condition below.fatigued. a fatigued character:cannot run or charge;takes -2 to attack rolls, defense rolls, saving throws, and skill checks; andmay recover and spend pe normally.refresh and ordinary pe recovery do not remove fatigued. eight hours of complete rest removes it unless the source applying fatigue states otherwise.exhausted. becoming exhausted sets current pe to 0 and locks it there. an exhausted character cannot recover pe through refresh, a short rest, or another ordinary pe-restoration effect. the condition must first end or become fatigued.each round, an exhausted character receives either movement or one main action, never both. movement is halved. a permitted main action may be one ordinary attack, one spell, or another action that costs no pe; it cannot be a full attack. defenses and reactions remain available when they require no pe.an exhausted character also:cannot run or charge; andtakes -6 to attack rolls, defense rolls, saving throws, skill checks, and ability checks.after one hour of complete rest, exhausted becomes fatigued. a third fatigue application instead causes unconsciousness, whose complete effects appear below. the recovery procedures for all three stages appear under physical energy and fatigue recovery.pronewhile prone, the selected attack method supplies one full-attack pass. an ability that places several attacks inside that pass still does so, but attack-speed increases do not add further passes unless an explicit rule says otherwise.
241combat · combat conditions

pages.title: Staggered and Dazed · Unconscious
pages.text:
combatcombat conditions
if the character becomes prone after already resolving an attack in the current round, every unresolved attack is lost. becoming prone therefore ends an ongoing full attack. a character who has not yet attacked may use the one remaining pass while prone, subject to the condition's other restrictions.a prone character:takes -2 to attack and defense against melee opponents;gains +4 dodge against ranged attacks; andcannot normally use a two-handed weapon effectively.a weapon, talent, or other explicit rule may create an exception to the two-handed restriction, such as allowing an appropriate spear to be braced against a charge.standing consumes the character's movement and requires no check. standing while threatened provokes an attack of opportunity. because standing does not consume the main action, the character may still use a main action afterward when no other rule prevents it.an explicit ability may remove or override prone immediately and preserve unresolved attack passes according to its own rules.staggered and dazedstaggered. each round, a staggered character chooses either movement or one main action that is not a full attack, never both. the permitted main action may be one ordinary attack, one spell, or another single action that does not produce a full attack. haste grants no additional action while the character is staggered.dazed. a dazed character receives no movement and no main action. dazed does not itself impose a numeric defense penalty; any further restriction comes from the effect applying it or another condition.unconsciousan unconscious character falls prone, drops everything held, and is helpless. the character receives no movement or main action, cannot speak or take another action, and cannot make active defenses.an unconscious character cannot spend pe, including the 5-pe response that can prevent a mortal wound.use this static defense:10 + applicable passive magical defensive modifiersdo not add bab, dexterity, weapon or shield bonuses, or another active-defense benefit. a deliberate attack that genuinely connects with the helpless body may deal lethal damage as described under damage and protection.stunned and paralyzedstunned. a stunned character drops everything held, receives no movement or main action, and cannot voluntarily leave their space. another creature or external force may still move the character.the character may parry, block, dodge, make otherwise eligible defensive reactions, and spend pe. remove the character's dexterity modifier from every defense roll. pe cannot suppress this loss of dexterity, although the character may use the ordinary 1-pe option to suppress one other eligible negative modifier on that roll.defensive movement cannot carry the stunned character out of their space. every successful hit against the character is a critical hit. resolve that critical through hp normally unless the attack independently qualifies as lethal damage.paralyzed. a paralyzed character cannot move, speak, take physical actions, or make active defenses. the character is helpless. a purely mental action remains possible only when its own rules require no speech, movement, somatic component, or other physical act.against an attack, use static defense:10 + applicable passive magical defensive modifiersdo not add bab, dexterity, weapon or shield bonuses, or another active-defense benefit.a winged creature that becomes paralyzed while flying falls. a swimming creature cannot swim and may drown according to the circumstances.a deliberate attack that genuinely connects with the helpless body may deal lethal damage and bypass hp. paralysis does not separately make every hit an automatic critical hit.shaken, frightened, and panickedfear has three cumulative stages: shaken, frightened, and panicked. an effect may apply a stated stage directly. further fear escalates an affected character as follows:shaken applied to a shaken character becomes frightened.
242combat · combat conditions

pages.title: Confused and Frenzied · Blinded and Deafened
pages.text:
combatcombat conditions
frightened applied to a shaken character becomes panicked.shaken or frightened applied to a frightened character becomes panicked.panicked is the highest general fear stage.fear penalties do not stack; use only the total penalty imposed by the character's current fear stage.shaken. a shaken character takes -2 to attack rolls, saving throws, skill checks, and ability checks. this includes fortitude saves. shaken does not itself impose a defense penalty.frightened. a frightened character takes -4 to attack rolls, saving throws, skill checks, and ability checks. this is the total frightened penalty, not an additional penalty stacked on shaken.each round, the character chooses either movement or one main action that is not a full attack, never both. defenses and otherwise eligible reactions remain available.if within the fear source's melee reach, the character must leave that reach if able and cannot voluntarily move closer to the source. the character cannot deliberately harm the fear source. they may ordinarily attack other enemies, heal, assist, defend, or take another supportive action. the dm may broaden this restriction when the nature or circumstances of the fear make other hostile action implausible.every spell a frightened character attempts has a flat 25% failure chance, including arcane, divine, offensive, defensive, and supportive spells. a spell lost to this failure still spends its full me cost.panicked. a panicked character takes a total -4 penalty to attack rolls, saving throws, skill checks, and ability checks. this replaces rather than stacks with the shaken penalty. the character drops everything held and uses their actions to flee the fear source at maximum speed. the character flees other immediate dangers rather than confronting them. if prevented from fleeing, the character cowers and cannot attack. ordinary movement hazards and attacks of opportunity still apply while fleeing.confused and frenziedconfused. at the beginning of each confused character's round, roll d100 once. that result controls the entire round; do not roll again for each action or attack pass.d100result for the round01–25act normally.26–50do nothing except babble incoherently.51–75deal 1d8 + strength modifier ordinary damage to oneself with the held item or an equivalent act of confused self-harm. route this damage normally through any applicable temporary hp, then hp and lp; it is not direct lp damage.76–100attack the nearest creature, friend or foe.a confused character cannot reliably distinguish allies from enemies. the d100 result controls the round. whenever that result permits or requires an attack against another creature, the character gives target priority to the creature that most recently attacked them, provided that creature is a legal target. a result requiring different behavior still takes precedence.while devoted to another confused result or target, the character does not make attacks of opportunity against unrelated creatures. confused does not itself impose a defense penalty.frenzied. a frenzied character remains under the player's control but must attack the nearest enemy to the best of the character's physical ability. if no physical weapon is available, the character uses unarmed attacks or attempts to grapple.allies are not enemies by default. if an ally seriously obstructs, attacks, shoves, or otherwise provokes the frenzied character, the dm may determine that the character now regards that ally as an enemy.frenzy may be entered voluntarily through an ability or imposed by a spell or another effect. the applying source controls its bonuses, duration, ending conditions, and any additional loss of agency.blinded and deafenedblinded. a blinded character's dodge is the static value:10 + babthe character may attack the area where they believe an enemy to be at -4, followed by a 50% miss chance. they may parry or block a melee opponent at -4.

pages.title: Power Scale and Domain Ranks · Rank Bands
pages.text:
combatpower scale and domain ranks
power scale and domain ranksdomain ranks describe the scale at which a specific attribute, attack, defense, spell, or ability operates. a rank belongs only to the value or power carrying it. it does not raise every statistic of the creature unless the creature's rules explicitly assign that rank more broadly.an ordinary statistic without an explicit domain rank operates at d rank.rank bandsrankscaledmortal or ordinary scale. normal statistics and ordinary d20 mathematics control.cexceptional, supernatural, or heroic scale. it dominates ordinary opposition but remains contestable by comparable specialists, preparation, tools, or circumstances.blegendary or monstrous scale. direct contests against lower ranks usually require exceptional leverage.agodlike scale. its power belongs to gods and comparable beings.aaworld-altering, avatar, true-ancestor, or conceptual scale. it can change battlefields, nations, natural laws, or metaphysical conditions.sspecial and incomparable. s sits outside the ordinary ladder; every s-ranked power defines what it can and cannot do.each ordinary step from d through aa represents roughly an order-of-magnitude increase in what that domain can accomplish. raw statistics still distinguish two opponents operating at the same rank.

pages.title: Applying Rank Gaps · Conditional and Special Ranks
pages.text:
combatpower scale and domain ranks
applying rank gapsidentify the rank governing the action and the rank governing its opposition. compare those ranks even when they come from different attributes or abilities. a strength-based attack opposed by a dexterity-based dodge therefore compares the attacker's strength rank with the defender's dexterity rank. combatants will normally favor their highest-ranked legal form of offense or defense.rank gapcombat resultsame rankapply no rank modifier. use ordinary statistics, level, skill, equipment, circumstances, and dice.higher by one rankthe higher-ranked side gains +10 in every independently resolved formula governed by that domain during the exchange. the lower-ranked side can still compete.higher by two ranksthe higher-ranked side gains +40 in every independently resolved formula governed by that domain during the exchange. a direct victory by the lower-ranked side normally requires leverage, a weakness, a relic, a counter-technique, or comparable preparation.higher by three or more ranksthere is no meaningful direct contest. the lower-ranked side needs a force multiplier or must change the nature of the contest.s involvedapply the s-ranked power's explicit rule instead of deriving a numeric result from rank distance.apply the rank modifier directly to the relevant formula; never add it to the underlying attribute score or use it to recalculate the ordinary ability modifier.a higher-ranked offense adds the rank modifier to its attack. if it hits, it also adds the same modifier directly to damage. these are separate applications: the attack bonus can increase margin of success, and the damage calculation still receives the direct rank bonus.a higher-ranked defense adds the rank modifier to its defense. the attack and defense modifiers are determined by the ranks actually governing those two sides of the exchange.the higher-ranked side in a roll-under check adds the modifier once to its threshold. the resulting check margin inherits that increase; do not add the rank modifier to the check margin again.any other independently resolved check, save, dc, or value receives the modifier when the ranked domain directly governs it. if that modified value is then used to calculate another result, do not apply the rank modifier again to the new result. do not add strength rank to initiative, will, spellcasting, or another unrelated domain.a lower-ranked combatant may still prevail by attacking a different domain, exploiting terrain or information, using allies or a suitable relic, invoking a specific counter, or otherwise avoiding the direct comparison.conditional and special ranksa + or - after a rank marks a conditional shift, not an ordinary numeric modifier. the ability must state the condition that causes the shift.b+ operates at b rank normally and becomes a rank when its stated condition is met.c++ operates at c rank normally and can rise two steps to a rank when its stated condition is met.a+ operates at a rank normally and becomes aa rank when its stated condition is met.b++ operates at b rank normally and can rise two steps to aa rank when its stated condition is met.c- operates at c rank normally and falls to d rank under its stated condition.if the condition is not active, use the printed letter without its signs. conditional shifts remain within d through aa and cannot enter s. s-ranked abilities always state their own operation, limits, and interactions.

pages.title: Example: Strength 18B Against C-Ranked Opposition
pages.text:
combatpower scale and domain ranks
example: strength 18b against c-ranked oppositiona dragon has strength 18b. its opponent has strength 24c. the opponent has the higher raw strength score, but the dragon's strength operates one rank higher.for a direct opposed strength check, the dragon receives the one-rank +10. in a pure roll-under contest, its adjusted threshold is 18 + 10 = 28, while the opponent's threshold remains 24. any bab, size, equipment, or situational modifiers required by the particular maneuver are then applied normally, and both sides compare check margins.if the dragon rolls 12, its check margin is 28 - 12 = 16. if the opponent rolls 10, their check margin is 24 - 10 = 14; the dragon wins by 2. the c-ranked opponent can still win with a sufficiently better roll because a one-rank gap remains contestable.for a weapon attack, compare the dragon's b-ranked strength offense with the rank governing the opponent's chosen defense. if the opponent dodges with c-ranked dexterity, the dragon adds +10 to its strength-based attack and, if the attack connects, adds +10 directly to damage. suppose the dragon's ordinary attack total is 22 and the opponent's defense is 20. rank raises the attack to 32, producing margin 12. the raw damage calculation then uses the weapon dice, the dragon's unchanged ordinary strength modifier, margin 12, and the direct +10 rank bonus. protection resolves normally afterward.the +10 attack contribution has already flowed into margin and is not added to margin again. the separate +10 damage contribution is nevertheless applied because strength governs the damage formula as well. if the opponent instead used a b-ranked defense, the ranks would be equal and neither rank modifier would apply.the notation never turns the dragon's strength score into 28, changes its attribute maximum, or produces a new strength modifier. strength remains 18 for every ordinary calculation; +10 is the independent effect of the one-rank gap. against d-ranked opposition, a b-ranked strength offense receives +40 in each independently resolved relevant formula instead.

  spells and spellcasting
  1. magic and spellcasting at a glancemagic is not what it was. in the first age, words of power could reshape reality and set cities ablaze. centuries of use, study, and rationalization have worn those workings into smaller, repeatable forms. the spell now called fireball is one surviving shadow. modern spells are teachable and dependable—magics sufficiently accepted by the world to function almost mundanely—and their reliability marks how much they have lost.a spellcaster learns individual spells, spends magical energy (me) to cast them, and uses caster level to determine their power. vanaheim has no daily preparation of spell slots: a learned spell remains known and can be cast whenever the character meets its requirements and can pay its cost.the core spellcasting jobs approach magic through different traditions:jobtradition and accesspriestdivine magic from a faith-modified priest list; casting requires high follower standing.shamanspirit magic from the shaman list; casting requires the spirit relationship that permits the job.paladindivine magic from the choosing god's paladin list; casting requires that god's continuing favor.helliondivine magic from the patron imperial faith's hellion list; casting requires high follower standing.sorcererinnate sorcery from the sorcerer list.warlockinnate or inherited elementalism from the warlock list.necromancerrestricted abyssal necromancy from the necromancer list, including preserved legacy spells where classes permits them.each character has one shared me pool even when several jobs grant spellcasting. bard performances are magical talents rather than spells and do not use this chapter's ordinary spellcasting procedure.ordinary necromancer spells use the same casting procedure as other spells, although their source and magical interactions are necromantic. true necromancy is the separate freeform practice owned by the necromancer profile in classes; it is not an ordinary spell-circle procedure and is not expanded here.the basic procedure is:confirm that the spell is known, currently castable, and within the character's spell-circle limit.confirm its target or area, components, me cost, and required free concentration.use the main action, pay me, and begin casting. resolve armor spell failure when applicable.complete the spell after its spell speed.resolve mr, protective spells, any saving throw, the spell's effect, and applicable protection in the order given under resolving a spell.combat supplies the detailed initiative, interruption, defensive casting, combat casting, and damage-routing procedures. individual spells state their own targets, ranges, areas, durations, components, saving throws, and exceptions.

success preserves the maintained spells and failure ends them. damage reduced to 0 requires no roll. the complete combat handling appears under combat — damage and maintained spells.touch deliveryan instantaneous touch spell must be delivered as part of its casting. a willing target normally requires no attack. against an unwilling target, use:1d20 + bab + dexterity modifier + 5this is a melee or ranged touch attack as the spell requires. dodge prevents delivery. parry or block normally creates enough contact for the touch effect to resolve unless the spell says that deflecting its hand, implement, or projectile defeats it.the touch attack supplies contact rather than weapon damage. the spell supplies its damage, saving throw, mr, condition, and other effects. if an instantaneous touch attack misses, the spell ends without effect.a touch effect remains charged only when its own entry grants a duration or charging procedure. such an entry may place the charge on a hand, another unarmed limb, or a weapon and states when it discharges. there is no general held-touch-charge rule.weapon-carried spell chargesa spellcaster may place a spell into a held melee weapon only when that spell's own entry explicitly permits weapon delivery. a successful weapon attack deals its ordinary weapon result and then delivers the spell. the spell entry states how long the charge lasts, whether a miss retains it, what causes discharge, which magical defenses apply, and when the charge ends. no other touch spell gains weapon delivery by inference.a melee weapon may carry no more than one weapon-carried spell charge at a time, regardless of the charge's source. a weapon that already carries a charge is not an eligible target for another until the first charge discharges or ends. a spell-specific entry may define its discharge and duration, but does not increase this limit unless it expressly says so.255spells and spellcasting · concentration and spell delivery
