pages.text: spells and spellcastingmagical devices8. magical devicesactivating a devicea character must possess the corresponding scrolls, wands, or staves talent to activate that device type.if the stored spell belongs to any of the user's actual class spell eligibilities, activation requires no check, even when the spell's circle is higher than the user can currently cast. secret or unprinted class eligibility counts. if the spell does not belong to the user's class eligibility, make an intelligence check. success activates the item; failure consumes the scroll or one charge and produces no spell effect.activation normally uses a main action. the stored spell resolves immediately without the user's ordinary spell speed, and the user spends no personal me. the device supplies its caster level, numerical effect, save dc, art adjustments, and other stored values. one scroll or one charge supplies the activation unless the item says otherwise.the stored spell retains its legal range and target requirements. a touch-range wand therefore still requires the appropriate touch attack. an individual item may define a different action, activation time, or other bounded exception.scrollsa scroll may hold a spell above the user's current casting circle. class eligibility, rather than current circle, determines whether activation is automatic.the scroll is consumed when activated. a failed off-list activation attempt also consumes it. its magical parchment disintegrates completely.wandsa wand applies its spell to one legal target. a self-only spell can affect only the user, a touch spell requires contact, and a ranged spell functions to its stored range. a wand does not turn its spell into an area effect.a wand remains intact while at least one charge remains. spending its final charge makes it crack and collapse harmlessly into unusable pieces.stavesunless its own entry says otherwise, one staff charge applies its spell to every eligible creature within 60 feet. a beneficial spell affects the wielder's recognized allies; a hostile spell affects every other eligible creature in range.a staff recognizes established companions. an unfamiliar friendly creature is safely included when willingly touching the wielder or one of those companions at activation. proximity alone gives no guaranteed protection, although the dm may accept clear circumstances. hostile contact does not fool the staff.a staff remains intact at zero charges. an individual staff may replace the ordinary range, targeting, or affected-creature rule. a staff containing an area spell must define its own placement and overlap behavior.recharging wands and stavesrecharge is a spell shared by several spellcasting classes. a caster can use a class's version of recharge only when the caster knows both recharge and the exact spell stored in the device through that class. device access, class eligibility without knowledge, and possession of a scroll do not replace either known spell.a spell may be available to recharge through several classes. a device may instead be impossible for any ordinary caster to recharge when no class can supply both required spells. the recharge spell entry owns the complete procedure, costs, time, and number of charges restored. an individual device may state an exception.259spells and spellcasting · magical devices

pages.title: 9. Metamagic · Metamagic Catalogue
pages.text: spells and spellcastingmetamagic9. metamagicmetamagic techniques modify ordinary spells personally cast through sorcerer, warlock, or necromancer. the shared mage progression in classes grants one metamagic selection at mage job level 10 and another at levels 14, 18, 22, 26, and 30.declare metamagic when casting begins. add its extra me cost to the spell's base me cost and pay the complete amount at once. if two metamagic abilities modify the same spell, add both costs. a failed or interrupted spell refunds none of that me.a spell can receive no more than two different metamagic abilities. the same ability cannot be applied twice. metamagic cannot modify a scroll, wand, staff, ritual spell, bard performance, talent, spell-like ability, or true necromancy unless an explicit rule says otherwise.metamagic cataloguepersistent spell — extra me 3. a spell maintained through concentration continues for 1d4 rounds after that maintenance ends, including voluntary release, lost concentration, unconsciousness, or the caster's death. the spell no longer occupies concentration during those rounds. dispel magic, successful magic resistance, or another effect that destroys or negates the spell ends or prevents it normally; persistence does not protect it. persistent spell does not make an instantaneous effect repeat.quicken spell — extra me 6. cast the spell as a free action with spell speed 0; it resolves immediately. only one quickened spell may be cast per round. its ordinary components, me, targeting, spell failure, and other requirements still apply. a quickened spell cannot be countered through ordinary counterspelling.empower spell — extra me 3 per +1 dc. increase the spell's save dc by +1 to +5, chosen when casting begins. the maximum +5 increase costs 15 extra me.silent spell — extra me 2. ignore the spell's verbal component. other components remain unchanged.still spell — extra me 2. ignore the spell's somatic component. because the modified spell has no somatic component, worn armor does not make its ordinary somatic spell failure roll. other components remain unchanged.shape spell — extra me 2. sculpt safe spaces inside the spell's existing area, allowing chosen creatures or portions of the area to remain unaffected. shape spell does not increase the spell's range, total area, damage, or number of targets and cannot modify a spell that has no area to shape.penetrating spell — extra me 4. halve the magic protection applied against this spell and round down.high density spell — extra me 4. reduce each target's magic resistance against this casting by caster level + 10 percentage points, to a minimum of 0%.manaburn spell — extra me 4. apply only to a spell with one target. in addition to the spell's ordinary resolution, the target makes a separate will save against the spell's normal dc. failure removes me equal to the underlying spell's base me cost; success removes half that amount, rounded down. manaburn cannot reduce me below 0. its drain excludes every metamagic surcharge.manawall spell — extra me 1–10. choose the extra me when casting begins. until that spell completes or fails, manawall absorbs up to twice the chosen amount in damage that would otherwise reach the caster. the selected me is spent even if no damage arrives. damage fully absorbed by manawall does not interrupt the spell.repeating spell — extra me equal to 2 + the spell's base me cost. after the original spell completes successfully, it resolves again at the same initiative on the following round without another action or me payment. use the original target or area, but make new attacks, saves, damage rolls, and other variable rolls. if the first casting is interrupted or fails, nothing repeats. the repetition cannot affect a target that no longer exists or is otherwise no longer eligible for that spell.extend spell — extra me 3. increase the spell's range by 60 feet and double its stated duration. extend spell cannot modify a touch-range spell. it does not create a fixed duration for an instantaneous spell or for a spell that lasts only while concentration is maintained.260spells and spellcasting · metamagic

pages.title: 10. Ritual Spells
pages.text: spells and spellcastingritual spells10. ritual spellsritual spells are large or specialized acts of magic that operate outside ordinary spellcasting. they commonly use magic circles, extended preparation, special materials or locations, multiple participants, stored or environmental power, or other requirements defined by the ritual. rituals can establish magical workshops, link prepared teleportation sites, create magical fortifications, or accomplish other workings whose scale or structure does not fit an ordinary spell. these are examples of what rituals may accomplish, not general abilities granted by ritual spell eligibility.every mage job makes the character eligible to learn ritual spells, but grants no ritual automatically. a mage can learn or perform only a ritual whose circle does not exceed the highest spell circle that mage can currently cast through the qualifying mage job. an individual ritual may explicitly permit priests or other non-mage participants; that exception grants access only to that ritual. a ritual may be performed by one caster or may require or benefit from several participants; the individual ritual decides.spiritual wrath is an example intended for priests and paladins. it is not an ordinary spell. this entry grants no ability to perform it; its complete requirements and procedure must first be supplied by the dm.the dm determines which rituals exist, where they can be discovered, and whether a character can learn one. every ritual supplies its own casting time, participants, me or other power source, materials, site, magic-circle requirements, checks, risks, interruption rules, and result. ritual spell eligibility grants no default procedure for improvising a ritual. metamagic and clarity do not modify ritual spells unless an explicit rule says otherwise.two known priestly examples are land of stability, which can protect prepared territory from natural disasters, and the great circle, a cooperative working used to cleanse and consecrate ground for a temple or sanctuary. these descriptions grant no access or casting procedure. a character needs the ritual's complete requirements and procedure from the dm.261spells and spellcasting · ritual spells

pages.title: 11. Reading a Spell Entry · Job Abbreviations
pages.text: spells and spellcastingreading a spell entry11. reading a spell entryread each spell from top to bottom: its header, an effect section that first explains the magic and then gives its rules, and any longer description that follows. the opening tells you what the spell does in the world before you resolve its mechanics. all required rules remain together in the effect section.job abbreviationscompact rules blocks may abbreviate jobs as follows:pri priest · sha shaman · pal paladin · hel hellion · sor sorcerer · war warlock · nec necromancerthese abbreviations identify jobs in spell entries and compact rules blocks.standard headereach ordinary spell uses the following header fields. values such as none, no, self, and instantaneous state an explicit answer.class/circle: the job-and-circle pairs for the spell, with a separate pair for each job: sor 3 · pri 3 · nec 3.school: the spell's magical school.me: the magical energy paid to cast it.spell speed: its initiative delay or longer casting time.components: its required v, s, and m components, or none.range: how far from the caster the spell can reach.target or area: the creature, object, or area the spell affects. an entry may specify both a target and an area.duration: how long the effect remains.concentration: its initial/maintenance requirement.save: the saving throw and result, such as will negates, reflex half, or none.magic resistance: yes when ordinary magic resistance applies and no when it does not.a specific, priced, unusual, or consumed material component receives a material line directly beneath the header. mechanically meaningful descriptors or unusual delivery restrictions may likewise appear there when useful.brewable identifies a spell that may be made into a potion. cannot be scribed marks an exception to the ordinary scroll rule.mechanical effectthe effect section explains what the spell does and gives its complete rules: the exact roll or dc, damage or healing, damage type, penetration, scaling, saving-throw result, and any operational exception. the rules needed to resolve the spell are together in this section; the longer description adds atmosphere and lore.262spells and spellcasting · reading a spell entry

pages.title: Description
pages.text: spells and spellcastingreading a spell entrydescriptionan optional description expands on the spell's appearance, sensation, history, customary interpretation, old accounts, material symbolism, or uncertain and cryptic observations. it adds atmosphere and lore alongside the complete rules in effect.descriptive uncertainty does not secretly alter the reliable game procedure above it. it may imply that scholars understand only part of the working, that older forms were greater, or that unusual magic exists beyond the catalogue, but any additional mechanical effect requires an explicit rule.263spells and spellcasting · reading a spell entry
